title: Stat/group pipeline ignores implicit grouping and per-group aggregation
description:
Confirmed via direct repro against compile(): our stat pipeline and line/path/area/ribbon group-splitting only ever look at an EXPLICIT mapping.group column. ggplot2's real rule is that group defaults to the interaction of every discrete aesthetic mapped on the layer (color/fill/shape/linetype), not just group=. This breaks three extremely common ggplot2 idioms silently (no warning, wrong-looking chart):

1. geom_line(aes(x=x, y=y, color=g)) with no explicit group= draws ONE zigzagging line across all groups interleaved by x, instead of one clean line per color group. Repro: ggplot({x:[0,1,2,0,1,2], y:[1,2,3,10,20,30], g:['a','a','a','b','b','b']}, {x:'x',y:'y',color:'g'}).add(geomLine()) -> compile() produces a single Line node with positions [[0,1],[0,10],[1,2],[1,20],[2,3],[2,30]] (interleaved/zigzag) instead of two Line nodes.

2. geom_bar()/geom_histogram() with fill mapped to a sub-category (e.g. ggplot(mpg, aes(class, fill=drv)) + geom_bar()) doesn't stack by fill at all -- stat_count (stat/mod.ts) counts by x only and returns a brand-new data object containing ONLY [xCol] and 'count', silently dropping the fill/color/group column entirely. Downstream lowerBarLayer (compile/mod.ts) then can't find the dropped column so falls back to a single solid-fill bar per x showing the total count. Repro confirmed: geomBar() with {x:'cls', fill:'drv'} on 5 rows (a:2x'f'+1x'4', b:2x'4') renders two solid #2a78d6 Polygon segments with no stacking and no legend, instead of stacked color segments.

3. geom_smooth(aes(color=g)) fits ONE trend line pooling all groups' data together (statSmooth in stat/mod.ts has zero group-awareness), instead of one fitted line per group. Repro confirmed: 2 groups with opposite slopes (flat vs steep) produce a single blended Line node, not 2.

Root cause is shared: applyStat and splitByGroup both only consult mapping.group, and stat functions (statCount/statBin/statSummary) discard every column except the ones they explicitly re-emit, so even a downstream per-group split has nothing left to split on. Needs (a) a shared 'effective group key' resolver used everywhere group-splitting happens (aes group ?? interaction of mapped discrete color/fill/shape/linetype), and (b) stat_count/stat_bin/stat_summary/stat_smooth reworked to aggregate/fit PER effective-group instead of over the whole layer, preserving the group-defining column(s) in their output data.
acceptance_criteria: geom_line/path/area/ribbon with only color or fill mapped (no explicit group=) render one connected shape per distinct color/fill level, matching ggplot2. geom_bar()/geom_histogram() with fill mapped to a discrete sub-category stack/dodge counts correctly per (x, fill) combination and emit a fill legend. geom_smooth()/stat_summary() fit/aggregate independently per effective group when color/fill/group is mapped. New pipeline_test.ts cases cover all three scenarios above (they should currently fail before the fix).
close_reason: Implemented shared effective-group resolver and grouped stat/render fixes for line/path/area/ribbon, stat_count/stat_bin, stat_summary, and geom_smooth/stat_smooth with regression coverage.

title: Define gggplot geom extensions for model inspection
description: Map the model IR to extension geoms/products, likely geom_layer/geom_model_graph, geom_tensor, geom_embedding, geom_activation, and geom_attention. Decide which are ordinary chart geoms versus specialized scene views, and register Live/emitted adapters without putting framework-specific loaders in core. Acceptance: extension definitions, capability metadata, example specs, and an integration test through the registry.
notes: Use ordinary gggplot extensions for tabular products such as parameter inventories and embeddings; keep specialized graph/matrix/attention components package-owned through explicit Live/emitted adapters.

title: Build useGPU model views for graph and tensor data
description: Implement runtime components for a layer graph (nodes/edges), tensor shape/size views, matrix/heatmap inspection, and optional embedding/activation point clouds. Keep large arrays resident or summarized rather than duplicating them on the CPU; expose selection/hover hooks as host callbacks. Acceptance: deterministic RenderTree or component fixtures plus a small interactive demo.
notes: Views may consume runtime-shared GPU tensors only through a validated adapter. Default to useGPU-owned buffers so the visualization layer controls post-loading storage, cache identity, and eviction.

title: Add an explicit PyTorch export/conversion bridge
description: Investigate a Python-side bridge for state_dict or TorchScript/ExportedProgram inputs that emits the model-inspection IR or SafeTensors/ONNX. Do not unpickle arbitrary .pt files in the browser. Acceptance: a documented CLI/API, one tiny PyTorch fixture, clear trust warning, and a format decision for what the first bridge accepts.
notes: PyTorch conversion remains a trusted bridge, but it is no longer the only route. Prefer a JS-native ONNX/Transformers.js path for the first browser vertical slice; retain explicit warnings for pickle/PT2 inputs.

title: Implement SafeTensors and ONNX metadata loaders
description: Build browser/Node-compatible loaders that can inspect headers and tensor metadata without eagerly copying all tensor payloads. Support lazy tensor slices or bounded summaries where practical, and document limitations for dynamic graphs. Acceptance: fixtures, dtype/shape parity tests, truncation and malformed-file errors, and memory-bound tests.
notes: Implemented (2026-08-02): browser/Node-safe direct SafeTensors and ONNX metadata loaders in @gggplot/model-inspect. inspectSafeTensors validates bounded JSON headers, dtype/shape/contiguous payload ranges, and returns a lazy range-validated TensorSource. inspectOnnx parses the main ONNX graph directly without runtime execution or payload copies: nodes, node I/O, inputs/outputs/value metadata, initializers, opsets, raw_data byte ranges, and external-data metadata. It creates a canonical ModelDocument with parameter/input/output/intermediate descriptors and direct graph edges; typed repeated-field payloads remain metadata-only. Untrusted limits cover model/header/string/node/tensor sizes. Dynamic subgraphs are reported but not expanded, documented in packages/model-inspect/README.md. Tests cover dtype/shape parity, selected range reads, malformed/truncated/oversized data, and SafeTensors overlap rejection. Verified direct parsing against bundled mnist-12.onnx (26,143 bytes; 22 nodes, 21 edges, 21 tensors) and full suite/check pass.
close_reason: Implemented bounded SafeTensors and direct ONNX metadata loaders with lazy range sources, tests, docs, and MNIST validation.

title: Define a model graph and tensor inspection IR
description: Create a serializable intermediate representation for model metadata: model, layers/nodes, edges, parameters, tensor shapes, dtypes, devices, parameter counts, optional summaries, and provenance. Include shape validation and stable IDs, with no GPU handles or framework objects in serialized data. Acceptance: TypeScript types, validators, JSON fixtures, and tests for malformed/partially loaded models.
notes: IR must include payload/source references, logical dtype/shape/strides, tensor roles, and residency policy without embedding GPU handles. The GPU-resident design is specified in docs/MODEL_INSPECTION_PLAN.md.
close_reason: Implemented packages/model-inspect with serializable model graph/tensor/runtime IR, logical and physical storage metadata, residency specs, validators, fixtures, and root workspace quality-gate integration.

title: Create a standalone GPU model-inspection package
description: Explore a separate package for loading model metadata/tensors and visualizing neural-network structure through useGPU, integrating with gggplot via explicit extension contracts. The package must separate safe portable model formats from optional conversion bridges, avoid executing untrusted Python/pickle artifacts in the browser, and expose serializable inspection products that can be rendered as graph, tensor, embedding, activation, and attention views.
notes: Detailed branch scope is documented in docs/MODEL_INSPECTION_PLAN.md. Recommended package boundary: @gggplot/model-inspect with artifact adapters -> canonical model document -> inspection products -> useGPU views -> optional gggplot extension adapters.

title: Add 3D interaction and visual QA coverage
description: Define and test orbit camera behavior for the new 3D marks, including transparent versus opaque depth ordering, clipping, axis/grid readability, and screenshots or deterministic render-tree fixtures. Acceptance: node-budget and render-tree tests cover each supported topology and the docs gallery has at least one example beyond points and lines.

title: Design the 3D bin product and choose geom_bin versus geom_voxel
description: Specify the dense hypercube/tensor product for 3D binning: axes, bin edges, group dimensions, empty-bin retention, count/weight/density fields, sparse rendering policy, and domain/scale behavior. Compare API names and recommend geom_bin_3d, geom_voxel, or another stable public name. Acceptance: serializable product schema, CPU reference reducer plan, renderer topology sketch, and explicit decision on whether a 2D geom_bin alias is appropriate.

title: Design and implement geom_surface or geom_mesh for height fields
description: Evaluate a named surface primitive for gridded x/y/z data, including regular-grid and sparse/missing-cell rules, triangle winding, color/height mapping, and camera/depth behavior. Implement only after the contract is accepted; keep irregular meshes or arbitrary scene graphs out of this issue. Acceptance: a small height-field fixture compiles to a documented mesh topology and both backends agree.

title: Add planar 3D surface modes for polygon area ribbon rect and tile
description: Add z-aware planar surface realizations for polygon/area/ribbon/rect/tile without inventing volume. Define whether z is a mapped constant-per-group plane or per-vertex coordinate, preserve existing stat outputs and topology, and validate winding/occlusion. Acceptance: representative grouped polygon and band fixtures render in Live and emitted output with conformance tests.

title: Expand unified 3D geom coverage
description: Plan and implement additional 3D geom modes in the unified core grammar. Preserve the existing rule that mapped z selects a declared mode, require explicit topology and occlusion semantics, and keep unsupported combinations failing clearly rather than silently falling back. Start with low-risk z extensions, then add planar surfaces, prisms, and voxel/bin products only after their data contracts are specified.

title: Decide the unified home for the 3D guide-configuration surface (GuideSpec3D, sizeMode, tickCount)
description:
Decide where the 3D-only guide-configuration surface lands in the unified GGSpec, BEFORE .4 removes Guides3D and BEFORE .7 has to reproduce the existing site examples.

WHAT IS UNHOMED TODAY. Point3DSpec carries two user-facing surfaces that the unification plan does not place:
  - guides: GuideSpec3D = { axes?: boolean; grid?: boolean; titles?: boolean; tickCount?: number }
  - params.sizeMode: "constant" | "perspective" (gggplot-4q2.8.3 Q15)

THREE OF THE FOUR GUIDE FIELDS HAVE 2D HOMES. theme.grid and theme.axes already exist and already mean "omit grid lines" / "omit axis rules" in the 2D compiler (compile/mod.ts reads both). 'titles' is close to the existing axisGuideOverlay 'titles' option. Decide whether the 3D spec keys collapse onto the theme keys outright or whether a guides part is introduced for both dimensions.

tickCount IS THE REAL PROBLEM: THERE IS NO 2D COUNTERPART. 2D derives its tick count from panel width inside guideLayout (tickCount = clamp(floor(width / 90), 2, 8)). A perspective-projected cube has no panel width and no stable margin, which is exactly why the 3D guides took a fixed count (DEFAULT_TICK_COUNT = 5, overridable). Options to weigh: (a) a theme key that overrides the width-derived count in both dimensions; (b) fold it into the scale as a breaks/n-breaks declaration, which is the ggplot2-shaped answer and generalizes to explicit breaks; (c) drop the knob and derive a 3D count from something intrinsic. Recommendation to evaluate first: (b), because it is the only option that also answers "how do I set explicit breaks", and because it composes with gggplot-42n.

INTERACTION WITH gggplot-42n. If breaks become pretty/extended rather than raw linspace, tickCount stops being an exact count and becomes a hint. Decide this surface and 42n together or the answer will be relitigated.

sizeMode maps cleanly onto Layer.params (it is already a per-layer param), but it is meaningful ONLY in a geom's 3D mode, so it becomes another combination the .1 resolver must validate rather than silently ignore.

WHY THIS BLOCKS .7. Its acceptance criterion is that the four existing 3D site examples retain their appearance. Swizzled3D is built on guides: { grid: false, tickCount: 3 }; without a decision here that example cannot be expressed in the unified spec at all.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision names the unified home for every field of GuideSpec3D and for params.sizeMode, with the tickCount question resolved explicitly (theme key, scale breaks declaration, or removal) and its interaction with gggplot-42n stated. The four existing 3D site examples are shown to be expressible in the unified spec, Swizzled3D included. sizeMode is listed among the mode-specific combinations the .1 resolver validates. No 3D guide field is silently dropped during the migration.
notes: DECISION 2026-07-31: no unified GuideSpec3D. grid -> theme.grid; axes -> theme.axes; titles -> new shared theme.axisTitles; tickCount -> ordinary Scale.nBreaks hint, with Scale.breaks for exact values and precedence breaks > nBreaks > layout/default hint. gggplot-42n owns pretty break generation but does not block RenderTree unification. sizeMode remains Layer.params and is validated by the selected geom mode. Updated docs §10.6 and dependent bead ownership.
close_reason: Unified guide configuration decided and documented: shared theme switches, Scale.breaks/nBreaks, mode-validated sizeMode; dependent bead ownership and graph updated.

title: Add shared 3D modes for geomLine and geomPath
description: Extend the same public geomLine/geomPath builders and registry definitions with 3D modes selected by a mapped z. Reuse effective grouping, ordering, color, alpha, linetype, and linewidth behavior where renderer traits support it; pack chunked vec4 polylines and retain GPU camera projection. Document or reject traits that do not have a valid 3D realization rather than silently diverging.
acceptance_criteria: geomLine/geomPath with x/y compile exactly as before; adding z uses the 3D mode with one fluent/spec/compiler/render/emitter path. Multi-group lines do not connect across groups. Sorting differs correctly between line and path. Unsupported stats, positions, or visual traits fail explicitly. Live and emitted 3D polylines have parity. The live-GPU gate stays green: deno task test:draw-calls shows #three-d drawing in the expected range (today 4 surfaces, 238 draws, 2731 instances) and #start unchanged. This is required because unit tests and route-health checks both stay green while a layer draws nothing (the gggplot-4q2.9 failure mode).
notes: geomLine/geomPath now declare 2D+3D modes; z selects identity-only 3D. Shared lowerLine preserves line x-sort vs path input order, effective grouping, dash/color/linewidth/alpha, and packs vec4 ChunkedLine tensors with depth/transparency. Emitted 3D line module type-checks. Docs helix exercises live grouped geomPath. Full suite 419 passed; GPU gate passes at surfaces=4 draws=281 instances=3883 pipelines=60 passes=188.
close_reason: Closed

title: Migrate the docs site and retire Point3DSpec/parallel 3D entry points
description: Rewrite all 3D site examples as ggplot(data, aes(...)).add(geomPoint(), camera3d(...)).build(), route them through compile/GGPlot/emitSource, and update API/reference documentation. Provide a short migration note for Point3DSpec, compile3d, GGPlot3D, and emitPoint3dSource. Remove the parallel geom_3d spec/registry/render/emitter modules or retain only time-bounded deprecated adapters that lower immediately into GGSpec.
acceptance_criteria: No docs or app path constructs Point3DSpec or asks users to choose a 3D compiler/renderer/emitter. Four existing visual examples retain their appearance and interaction under the shared API. Public exports and migration notes clearly identify removals/deprecations. Search confirms no accidental parallel serialization remains.
notes: All four site examples now build ordinary GGSpec with ggplot+geomPoint/geomPath and use compile/GGPlot/emitSource. Removed core geom_3d directory, package subpath exports, site aliases, Point3DSpec/Render3DNode/Guides3D, compile3d, GGPlot3D/Overlay, and emitPoint3dSource. Shared vec4 packing moved beside vec2 packing. Added docs/MIGRATING_3D_API.md. ggsave now detects 3D and lets Scene3D own passes; static export disables OrbitControls and normalizes vec4 companions. Checks pass, 384 tests pass, both GPU routes pass, and visual+PNG gate passes all 16 routes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Extend emitSource to unified 3D RenderTrees and canonical camera parameters
description: Make emitSource handle the new named 3D camera/view wrapper, Tick, 4-axis Cartesian range, vec4 marks, in-scene guides, and flat overlay. The source GGSpec remains parameter-serialized; emitted standalone rendering may derive or inline the view-projection matrix from the same canonical camera. Delete emitPoint3dSource after parity and standalone type-check tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: emitSource(compile(spec)) is the only emitter call for 2D and 3D. Emitted 3D source type-checks standalone and matches the live path for positions, camera, ranges, guides, point appearance, depth/transparency, and overlay. No accepted camera option is dropped. Existing 2D emission snapshots remain stable unless an intentional shared wrapper change is documented.
notes: emitSource now handles Scene3D, Tick, 4-axis ranges, vec4 Point tensors via Point3D adapter, canonical camera serialization, in-scene guides, and sibling flat overlay. Generated wrapper mirrors live OrbitControls/OrbitCamera + two Passes and preserves bearing/pitch/radius/target/fov/near/far. Standalone generated 3D module deno-checks; full suite 416 passed; site check passes. Plot namespace alias changed to PlotComponents to permit an actual <Plot> node.
close_reason: Closed

title: Unify live 2D/3D rendering behind GGPlot with one plot-wide camera
description: Teach the ordinary GGPlot/renderTree host to realize the 3D camera/view RenderNodes: seed OrbitControls from GGSpec camera, keep live camera changes as runtime-only state, mount the 3D Cartesian scene, and draw legends/titles in the existing flat overlay pass. Keep FlatCamera/Embedded behavior unchanged for 2D. Remove the apps/site-only GGPlot3D/GGPlot3DOverlay orchestration once the shared host covers it.
acceptance_criteria: GGPlot renders either dimension from GGSpec with no caller-selected mode and no separate 3D component. Omitted camera uses the standard default; explicit camera seeds controls; interactive changes do not mutate GGSpec. Exactly one camera governs the whole 3D plot. Existing 2D live tests and instrumentation remain green, and a visual 3D smoke test verifies projection, guides, depth, and overlay. The live-GPU gate stays green: deno task test:draw-calls shows #three-d drawing in the expected range (today 4 surfaces, 238 draws, 2731 instances) and #start unchanged. This is required because unit tests and route-health checks both stay green while a layer draws nothing (the gggplot-4q2.9 failure mode).
notes: GGPlot/renderTree now owns Scene3D: one OrbitControls/OrbitCamera seeded from canonical GGSpec.camera, one scene pass, and one sibling flat overlay pass. Docs site Scene3D accepts ordinary GGSpec and delegates entirely to GGPlot; no caller-selected compiler/renderer remains. Site check/build pass. Unified route draw gate passes at surfaces=4 draws=282 instances=3727 pipelines=58 passes=186 (new ordinary guide/overlay tree increases draws from the legacy baseline).
close_reason: Closed

title: Lower shared geomPoint 2D/3D modes through one compile path and RenderTree
description: Move point_3d lowering behind the ordinary point GeomDefinition 3D mode so geomPoint plus z uses compile(GGSpec). Reuse common color/size/alpha scale and flat packing paths, producing vec2 for 2D and vec4 [x,y,z,1] for 3D. Represent the 3D Cartesian range, axes, point mark, grids, axes, ticks, labels, and flat overlay as ordinary RenderNodes; add Tick and the minimal named camera/view wrapper component to ComponentName. Eliminate Guides3D and Render3DNode as parallel compiler products once parity tests pass.
design:
CONSTRAINT ON THE NAMED CAMERA/VIEW WRAPPER COMPONENT (added by plan review, 2026-07-31). This is the highest-novelty piece of the epic and needs an explicit node shape decided BEFORE coding.

The wrapper must do three things: seed OrbitControls from GGSpec.camera, mount the Cartesian scene, and compose the flat legend/title overlay. The third cannot be a child of the first two. Verified while building gggplot-4q2.11: OrbitCamera provides ViewProvider but NOT LayoutContext, and Embedded needs a layout to bridge pixel space into the normalized [-1,1] coordinates the 2D guide builders emit. The overlay therefore has to be a SIBLING pass — <FlatCamera><Pass overlay>...</Pass></FlatCamera> — placed after the 3D pass, where Pass's 'overlay' flag sets the color attachment loadOp to 'load' so it composites instead of clearing (see @use-gpu/workbench pass/util). Depth is cleared, so the overlay always draws on top.

So one RenderNode has to expand into two passes, two cameras, and two DISTINCT child subtrees, while renderTree today maps one node to one component with a single flat children list. Decide the encoding explicitly: separate scene-children and overlay-children on the wrapper node, two sibling nodes under a thin parent, or a registry component that partitions its children by a marker. Whichever is chosen must keep renderTree's recursive contract intact for 2D.

The current 32h estimate for this bead includes the wrapper. The review flagged that as light but deliberately did not change the number; once the node shape is drafted, consider splitting the wrapper into its own bead and re-estimating.
acceptance_criteria: Equivalent Point3DSpec and unified GGSpec inputs produce the same trained domains, packed positions, colors, sizes, camera initialization, guides, and overlay. compile() returns RenderNode for both dimensions. geomPoint is the only public point builder needed. Identity stat/position are supported in 3D; other combinations reject via the resolver. No CPU point projection is introduced. The live-GPU gate stays green: deno task test:draw-calls shows #three-d drawing in the expected range (today 4 surfaces, 238 draws, 2731 instances) and #start unchanged. This is required because unit tests and route-health checks both stay green while a layer draws nothing (the gggplot-4q2.9 failure mode).
notes: Unified compile(GGSpec) now lowers ordinary geomPoint+x/y/z via the shared registry/scales into a vec4 Point RenderNode. Added Scene3D two-branch RenderTree (Plot/Cartesian in orbit pass + Embedded flat overlay), ordinary Grid/Axis/Tick/Label guide nodes, shared color/size/alpha packing, coord axes override, canonical camera defaults, and theme axes/axisTitles switches. 2D remains unchanged. Full suite 415 passed; three-d draw gate exactly surfaces=4 draws=238 instances=2731.
close_reason: Closed

title: Generalize position scales, coord swizzles, and layer context from x/y to x/y/z
description: Complete the compiler type widening required after gggplot-5tg: train z with the same Scale declaration/training/mapping primitives as x/y; add scaleZContinuous/Discrete/Log10/Sqrt; replace xDomain/yDomain-only context and domain contribution assumptions with axis-keyed forms where appropriate; preserve x/y convenience APIs. Use the same validated use.gpu axes swizzle representation for 2D and 3D, always pinning homogeneous w internally. Keep existing 2D coordCartesian/coordFlip/coordPolar behavior byte-compatible.
acceptance_criteria: One position-scale trainer handles x/y/z and declared limits, transforms, expansion, and discrete levels consistently. LayerContext and compiler domain plumbing can carry z without parallel PositionScale3D types. scaleZ builders and z labels/guides use ordinary Scale/PlotLabels. Existing 2D tests remain unchanged; new parity tests compare x/y/z training. Homogeneous w is never grammar-visible.
notes: Unified trainPositionScale handles x/y/z with continuous/discrete, declared limits, transforms, expansion, breaks, and nBreaks validation. Added all four scaleZ builders and PlotLabels.z. LayerContext/DomainContributionCtx now carry axis-keyed scales/domains while retaining x/y conveniences. Shared resolveAxes3d pins w; legacy geom_3d delegates to it. Full deno task test: 413 passed.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add canonical singleton camera3d to GGSpec and the fluent DSL
description: Add one optional top-level GGSpec.camera and a SpecPart camera tag with camera3d(options?) builder semantics matching singleton coord/facet replacement. The canonical JSON is a fully resolved orbit pose plus explicit perspective projection: kind and projection discriminators, bearing, pitch, radius, target, fov, near, and far. camera3d() serializes the documented standard three-quarter default; partial options merge with that default at build time. Runtime OrbitControls state and derived matrices never enter GGSpec. Remove the misleading unified input that accepts orthographic/up/aspect/orthographicHeight and silently loses those fields; retain lookAt only as an explicit migration helper that immediately produces canonical orbit JSON, if compatibility requires it.
acceptance_criteria: GGSpec structurally permits zero or one camera. camera3d(), partial overrides, repeated replacement, JSON round-trip, invalid frustum/radius, and lookAt migration behavior are tested. The default is documented and emitted as explicit plain data when camera3d() is called. Orthographic input is rejected until a projection implementation exists; no accepted camera field is silently discarded. The documented default is pinned to the existing DEFAULT_CAMERA_3D constant (geom_3d/types.ts) by reference or by test, so the decision doc's inline copy of bearing pi/4 / pitch 0.45 / radius 3.6 / fov pi/4 / near 0.1 / far 100 cannot drift from the code.
notes: Implemented canonical root Camera3D JSON in ir/camera.ts, GGSpec.camera, camera3d() singleton DSL replacement, explicit camera3dFromLookAt migration sugar, runtime rejection of orthographic/unknown fields, full validation, cloned targets, and one source of truth for defaults shared with the legacy geom_3d constant. Added camera_dsl_test.ts. Validation: deno task check:core; focused camera + legacy geom_3d tests (40 passed); full deno test -A (407 passed).
close_reason: Canonical singleton camera3d GGSpec/DSL component implemented with defaults, overrides, validation, look-at migration, JSON tests, and full-suite coverage.

title: Define dimensional geom modes and a plot-level dimension resolver
description: Replace the fixed dims idea with registry-declared dimensional modes. A shared geom may expose both 2D and 3D modes with mode-specific required position aesthetics, lowerer, supported stats, and supported positions; an intrinsically 3D geom exposes only 3D. Resolve each layer from its effective mapping after inheritAes merge, then require one plot dimension. A mapped z selects 3D only when that geom declares z as a position axis; geomTile/statSummary2d must keep using z as a 2D value aesthetic. Default empty plots to 2D. Reject mixed 2D/3D layers, missing required axes, unsupported 3D stats/positions, and 3D facets with actionable errors.
design: Mode metadata also declares supported mode-specific params. Initial 3D point mode accepts sizeMode constant or perspective; the 2D point mode and other modes reject sizeMode. Plot resolution rejects a top-level camera when all drawable layers resolve to 2D.
acceptance_criteria: Registry metadata represents 2D-only, 3D-only, and shared geoms without duplicate public geom kinds. Tests cover inherited and layer mappings, shared geomPoint with and without z, tile z remaining 2D, intrinsic 3D selection, empty plots, and all rejection paths. The resolver runs before scale/stat/lowering branches and returns a single typed plot dimension. Camera-on-2D fails clearly. Mode-specific params are validated, including sizeMode accepted only by the 3D point mode with constant or perspective values.
notes: Implemented GeomMode/PlotDimension registry metadata, effective-mapping resolution, shared point 2D/3D modes, z-as-value preservation for 2D-only geoms, intrinsic 3D support, mixed-mode/camera/facet/coord validation, identity-position requirements, stat/position gates, and mode-specific sizeMode validation. geomBlank is dimension-neutral. compile now guards against silent 3D-to-2D fallthrough until .4 lands. Added dimension_resolver_test.ts. Non-identity stats may synthesize required positions, preserving QQ. Validation: check:core; focused dimension + pipeline 187 passed; full deno test -A 414 passed.
close_reason: Dimensional geom modes and pre-compile plot resolver implemented with shared-point inference, z-value preservation, validation, and full regression coverage.

title: Epic: unify the 2D/3D grammar, spec, compiler, and renderer
description: Implement the decision from gggplot-8y2: one GGSpec and fluent grammar, shared geom builders whose dimensional mode is selected from geom capability plus effective mappings, and one serialized singleton camera3d component. Preserve specialized internal lowering only where it remains useful; remove Point3DSpec and the parallel compile/render/emit entry points after migration.
acceptance_criteria: A 2D and 3D point plot use the same GGSpec, geomPoint builder, compile entry point, RenderNode contract, live renderer, and emitter. GGSpec has at most one canonical serialized camera. Existing 2D z-as-value uses remain 2D. Unsupported mixed dimensions, 3D stats/positions, camera-on-2D, and 3D faceting fail clearly. Point3DSpec and parallel entry points are retired or temporary deprecated shims with a documented migration.
notes: Implemented complete unified 2D/3D API: dimensional geom modes/resolver; singleton canonical camera3d; shared x/y/z scales and swizzles; geomPoint/Line/Path 3D modes; one RenderTree/live renderer/emitter/export path; shared guides and overlays; legacy parallel core API removed with migration guide. Final validation: deno task check; 384 tests; draw-call gates for start+three-d; visual/PNG smoke on 16 routes.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Zachary Charlop-Powers
comments.text:
Plan review (2026-07-31, from the session that built gggplot-4q2.10/.11). Verdict: sound, start it. Two corrections this plan makes to the original 8y2 description are improvements and I endorse both: (a) rejecting fixed GeomDefinition.dims 2|3 in favour of per-geom modes, which avoids duplicate geom identities for shared marks; (b) rejecting a global "mapped z means 3D" rule. VERIFIED (b): geom/mod.ts:168 declares z as an optional aesthetic on tile, so a global rule really would reroute existing 2D summary plots into 3D scenes. Nuance for whoever implements .1: that z lives in doc(...) METADATA, not a runtime code path, so do not go looking for a runtime z-consumer in tile, fail to find one, and conclude the constraint was imaginary. The lookAt/orthographic finding is also real: Camera3D advertises projection perspective|orthographic plus orthographicHeight/up/aspect, orbitFromLookAt drops them, and cameraViewProjection always builds perspective (the existing geom_3d test already documents "perspective-only"). Throwing rather than silently losing fields is right.

FIVE FINDINGS, most consequential first.

1. NO HOME FOR THE 3D GUIDE-CONFIGURATION SURFACE, AND .7 CANNOT PASS WITHOUT ONE. .4 says "eliminate Guides3D", but neither §10 nor any child says where Point3DSpec.guides (GuideSpec3D = {axes, grid, titles, tickCount}) and params.sizeMode land in the unified GGSpec. Three of the four fold onto existing 2D theme keys (theme.grid, theme.axes), but tickCount has NO 2D counterpart: 2D derives tick count from panel width inside guideLayout (floor(width/90), clamped 2..8), and a perspective cube has no panel width, which is exactly why 3D took a fixed count. This is not hypothetical — .7's acceptance criterion is "four existing visual examples retain their appearance", and the Swizzled3D example is built on guides: { grid: false, tickCount: 3 }. As written .7 cannot pass. Filed as gggplot-4q2.13.9, blocking .4 and .7.

2. gggplot-42n SHOULD BE SEQUENCED INTO THIS EPIC, NOT LEFT BESIDE IT. The unification rewrites exactly the guide-emission code where that bug lives (axisTickValues' raw linspace vs use.gpu Grid's own nice ScaleTrait divisions). Fixing it after .4 means doing the guide work twice; fixing it with .4 means the unified path is born correct. It also interacts with finding 1: if breaks become pretty/extended, tickCount becomes a HINT rather than an exact count, which changes what belongs in the spec. Dependency added: 42n now blocks .4. Separately gggplot-4q2.12 (camera-aware tick-label edges) touches the same guide code and would conflict with .4, so it now depends on .4.

3. THE "MINIMAL NAMED CAMERA/VIEW WRAPPER COMPONENT" CARRIES THE MOST NOVELTY AND GETS ONE CLAUSE. It must seed OrbitControls, mount the Cartesian scene, AND compose the flat overlay — but the overlay must be a SIBLING pass (<Pass overlay> under FlatCamera), never a child of the orbit camera, because OrbitCamera supplies ViewProvider and no LayoutContext (verified when building gggplot-4q2.11; Pass's 'overlay' flag sets the color attachment loadOp to 'load'). So this single RenderNode must expand into two passes, two cameras, and two distinct child subtrees, while renderTree today maps one node to one component with a flat children list. That needs an explicit node shape decided up front (scene-children vs overlay-children, or two siblings under a wrapper). Constraint added to .4's design. Estimates deliberately left alone, but flagging that 32h for .4 INCLUDING this looks light, and once the node shape is drafted the wrapper may deserve its own bead.

4. NO LIVE-GPU GATE IN ANY ACCEPTANCE CRITERION. .5 asks for "a visual 3D smoke test", but the lesson of gggplot-4q2.9 — and of building .10/.11 — is that unit tests and route-health checks both stay green while the layer draws NOTHING. The draw-call gate is what actually catches it, and it caught two upstream traps during .10: the Grid auto homogeneous-w range and Tick's tangent-vs-offset semantics. Added to .4/.5/.8 acceptance: deno task test:draw-calls stays green with #three-d in the expected range (today 4 surfaces, 238 draws, 2731 instances) and #start unchanged.

5. MINOR: THE DEFAULT CAMERA NUMBERS ARE NOW DUPLICATED. §10.3 restates bearing pi/4, pitch 0.45, radius 3.6, fov pi/4, near 0.1, far 100 inline; those already exist as DEFAULT_CAMERA_3D in geom_3d/types.ts. Either have .2 reference the constant or pin them with a test, or the doc will drift. Added to .2's acceptance.

ON THE ESTIMATE: 158h sums correctly across the eight children, and excluding gggplot-5tg is honest since that bead is open and unestimated. 20-25 days reads optimistic mainly because of finding 3 — the wrapper is the one piece with no existing analog in either path. Numbers left unchanged pending the node-shape decision.

title: SPIKE: one grammar/spec for 2D and 3D — shared geom API and singleton camera
description:
DESIGN SPIKE. Assess and specify one public grammar and one GGSpec serialization for 2D and 3D. Produce a decision section in docs/DESIGN_3D_CONSIDERATIONS.md (or an ADR) and ordered implementation beads. Do not implement the refactor from this bead.

WHY NOW

Point3DSpec is a parallel serialization because the 3D slice began as a spike, not because 3D requires a separate grammar. It is effectively a flattened single-layer GGSpec: it reuses the same data/mapping concepts and literally reuses PlotLabels and Theme. AesName already includes z; the 3D overlay already reuses the 2D legend/label/render-tree paths; and both point paths already emit flat tensors. The genuine 3D-only concerns are camera/view wiring, a third position scale/guide, depth/topology, and some host behavior.

DESIGN DIRECTION

1. Unify the user-facing grammar and serialized GGSpec. Internal lowering may remain dimension-specialized where useful.
2. Do not add a spec-level mode flag. For shared marks such as point, line, and path, keep one public geom builder and let the mapped position axes plus geom capability select 2D or 3D lowering. Reserve 3d-suffixed names for intrinsically 3D topology such as surfaces. Assess registry metadata such as supportedPositionAxes or dimensional capability; a fixed GeomDefinition.dims: 2 | 3 is likely too restrictive for shared geoms.
3. Camera is a named top-level spec component beside coord/facet/theme: camera3d(options?) -> SpecPart {tag: camera} -> GGSpec.camera. It is not a geom and not a coord. Coord is data-to-cube; camera is cube-to-screen.
4. GGSpec has at most one camera. The builder uses singleton replacement semantics like coord/facet; later camera3d calls replace the earlier value, preferably with a diagnostic. Camera is plot-wide, never per-layer or per-facet.
5. camera3d() has a documented standard three-quarter perspective default and accepts partial overrides. Calling it serializes an explicit canonical camera declaration; omitting it still resolves to the same default for a 3D plot. Serialize plain camera parameters, never live controls; matrix lowering is a compiler/emitter concern.
6. Reject a camera on a purely 2D plot rather than silently ignoring it. Initially reject mixed 2D/3D layers unless the spike defines a coherent z-scale/guide contract; implicit z=0 promotion is not a free default.

QUESTIONS THE SPIKE MUST RESOLVE

- Exact geom capability metadata and dimensionality inference, including inherited plot mappings, layer mappings, missing z values, and intrinsically 3D geoms.
- Blocking type work: PositionAxis currently excludes z and Coord.project differs from the 3D swizzle. Confirm whether gggplot-5tg is sufficient.
- Shared stat/position behavior in 3D, including which existing operations remain meaningful and how unsupported combinations fail.
- Mixed-dimensional layers and 3D faceting policy.
- Whether Guides3D and Render3DNode can collapse into ordinary RenderNodes, including the missing Tick component.
- One emitter instead of emitSource plus emitPoint3dSource. Source specs serialize canonical camera parameters; emitted render code may contain the derived matrix.
- Camera projection model. The existing lookAt Camera3D includes orthographic/up/aspect fields that orbitFromLookAt does not preserve. Choose a canonical tagged model that supports these end to end, or reject unsupported forms; never silently discard fields. Prefer one simple canonical camera3d input, with lookAt convenience lowering immediately if retained.
- Compatibility and migration for Point3DSpec, geomPoint3d, apps/site, and emitted source.

DELIVERABLE

A written unify/partial/keep-parallel decision; concrete serialized examples for a shared geom in 2D and 3D, default camera, partial camera override, and no-camera 2D; exact registry/inference and singleton rules; migration plan; ordered implementation beads; and an honest compiler/type-widening cost estimate.
design: REVISED DESIGN CONSTRAINTS (2026-07-31): Unify the public grammar and GGSpec first; internal lowering may remain specialized. Shared marks such as point, line, and path should use one public builder, with a mapped z axis activating 3D lowering. Reserve 3d-suffixed geom names for topology that is intrinsically 3D, such as surfaces, rather than for a rendering mode. Therefore do not assume GeomDefinition.dims: 2 | 3 is sufficient: assess registry metadata such as supportedPositionAxes or dimensional capability, and derive active plot dimensionality from mappings plus geom requirements. A plot must not need a user-visible mode flag. Camera is a distinct named spec component, not a geom and not a coord: camera3d(options?) produces SpecPart {tag: camera} and stores one optional top-level GGSpec.camera value. GGSpec structure guarantees at most one camera; repeated add calls use the existing singleton convention for coord/facet, with later replacement and preferably a diagnostic. The camera declaration is plain JSON and canonical orbit parameters; partial overrides resolve against a documented standard three-quarter perspective default. Calling camera3d() must serialize an explicit canonical/default camera block, while omitting it still gives the same deterministic default for a 3D plot. Camera parameters, not runtime controls or a matrix, are the source-spec serialization; the compiler may lower them to a matrix for rendering/emission. Camera is plot-wide: no per-layer or per-facet cameras. Reject camera on a purely 2D plot rather than silently ignoring it. The spike must explicitly resolve projection semantics: the existing lookAt Camera3D union includes orthographic fields that orbitFromLookAt cannot preserve. Canonical serialization must not silently discard projection/up/aspect/orthographicHeight; either support a tagged projection model end to end or reject unsupported orthographic input. Prefer a single simple canonical input, with any lookAt convenience helper lowering immediately to it. Initially reject mixed 2D/3D layers unless a coherent shared z/scale/guide contract is designed; implicit z=0 promotion is useful but not a free default.
acceptance_criteria: Decision document specifies: (1) one GGSpec and one fluent grammar for shared 2D/3D marks; (2) exact geom capability metadata and dimensionality inference rules; (3) camera3d API, defaults, partial override behavior, canonical JSON shape, singleton/replacement behavior, and validation on 2D plots; (4) perspective/orthographic and lookAt handling without semantic loss; (5) mixed-dimensional layer policy; (6) migration from Point3DSpec and geomPoint3d, with implementation beads and cost estimate. Include example serialized specs for default camera, partial override, and no-camera 2D plot.
notes: DECISION COMPLETED 2026-07-31: unify, with specialization behind shared geoms. The accepted design is docs/DESIGN_3D_CONSIDERATIONS.md §10. Fundamental correction: dimension is selected from geom-declared modes plus the effective mapping, not from a fixed geom dims field and not from z globally, because tile/statSummary2d already use z as a 2D value aesthetic. Camera is one top-level canonical perspective-orbit JSON component built by camera3d(); omission uses the same default, partial options serialize fully resolved values, later additions replace, runtime controls/matrices stay out of GGSpec, and camera-on-2D is invalid. Mixed dimensions and 3D facets reject initially. Implementation epic gggplot-4q2.13 has eight ordered children (.1-.8); .1 and .2 are parallel ready foundations, .3 correctly depends on gggplot-5tg, .4 joins them, .5/.6 split live and emit, then .7/.8 migrate/extend. Estimate: 158 hours, honest 20-25 developer-day range excluding gggplot-5tg.
close_reason: Design spike completed: accepted unified grammar/GGSpec/camera decision documented in DESIGN_3D_CONSIDERATIONS §10; implementation epic gggplot-4q2.13 and ordered child dependencies created.

comments.author: Zachary Charlop-Powers
comments.text: API review (2026-07-31): The unification premise is right, but two details were too implementation-led. First, fixed dims: 2 | 3 metadata would make the registry choose between separate geom identities and undercut a shared geom API. For marks with identical semantics, the mapped position axes plus geom capability should select lowering; intrinsically 3D topology can keep a 3d-specific name. Second, camera must be a first-class singleton grammar component, not merely an optional field mentioned by the emitter. Proposed camera3d() follows the existing SpecPart/add model, serializes canonical parameters with good defaults and partial overrides, and is invalid on a 2D-only plot. The current Camera3D lookAt/orthographic union also loses projection-related fields when converted to orbit, so the spike must prevent that silent semantic loss. The DESIGN and ACCEPTANCE fields now supersede the older fixed-dims recommendation in the description.

title: Grid lines and tick labels can disagree: use.gpu ScaleTrait divisions vs gggplot's trained breaks
description: Surfaced while deciding gggplot-4q2.8.5 (3D guides); the defect is in the EXISTING 2D path and 3D would inherit it. compile/mod.ts emits node('Grid', {axes, width, zBias}) with no first/second ScaleProps, so use.gpu's Grid generates its OWN grid-line positions internally (ScaleTrait: mode/divide/unit/base/nice=true -> 'nice' round divisions; see @use-gpu/plot/mjs/layer/grid.mjs, util/domain.mjs linear/logarithmic). But the tick LABELS come from gggplot: compile/axes.ts axisTickValues uses linspace(domain, tickCount) over the trained domain, which is NOT nice-rounded and uses a tickCount derived from canvas width (floor(width/90), clamped 2..8). So grid lines and labelled ticks are generated by two different algorithms and need not coincide — e.g. an expanded continuous domain like [-0.4, 10.4] labels at linspace steps while the grid rules at nice multiples. ggplot2's contract is that panel grid lines sit AT the breaks. Fix direction: make gggplot's trained breaks authoritative and pass them down — either supply Grid's first/second ScaleProps so its divisions match, or replace Grid with explicit Line nodes at the break positions. Whichever way, breaks must be computed ONCE and shared by grid + ticks + labels. Also worth adopting nice/pretty breaks (ggplot2 uses labeling::extended) instead of raw linspace. Blocks nothing, but gggplot-4q2.10 (3D in-scene guides) will replicate the mismatch if this stays open.
notes:
LIVE EVIDENCE (from gggplot-4q2.10, 2026-07-31): now visible in the shipped 3D route, not just theoretical. The site's helix demo trains a domain of roughly [-0.9992, 1.0], and linspace over that raw domain labels ticks '0.5004' / '-0.9998' / '-0.4998' instead of 0.5 / -1 / -0.5. Screenshotted in a real WebGPU browser. So the defect has two halves: (a) breaks are not 'nice' (ggplot2 uses labeling::extended pretty breaks, we use raw linspace over the expanded domain), and (b) use.gpu's Grid generates its OWN nice divisions internally, so the grid lines do not sit at the labelled breaks either.

Scope note: geom_3d now reuses the SAME generator (compile/axes.ts axisTickValues + tickLabel, exported for this in gggplot-4q2.10), so fixing it here fixes 2D and 3D together — that reuse was deliberate. A fix should compute breaks ONCE and feed grid + ticks + labels: adopt pretty/extended breaks, then either pass Grid's first/second ScaleProps so its divisions match, or replace Grid with explicit lines at the break positions.
close_reason: Computed shared pretty breaks for 2D/3D labels and grids; use.gpu Grid receives exact divisions for regular breaks and serializable GuideLines render irregular explicit breaks. Full suite: 390 passed.

title: 3D legend + plot-title overlay: screen-space pass over the 3D render
description: Implement the Q17 half of the gggplot-4q2.8.5 decision (docs/DESIGN_3D_CONSIDERATIONS.md §7). Legends and plot titles are PAGE furniture — content depends on trained color/size/alpha scales, never on the camera — so reuse compile/legends.ts legendNodes + plotLabelNodes VERBATIM (they already produce flat [-1,1] RenderNodes); 3D grows no legend code of its own. Wiring constraint: OrbitCamera provides only ViewProvider, NOT LayoutContext, so the overlay CANNOT hang under the orbit camera — mount it as a sibling under the canvas's own flat layout (AutoCanvas/FlatCamera), drawn after the 3D pass with depthTest:false. See apps/site/src/scene3d.tsx for the current OrbitControls->OrbitCamera->Pass->GGPlot3D tree. Framing: the 3D pass is deliberately NOT inset for the legend — there is no 3D analog of guideLayout shrinking panel bounds. If overlap turns out to matter, the fix is a camera offset/dolly (a camera concern), NOT a margin solver. Needs 3D color/size scales to be exposed to the legend builder (trainColor3d already exists in geom_3d).
notes:
DONE + VERIFIED LIVE. Implements Q17 of gggplot-4q2.8.5.

geom_3d/legend.ts buildOverlay3d() reuses the 2D builders VERBATIM (compile/legends.ts legendNodes + plotLabelNodes) — 3D grew no legend code of its own, exactly as the decision required. Render3DNode gained overlay: RenderNode[] (flat [-1,1] nodes, camera-invariant, so resolved at compile time); empty when there is nothing to key, letting the host skip the second pass. geom_3d/overlay.tsx GGPlot3DOverlay wraps them in Embedded{normalize} (the same bridge the 2D root uses, and what establishes the Plot font/virtual-layers wrapper) under its own FontLoader.

Wiring in apps/site/src/scene3d.tsx: <FlatCamera><Pass overlay><GGPlot3DOverlay/></Pass></FlatCamera> as a SIBLING after the OrbitControls/OrbitCamera pass — never inside the orbit camera, which supplies ViewProvider but no LayoutContext. Verified in @use-gpu/workbench pass/util that Pass's 'overlay' flag sets the color attachment loadOp to 'load' (and 'merge' would do the same for depth), so the flat pass composites onto the 3D render instead of clearing it; depth is cleared, so the overlay always draws on top. The 3D pass is deliberately NOT inset for the legend, per the decision. A mapped size column is NOT keyed: 3D sizes are raw values with no trained size scale for the 2D builder to describe.

Host theme: added withSiteChartTheme3d to apps/site/src/chart_theme.ts. 3D reads the same Theme keys as 2D and needs them for the same reason — without a host theme the guide/legend text falls back to near-black, invisible on the dark canvas (observed in the browser before the fix). Deliberately no fontFamily for 3D: the 2D host loads Basic/Lato via createFontResources and hands them to GGPlot's FontLoader, while the 3D scene mounts a bare FontLoader, so naming an unloaded family would request a face that does not exist.

REAL 2D BUG FOUND AND FIXED: compile/legends.ts plotLabelNodes had plot title/subtitle at POSITIVE y and caption at negative. In the flat guide space y grows DOWNWARD — guideLayout maps the TOP margin onto '-1 + 2*topPx/height', and axisGuideOverlay places x tick labels (visually low) at the numerically larger panelBounds[3]. So the title was rendering along the BOTTOM edge and the caption along the top. No 2D example or test had ever put a plot title on screen, so it went unnoticed until the 3D overlay rendered one. Title/subtitle now negative, caption positive, tag top-right; test added asserting the ordering.

VERIFIED: deno task test 397/397; deno task check clean. Draw-call gate #three-d = 4 surfaces, 238 draws, 2731 instances (was 1 surface/33 draws); #start unchanged. Visual gate 16/16 routes, exit 0. Screenshotted all four 3D examples in a real WebGPU browser: discrete swatch legend (band: high/low/mid), continuous COLORBAR legend (distance from origin, 1.73/0.35), title+subtitle now at top-left, in-scene guides unaffected.
close_reason: Screen-space legend + plot-title overlay built and verified live: reuses the 2D builders verbatim, composited via a sibling FlatCamera Pass with overlay loadOp. Also fixed an inverted title/caption placement in the shared 2D builder that this surfaced.

title: 3D in-scene guides: Axis/Grid/ticks/labels inside Cartesian
description: Implement the Q16/Q18 half of the gggplot-4q2.8.5 decision (docs/DESIGN_3D_CONSIDERATIONS.md §7). Guides are IN-SCENE, inside Cartesian, in data space — the same split the 2D compiler already uses (compile/mod.ts emits Grid/Axis inside the view; only text goes to the overlay). Work: (1) Render3DNode gains a DECLARATIVE guides field (which axes are drawn, their ranges, tick values + label strings), never pre-baked screen positions, so the render layer keeps per-frame anchoring freedom while emit.ts resolves it once from the serialized initial camera. (2) geom_3d/render.tsx emits three Axis nodes (axis: x|y|z) + up to three Grid nodes (GridTrait.axes is a 2-AXIS PAIR: xy/yz/xz, one per coordinate plane) with auto=true — use.gpu culls the camera-facing face in-shader (getGridAutoState vs getViewPosition), so gggplot needs NO live camera on the CPU. (3) Tick/Label from the trained 3D position scales (geom_3d/position.ts trainPosition3d), NOT use.gpu's Scale component — the grammar owns breaks, same as 2D axisTickValues. (4) Label depth=0 (pixel-constant, consistent with Q15 sizing) and anchors pinned to FIXED cube edges (minimum-corner), camera-independent; labels billboard by construction (use.gpu label vertex shader is screen-aligned). (5) emit.ts parity: emitted source carries the same guide nodes. (6) Theme surface: reuse 2D theme.grid/axes/gridColor/gridWidth/axisColor/axisWidth. Do NOT run guideLayout — the 3D pass has no flat panel to inset. Known limitation to document: at some bearings a fixed edge swings behind the cube (camera-aware edge selection is a separate deferred bead).
notes:
DONE + VERIFIED LIVE. Implements the Q16/Q18 half of gggplot-4q2.8.5.

New packages/core/src/geom_3d/guides.ts: Guides3D is DECLARATIVE (per-axis range, break positions + label strings, grid planes, the minimum-corner origin, resolved style) — no pre-baked screen positions, so the render layer keeps per-frame anchoring freedom while emit resolves once from the serialized camera. Breaks come from the 2D generator: exported axisTickValues + tickLabel from compile/axes.ts and reused them, so 2D and 3D cannot drift and gggplot-42n stays a single-point fix. Discrete axes tick at level indices (numericRange convention), continuous at linspace over the trained domain.

Wiring: Point3DSpec gained guides/theme/labels (theme + labels reuse the 2D Theme/PlotLabels types); Render3DNode gained guides; lowerPoint3d builds them from the SAME trained scales the marks use, so ticks can never describe a different data box than the Cartesian range. render.tsx and emit.ts realize the identical tree: Grid x3 (xy/yz/xz, auto) + Axis x3 + Tick + Label(ticks) + Label(title) per axis, all inside Cartesian in data space. Label depth=0 (pixel-constant, per Q15/Q18); anchors pinned to fixed minimum-corner cube edges.

TWO REAL TRAPS FOUND BY READING USE.GPU SOURCE (both now documented in DESIGN_3D_CONSIDERATIONS §7):
1. The homogeneous range must be pinned to [1,1]. Cartesian's matrix only reads the 3 data ranges, but it publishes the PARSED ranges as RangeContext, and parseRanges3 pads a 3-range input with a default 4th range of [0,2]. Grid 'auto' reads parentRange[i] for EVERY i including w, so an unpinned w range seats grid vertices at w=0 (a direction, not a point). Added coord.ts cartesianRange4() used by both live and emit paths; emit previously appended [0,1], which had the same flaw. Regression test added.
2. Tick's 'tangent' is NOT the tick direction — the mark is drawn along 'offset'; 'tangent' feeds the LOD rule that thins ticks as projected spacing tightens, so its LENGTH must be the break spacing.

Also fixed during visual verification: the axis-title pixel nudge pushed vertically regardless of placement, so the y-axis title landed on top of its own tick labels. Offsets are now direction-aware (tickLabelOffset/titleLabelOffset in guides.ts), shared by render + emit.

VERIFIED: deno task test 393/393; deno task check clean; deno fmt clean. Draw-call gate #three-d went 1 draw/160 instances -> 33 draws/751 instances (guides reach the GPU); #start unaffected. Visual gate 16/16 routes, no console errors. Screenshotted the live canvas in a real WebGPU browser: grids render on the FAR faces only (Grid auto's in-shader back-face culling works), plus three axis rules, tick marks, tick text and x/y/z titles clear of the ticks.

KNOWN COSMETIC, NOT A GUIDES BUG: break VALUES are linspace over the raw trained domain, so the helix demo (domain ~[-0.9992, 1]) labels ticks '0.5004' instead of '0.5'. That is gggplot-42n, inherited from the 2D path.
close_reason: In-scene 3D guides built and verified live: declarative Guides3D from the trained scales, realized identically by render.tsx and emit.ts as Grid(auto)x3 + Axis x3 + Tick/Label per axis. All gates green.

title: Unify 2D Coord.project onto a use.gpu-style axes swizzle string
description: Decided under gggplot-4q2.8.2 (Q4): 2D Coord.project [PositionAxis,PositionAxis] is isomorphic to a use.gpu output-axis swizzle ([y,x] <-> yxzw), the general form 3D already uses (geom_3d/coord.ts resolveAxes3d). Unify the 2D representation onto the same swizzle so coord_flip (2D) and 3D axis remap share one path. Cross-cutting on the stable 2D compiler: ir/types.ts (Coord.project; widen PositionAxis to include z), compile/axes.ts, compile/facet_layout.ts, dsl/layout.ts (coordFlip sugar) + 2D tests. Representation-only; keep coordFlip() and coord_polar(theta=) behavior identical. This is now a prerequisite for gggplot-4q2.13.3, the x/y/z compiler widening; land it before that child rather than waiting for the remaining 3D unification.
notes: Replaced Coord.project tuples with canonical Coord.axes swizzles. coordFlip/coordPolar(theta=y) serialize axes:'yx'; 2D compiler validates xy/yx plus full xyzw/yxzw boundary forms; PositionAxis widened with z; axes, facet, and docs migrated. check:core and 181 pipeline tests pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: 3D guides: in-scene axes/grid vs screen-space overlay; legends; billboarded labels
description: Q16-Q18. AxisTrait/GridTrait (axis/axes, range, zBias) are a different layout problem than compile/guides.ts's 2D margin solver (guideLayout measures text into pixel margins). Decide in-scene 3D axes vs screen-space overlay, how legends composite over the 3D pass, and whether tick labels billboard to face the camera.
notes:
DECIDED (planning only — no runtime code; the decision is additive, so nothing had to change to make it true). Recorded in docs/DESIGN_3D_CONSIDERATIONS.md §7 + §1 trait table + §8 status table + §9 process.

Q16: axes/grids/ticks are IN-SCENE, inside Cartesian, in data space; only legends and plot titles are screen-space. Not a new split — compile/mod.ts already emits Grid/Axis INSIDE the 2D Cartesian/Polar view and sends only text to the flat overlay (axisGuideOverlay/legendNodes). 3D = three Axis nodes (axis x|y|z) + up to three Grid nodes (GridTrait.axes is a 2-AXIS PAIR xy/yz/xz, one per cube coordinate plane). guideLayout does NOT carry over: it exists to inset a FLAT panel for measured text, and a perspective-projected cube has no flat panel or stable margin. KEY FINDING: Grid's 'auto' prop already IS camera-aware back-face selection, resolved in-shader per frame — getGridPosition emits each line twice (min face + shifted max face) and getGridAutoState compares getViewPosition() against the transformed face normal, collapsing the camera-facing copy to vec4(0). So gggplot never needs the live camera on the CPU for grids.

Q17: legends + plot titles stay screen-space, reusing compile/legends.ts legendNodes/plotLabelNodes VERBATIM (they already emit flat [-1,1] RenderNodes) — 3D gets no legend code of its own. Wiring constraint: OrbitCamera provides only ViewProvider, NOT LayoutContext, so the overlay is a sibling under the canvas's flat layout, after the 3D pass, depthTest:false. The 3D pass is deliberately NOT inset for it; if overlap matters the fix is a camera offset/dolly, not a margin solver.

Q18: billboarding is NOT a choice — verified in @use-gpu/wgsl instance/vertex/label.wgsl that Label glyphs are screen-space quads (worldToClip(position) + a screen-space offset scaled by getScreenScale(clip.w, depth)), so they always face the camera and cannot be tilted. The real decision is the ANCHOR. Pinned: LabelTrait.depth = 0 (pixel-constant, consistent with Q15 sizing) and tick labels/axis titles anchored to FIXED minimum-corner cube edges, camera-independent. Documented limitation: at some bearings an edge swings behind the cube. Camera-aware edge selection can NEVER be compile-time (per Q8 the live view is runtime state that never reaches the compiler) — deferred to gggplot-4q2.12.

IR consequence: guides lower DECLARATIVELY (which axes, ranges, tick values, label strings), never as pre-baked screen positions — the render layer keeps per-frame anchoring freedom while emit.ts resolves once from the serialized initial camera.

Follow-ups filed: gggplot-4q2.10 (in-scene axes/grid/ticks/labels), gggplot-4q2.11 (screen-space legend/title overlay), gggplot-4q2.12 (camera-aware edge selection, deferred, blocked on .10), gggplot-42n (BUG surfaced in the EXISTING 2D path: grid lines come from use.gpu's own nice ScaleTrait divisions while tick labels come from gggplot's linspace breaks, so they need not coincide; ggplot2's contract is grid lines AT the breaks).
close_reason: Q16-Q18 decided and recorded in docs/DESIGN_3D_CONSIDERATIONS.md §7; implementation split into gggplot-4q2.10/.11/.12 and bug gggplot-42n.

title: 3D transforms (ObjectTrait) — expose in the grammar or keep compiler-internal?
description: Q1-Q3. ObjectTrait gives every node position/scale/rotation/quaternion/matrix; 2D gggplot has no layer-transform concept. Decide whether transforms are grammar-visible (a transform() spec part? plot/layer level?) or compiler-internal for coords/facets only. Pin euler order for serializability (composeTransform default xyz).
notes: DECIDED (Q1-Q3). Q1: transforms stay COMPILER-INTERNAL, NOT a grammar surface. Rationale: ggplot2 has no layer-transform concept and ARCHITECTURE 'Design rules' pins the DSL to geom_*/scale_*/coord_*/facet_*/theme_* spec parts, so a transform() part would be a new top-level concept with no ggplot2 counterpart. It is also unnecessary — every grammatical reason to move a layer in space is already owned by a decided concept: axis remap = coord swizzle (4q2.8.2 Q4), framing = camera (4q2.8.1 Q8), panel placement = facets. ObjectTrait stays available to the COMPILER to realize those (e.g. 3D facet panels). Q2: moot (not exposed); for internal use the order is fixed by Cartesian itself (read from @use-gpu/plot/mjs/view/cartesian.mjs): normalize(range) -> swizzle(axes) -> composeTransform(TRS/matrix), camera view*projection on top — i.e. a compiler transform acts in CUBE space, after the coord, before the camera, which keeps coord semantics and camera framing independent. Q3: pin xyz Euler order (composeTransform default) if ever serialized; internal callers should prefer quaternion/matrix, which are order-free. CONSEQUENCE: Render3DNode carries no transform field and render.tsx passes no ObjectTrait props — documented inline at the Cartesian call site so the next reader doesn't add one by reflex. No behavior change; repo suite 387/387, deno task check clean. Docs: DESIGN_3D_CONSIDERATIONS §2 + header + status table + process updated.
close_reason: Closed

title: 3D mark sizing + depth/transparency semantics
description: Q12-Q15. PointTrait/LineTrait 'depth' selects pixel-constant (0, ggplot2-like physical sizes) vs perspective-scaled world units (1). Current code sets depth:1 ACCIDENTALLY — combined with OrbitCamera.scale that is why point visibility was so confusing. Decide the default and whether it is user-controllable. Also ROPTrait: default depthTest/depthWrite, and gggplot's contract for alpha<1 in 3D (order-dependent; use.gpu has mode:'transparent').
notes:
BLOCKER FOUND: PointTrait.depth and OrbitCamera.scale are coupled and must be settled together. depth:1 (perspective world-unit sizing) + scale:2160 is the only combination observed to render; depth:0 (constant pixels = ggplot2 physical-size semantics, and the resolution-independent choice since it removes the canvasHeight/scale ratio) renders NOTHING. Work out use.gpu's point size vs view-ratio math before choosing. ALSO: the live 3D canvas is currently NOT drawing on the docs page even with the depth:1+scale pairing restored — needs a visual re-check; the pipeline itself is tested and emits correct data.
CORRECTION (after gggplot-4q2.9, commit b4d86c9): the 'BLOCKER FOUND' note above is void. depth:0 does NOT render nothing — nothing rendered at ANY depth because mark tensors carried gggplot's shorthand format ('vec4') into use.gpu's schema, so the layer silently drew zero. With that fixed, depth 0 and depth 1 both draw all 160 points, with and without OrbitCamera.scale (verified by draw-call instrumentation). So depth/scale are NOT coupled by a render-or-not constraint; this bead is a free design choice on the merits: pixel-constant (ggplot2 physical-size semantics, resolution-independent, lets scale go away) vs perspective world units.
DECIDED + IMPLEMENTED. Q15: default sizing = pixel-constant (Point depth:0, ggplot2 physical-size parity); user override via params.sizeMode 'constant'|'perspective' (perspective->depth:1). Q10 (belongs to 4q2.8.1) fixed as a byproduct: dropped OrbitCamera.scale in scene3d.tsx (scale=null -> unit=1, ratio=pixelRatio), so pixel sizes are true device pixels and framing is resolution-independent; ChartCanvas3D fixed height is now a plain layout choice. title: 3D camera model: spec vs coord vs runtime; lookAt vs orbit; fix resolution-dependence
description: Q8-Q11. Camera is currently BOTH lookAt (spec/emit via cameraViewProjection) and orbit (live via orbitCameraProps) — two parameterizations of one camera. OrbitCamera.scale makes framing resolution-dependent (view ratio = canvasHeight/scale); current code pins a fixed frame height as a workaround. Decide: is the camera spec, coord, or runtime view state (cf. ARCHITECTURE 5 Phase 3 pan/zoom)? Pick ONE canonical parameterization. Fix resolution independence. Optional: @use-gpu/interact for orbit/zoom (NOT installed; adds runtime state vs serializable spec tension).
notes:
PARTIAL DECISION: canonical camera = ORBIT (radius/bearing/pitch/target) — chosen because OrbitCamera consumes it AND OrbitControls (@use-gpu/interact, now installed ^0.20.0) seeds from/emits the same fields, so interactivity is a later drop-in with NO spec change (spec = initial view, runtime = live view; same split as ARCHITECTURE 5 2D pan/zoom). Resolves Q9 (one canonical form; lookAt is sugar via orbitFromLookAt). Added DEFAULT_CAMERA_3D standard three-quarter view + made Point3DSpec.camera OPTIONAL. STILL OPEN: Q8 (is camera spec/coord/runtime formally?), Q10 (resolution independence — still blocked on sizing, see 4q2.8.3), Q11 (actually wire OrbitControls). NOTE: OrbitCamera is perspective-only; an orthographic 3D camera would be a separate kind.
Q10 (resolution-independence) RESOLVED under gggplot-4q2.8.3: OrbitCamera.scale removed from scene3d.tsx now that default sizing is pixel-constant (depth:0); framing no longer depends on canvasHeight/scale. STILL OPEN here: Q8 (is camera formally spec/coord/runtime?) and Q11 (actually wire OrbitControls).
DECIDED + IMPLEMENTED (Q8, Q11; Q9/Q10 already settled). Q8: camera = SPEC (initial serializable orbit view) + RUNTIME (live view owned by OrbitControls); NOT a coord (coord = axes swizzle+Cartesian range = data->cube; camera = cube->screen; kept separate). Mirrors ARCHITECTURE §5 2D pan/zoom split. Q11: OrbitControls wired in apps/site/src/scene3d.tsx via render-prop, seeded from spec initial orbit params, feeding live radius/bearing/pitch/target to OrbitCamera each frame; drag/zoom mutate runtime only, spec+emit (initial view) unchanged. AutoCanvas already provides DOMEvents+CursorProvider+LayoutContext (Canvas supplies LayoutContext=full-canvas rect), so no extra event wiring. Removed dead Fragment import/pragma. VERIFIED: check:site clean, lint clean, draw-call gate #three-d draws=1 instances=160 with OrbitControls in tree. Still open (deferred, not blocking): live->spec 'save this view' round-trip; perspective-only (ortho camera would be a separate kind). title: Research: correct use.gpu 3D render wiring (Cartesian IS usable) — analyze source + examples
description: Zach: Cartesian CAN be used for 3D; analyze use.gpu source + the plot/3d.tsx example rather than guessing. KEY FINDING this session: the black canvas was NOT Cartesian vs no-Cartesian nor camera choice — it was a swallowed 'Required context FontContext was used without being provided in SDFFontProvider' error. Plot wraps SDFFontProvider (needs FontContext); Embedded imports Plot internally too, so EVERY path needed a FontLoader. Adding FontLoader (from @use-gpu/workbench, as packages/3d did) clears the crash. Now: analyze plot/3d.tsx (https://gitlab.com/unconed/use.gpu/-/blob/master/packages/app/src/pages/plot/3d.tsx) + Cartesian/OrbitCamera/Pass/Point source in node_modules to nail the exact 3D wiring (Cartesian range + camera + FontLoader + correct Point props/positions shape). Verify a helix renders in the docs 3D example.
notes: RESOLVED via source analysis. Cartesian IS usable (Zach was right): reading cartesian.mjs shows it maps a 3-axis range -> [-1,1] cube via a mat4 and provides MatrixContext/RangeContext/TransformContext (NOT LayoutContext) that Point needs. The blocker was never Cartesian vs camera choice -- it was the missing FontLoader (FontContext for Plot's SDFFontProvider). Working wiring documented in 4q2.6.

title: geom_3d live render + docs 3D example (visual proof)
description: Wire geom_3d into a live use.gpu render component (Cartesian 3D range + camera matrix + Point) and add a rendering 3D example to the docs site; verify it draws in WebGPU.
notes:
Built the geom_3d live-render component (render.tsx: Embedded>Cartesian{range,cameraMatrix}>Point) + site hosts (scene3d.tsx, ChartCanvas3D.tsx) + subpath aliases. Added a '3D (preview)' docs page. BLOCKED: the vec4 Point does not rasterize through use.gpu's Cartesian view -- tried Plot vs Embedded, OrbitCamera vs FlatCamera, raw-array vs FlatTensor-object positions, formats on/off, camera-matrix on/off, 2/3/4-axis range, depth on/off, and fixed a real bug (example passed category strings as colors -> parseColorRGBA returned black). Canvas mounts under WebGPU with no console errors but draws nothing; needs a dedicated use.gpu source/view spike, not black-box iteration. STOPGAP: docs page shows the REAL emitted use.gpu source + lowered-node summary (honest, tested pipeline output) instead of a black canvas; live component kept as WIP, not mounted.
DONE: 3D helix point cloud renders live in WebGPU on the docs 3D (preview) page. Fix = FontLoader (Plot's SDFFontProvider needs FontContext; that swallowed error was the black canvas) + OrbitCamera scale + correct wiring OrbitCamera>Pass>FontLoader>Plot>Cartesian(range)>Point. Flat-native: Point consumes FlatTensor vec4 objects directly (no CPU expansion). GPU camera projection confirmed visually (perspective helix, height-band colors).
RETROSPECTIVE (approach critique): this was solved by trial-and-error, NOT research — Zach's criticism is correct. I permuted wrappers (Plot vs Embedded vs Cartesian), cameras (OrbitCamera vs FlatCamera), position shapes (raw Float32Array vs FlatTensor object vs nested arrays), and props (formats on/off, matrix on/off, 2/3/4-axis range, depth on/off) until pixels appeared, instead of first reading use.gpu's model. Cost: many wasted iterations and one wrong conclusion I stated confidently (that Cartesian was unusable in 3D). WHAT ACTUALLY WORKED, and why: (1) FontLoader is REQUIRED — Plot wraps SDFFontProvider which reads FontContext; Embedded imports Plot too, so every path needed it. Its absence threw an error the React error boundary swallowed, which is why everything was silently black with 'no console errors'. This was the single root cause of the whole saga. (2) Cartesian IS correct for 3D (read cartesian.mjs): it takes a 3-axis range, builds a mat4 mapping data->[-1,1] cube, and provides MatrixContext/RangeContext/TransformContext that Point needs; it does NOT need LayoutContext (that's Embedded, which is why OrbitCamera+Embedded failed). (3) OrbitCamera provides only ViewProvider (view/projection uniforms). (4) Point accepts FlatTensor OBJECTS directly (use.gpu source shape) with formats:{positions:'vec4<f32>'} — flat-native works, no CPU expansion. (5) OrbitCamera.scale was the last missing piece for visibility. KNOWN-BAD in the current setup: scale is coupled to canvas height (view ratio = canvasHeight/scale) so framing breaks on resize — I papered over it with a fixed frame height. Also unverified after the color-scale change.
CORRECTION: this was closed stating the live render works, and it did at the time (helix screenshot; that state merged to master ba0bcda). It has since STOPPED drawing on branch feature/geom-3d-scales — tracked as gggplot-4q2.9. Leaving this closed because the work did land and did render; the regression is its own bead.
CORRECTION (see gggplot-4q2.9, closed): the earlier note pointed at 4q2.9 as a branch regression. It was not a regression — instrumenting master's own build shows the three-d route issues ZERO draw calls there too, so the live 3D canvas has never actually drawn since ba0bcda; only the emitted source and the lowering were ever verified. Root cause and fix in b4d86c9.
