title: stat_ydensity drops categorical position axis: geom_violin renders nothing with only x/y mapped
description: Found in passing during gggplot-tzc.8. geom_violin (and any ydensity/density consumer) renders nothing when only x/y are mapped (no color/fill/shape/group). Root cause in packages/core/src/stat/distributions.ts:134 statDensityAxis: groupCols = groupColumnsOf(mapping,data).filter(c=>c!==valueCol), and groupColumnsOf (group/mod.ts:47) only considers IMPLICIT_GROUP_AES = [color,fill,shape,linetype] — NOT the categorical POSITION axis (x for ydensity, y for density). So for aes(x=cat, y=value): (1) all rows pool into ONE density across x categories (wrong — each category should get its own curve), and (2) the output dataFrame (out only holds valueCol + density + groupCols) has NO x column while the returned mapping still names the original x col, so violin lowering finds no x and draws nothing. Fix: in statDensityAxis(axis), treat the OTHER position axis posAxis=(axis==='y'?'x':'y') as a grouping+carry-through column when mapped and discrete — group density per posAxis category, emit posAxis in the output columns (constant per group), and set it in the returned mapping. Mirrors ggplot2 stat_ydensity computing one density per x group. Add a test: geom_violin with only x(discrete)/y mapped produces one density group per x level, output has the x column, renders a non-empty ChunkedFace. Keep existing color/fill-grouped violin behavior working.
close_reason: stat_ydensity/stat_density now group by the categorical position axis when no color/fill/shape/linetype is mapped. Fix in stat/distributions.ts statDensityAxis: when implicit group cols empty and posAxis (opposite the value axis) col is mapped+discrete, promote it into groupCols (density per position-category, posCol carried through output), and set mapping.group=posCol so lowerViolin's splitByEffectiveGroup splits per x-level. No-op (byte-identical) when color/fill IS mapped. Exported isDiscreteColumn for reuse. geom_violin with only x/y now renders one ChunkedFace with 2 mirrored 16-vertex loops instead of nothing. Full check clean, 305 core (1 new test), test:visual 15/15 green (violin routes ran), fixtures deterministic, only boxplot_violin.json changed. Verified by orchestrator.

title: ChunkedLine renders solid regardless of dash pattern
description: Surfaced during gggplot-tzc.3. ChunkedLine is realized over the workbench raw-line primitive (LineLayer/RawLines + useLineSegmentsSource), which has no dash support. lowerLine correctly batches nodes per dash pattern and threads a 'dash' prop through (satisfying tzc's node-split rule), but the dash value is not rendered — dashed/dotted geom_line/geom_path currently draw solid. Need a dash-capable line realization (e.g. shader-level stroke-dash on the raw line source, or route dashed batches through a dash-capable plot Line path) so per-dash style batches render correctly. Not a silent drop: the topology/prop plumbing already exists; only the visual realization is missing.
notes:
APPROACH DECISION (2026-07-19, user-selected): custom WGSL dash shader (screen-space-correct, reads st arc-length + dash array, discards 'off' fragments). Investigation findings for the implementer: (1) workbench RawLinesProps (primitives/raw-lines.d.mts) — the primitive ChunkedLine renders through — has NO dash uniform (props: position/segment/uv/st/color/width/depth/zBias/trim/size + source variants). It DOES expose st/sts (arc-length) which a dash material can consume. (2) plot's StrokeTrait (plot/mjs/traits.mjs:140) defines dash: optional(parseScalarArray) and plot Line's LineProps has dash?, but NO standalone reusable dash WGSL module was found in @use-gpu/wgsl or workbench — so plot's own dash rendering path must be located and either reused or replicated. (3) tzc.3 spike already established plot Line rejects our variable-length chunk topology, so we can't route dashed batches to plot Line without reintroducing nested arrays (regression). IMPLEMENTER MUST FIRST verify how plot actually renders dash end-to-end (does InnerLine produce visible dashes, via which shader/material?) and report that before authoring new WGSL; reuse Use.GPU's shader-linking machinery (@use-gpu/shader) rather than a bespoke pipeline. lowerLine already batches per dash pattern and threads a 'dash' prop onto the RenderNode — the plumbing exists; only the material is missing.
CHECKPOINT FINDING (before authoring WGSL): traced plot's StrokeTrait 'dash'
end-to-end -- InnerLine (plot/mjs/shape/line.mjs) destructures 'dash' out of
LineTraits into its catch-all 'flags' bag and forwards it into
schemaToArchetype/shape.flags, but grepped every real (non-lodash-false-
-positive) match for "dash" across @use-gpu/workbench/mjs, @use-gpu/plot/mjs,
and every .wgsl module under @use-gpu/wgsl (via each module's sourcemap
sourcesContent, which carries the original un-minified WGSL) and found NO
consumer anywhere -- LINE_SCHEMA, raw-lines.mjs's RawLines primitive (which
ChunkedLine already renders through), and every real fragment/vertex .wgsl
file are dash-blind. Outcome (b): no existing dash module to reuse; plot's
own dash rendering is dead code (typed + threaded, never wired to a shader).
Authored a minimal custom dash fragment material via @use-gpu/shader's
runtime `wgsl` tagged template (the same machinery render/rotated_label.tsx
already uses for a custom vertex shader) -- not a bespoke pipeline: it plugs
into RawLines' EXISTING 'getFragment' link point (workbench's
DEFAULT_MATERIAL_CONTEXT.solid.getFragment, currently getPassThruColor),
overriding it via provide(MaterialContext, ...) scoped to just the dashed
LineLayer element. Reads the per-vertex 'st' arc-length varying (a new
'sts' tensor computed in the live realization from the node's own positions
+ chunks, so RenderTree/fixture output is unchanged) and a small vec4 dash-
pattern uniform, discarding fragments in a gap. Screen-space correctness:
converts the DATA-space arc length to device-pixel-equivalent length inside
the shader via view.wgsl's getWorldScale(1.0, 0.0) -- the exact factor
RawLines' own line width already uses at its default depth -- which is
EXACT (not approximate) under gggplot's orthographic FlatCamera host,
because getWorldScale's only spatially-varying term collapses to a constant
1.0 whenever the projection's perspective row is zero (true by construction
for an orthographic camera), so a single global per-frame evaluation
(rather than a true per-fragment one keyed on unavailable clip-space w) is
correct, responds to future pan/zoom, and needed no vertex-shader surgery.
Implementation done: render/chunked_line.tsx (packDashUniforms,
computeArcLengths, getDashColorSource WGSL module, MaterialContext wiring;
solid lines never call provide(), so they render exactly as before) +
emit/mod.ts (CHUNKED_LINE_SOURCE/imports kept in textual parity). Tests:
packages/core/tests/chunked_line_dash_test.ts (10 new, pure-function +
emit/deno-check coverage). Full verification green: deno task check clean;
315/315 core tests pass (305 baseline + 10 new); fixtures --check clean
(dash is a material concern, RenderTree output unchanged); emit standalone
deno-check passes for both the original and a new dashed-line generated
module; deno task test:visual passed 15/15 doc routes with zero console
errors, including the 'representations' route's MtcarsLineStyles example
(geom_line linetype mapped to two dash levels), which mounts this exact
material in a real headless-Chromium WebGPU context.
close_reason: ChunkedLine dash rendering implemented via custom fragment material. Checkpoint finding: plot's StrokeTrait.dash is DEAD (folded into flags bag, no consumer in workbench/plot/wgsl) — so authored a minimal WGSL fragment material via @use-gpu/shader's wgsl template (same mechanism as rotated_label.tsx), plugged into RawLines' EXISTING getFragment link point (not a bespoke pipeline). Per-vertex arc length computed from positions+chunks (RenderTree/fixtures untouched), threaded as sts source; fragment reads st.x, converts to device-pixel via getWorldScale (exact for orthographic FlatCamera), discards gap fragments. Material scoped via Live.provide(MaterialContext) to dashed LineLayer only — solid lines byte-identical. Live/emit parity: CHUNKED_LINE_SOURCE mirrored + imports, emitted module deno-checks standalone. Full check clean, 315 core (10 new), fixtures --check clean, test:visual 15/15 (MtcarsLineStyles mounts dash material in real WebGPU, compiles/links clean). Caveat: headless env can't prove per-pixel dash placement, only clean mount/link. Verified by orchestrator.

title: Perf and conformance gate for the flat pipeline
description:
STAGE 6 of epic gggplot-tzc — final gate and closure. Blocked by tzc.5 AND tzc.6 AND tzc.7. Complete and final (third-pass: source-boundary tagging is the REQUIRED attribution mechanism for buffer creation; payload matching is optional write-side corroboration only — createBuffer receives a descriptor, not data, so payload matching cannot attribute it).

1. BENCH (packages/core/bench/, deno bench like reductions_bench.ts) for point, grouped line, stacked bar at 10k/100k/1M rows, in SEPARATE stages: (a) packing, (b) coordinate transform/munch (polar variant), (c) RenderTree construction, (d) emission. Bound the 1M case with fixed warmup and a hard per-case time budget (document the numbers).
2. GPU MARK-DATA UPLOAD INSTRUMENTATION — attribution mechanism (REQUIRED form): instrument at the SOURCE BOUNDARY where the live backend turns FlatTensor/MarkTopology arrays into Use.GPU sources (the ChunkedLine/ChunkedFace/Point realizations and any raw-source creation they call). Under a dev-only ?instrument flag, that boundary records each (tensor.array -> created source/buffer) association; counters then attribute subsequent buffer creations and writes to MARK DATA via those tracked identities. ArrayBuffer payload matching on writeBuffer MAY corroborate write attribution but is NOT the mechanism of record. Find Use.GPU's raw-source creation/update entry points once and document them in notes. Assertions via the visual-smoke harness or a dedicated instrumented route: (i) N re-renders, unchanged spec -> zero NEW mark-data source/buffer creations and zero mark-data writes; (ii) linear-scale x-domain change (tzc.7) -> same zeros while the frame redraws (uniform/guide writes permitted and uncounted).
3. NODE-BUDGET TEST (packages/core/tests/): fixture spec set; one mark node per renderer-compatible style batch per layer; enumerated exceptions ONLY: per-shape Point splits, per-dash ChunkedLine splits, plus any exception a converted geom documented inline with a bead reference. Anything else fails.
4. NESTED-ARRAY TRIPWIRE: walk every fixture RenderTree; no mark node carries array-of-arrays positions; no node carries an owners key; exemptions (guides/annotations if still nested) enumerated explicitly with a TODO bead reference.
5. Record bench + instrumentation results in docs/PERF_BASELINE.md (date + hardware); update docs/RESIDENCY_MATRIX.md.
6. EPIC CLOSURE: verify every epic acceptance bullet point-by-point in gggplot-tzc notes, then close the epic.
acceptance_criteria: Staged bench recorded with bounded 1M case; source-boundary-tagged instrumentation shows zero mark-data creations/writes on re-render AND on linear-domain change (uniform writes permitted); node-budget + tripwire tests in the default test run; PERF_BASELINE.md committed; epic closed with point-by-point verification.
notes:
USE.GPU RAW-SOURCE ENTRY POINTS (spiked once, per the bead's instruction) — full writeup + real numbers in docs/PERF_BASELINE.md; this note is the permanent record.

CREATE/UPLOAD PRIMITIVES (ultimate patch targets, node_modules/.deno/@use-gpu+core@0.19.0/node_modules/@use-gpu/core/mjs/buffer.mjs):
  - makeDataBuffer(device, data, flags) -> makeTypedBuffer -> device.createBuffer({size, usage, mappedAtCreation}). Descriptor only — NO payload — this is why source-boundary tagging (not payload matching) is the required create-attribution mechanism.
  - uploadBuffer(device, buffer, arrayBufferLike) -> device.queue.writeBuffer(buffer, 0, data, 0, data.byteLength).

MARK-DATA SOURCE BOUNDARY (what render/chunked_line.tsx and render/chunked_face.tsx call directly, node_modules/.deno/@use-gpu+workbench@0.19.0/node_modules/@use-gpu/workbench/mjs/hooks/useRawSource.mjs):
  - useRawSource(array, format, options, size, version) / useRawTensorSource(tensorArray, options): (a) useMemo-creates a GPUBuffer via makeDataBuffer, keyed on [device, byteLength-rounded alloc, flags] — NOT tensor identity, so a same-byte-size re-pack REUSES the buffer object; (b) useMemo-calls uploadBuffer, keyed on [device, format, source, array, buffer, version, ...size] — array IDENTITY is a dependency, so an unchanged tensor.array reference across re-renders skips this useMemo entirely (zero re-upload by construction — exactly what PackCache's tzc.5 reference-identity guarantee is FOR).
  - gpu_instrument.ts's withMarkAttribution brackets exactly these two useRawTensorSource calls (positions/colors/widths in chunked_line.tsx; positions/colors in chunked_face.tsx) plus the topology/segments sources (useLineSegmentsSource, useFaceSegmentsSource, useFaceSegmentsConcaveSource) — any createBuffer/writeBuffer triggered synchronously inside the bracket is counted as mark data.

POINT IS A DIFFERENT, NOT-FULLY-BRACKETABLE PATH: Point does NOT go through useRawTensorSource — REGISTRY maps 'Point' straight to @use-gpu/plot's own <Point> (node_modules/.deno/@use-gpu+plot@0.19.0/node_modules/@use-gpu/plot/mjs/shape/point.mjs: useTraits -> schemaToAttributes/schemaToArchetype from @use-gpu/core -> a LayerReconciler quote(yeet(shapes)) deferred batch). That batch's own raw-source/buffer allocation happens deep inside @use-gpu/plot's internal shape-reconciler pipeline, which is NOT synchronously reachable from our REGISTRY wrapping point the way ChunkedLine/ChunkedFace's own hook bodies are — createElement doesn't execute a component's body immediately, and Point's actual buffer work happens later when Live's fiber runtime processes the batch, on a call stack we don't control. CONSEQUENCE: Point's CREATE-side attribution is NOT implemented (a real, documented gap, not silently glossed over) — render/GGPlot.tsx's registerPointMarkArrays instead registers each Point node's FlatTensor array as a "known mark array" synchronously at RenderTree-to-Live-element construction time (which we DO control), giving WRITE-side-only corroboration (device.queue.writeBuffer's payload ArrayBuffer identity match) as a narrower fallback — never used for create attribution, per the bead's own rule that createBuffer's descriptor-only signature makes payload corroboration structurally impossible for creates. Follow-up if Point-specific create attribution is ever needed: spike @use-gpu/plot's shape-reconciler/LayerReconciler internals (traits.mjs, workbench's LayerReconciler) to find its OWN raw-source allocation call site and bracket THAT directly instead.

INSTRUMENTATION RESULTS — split by what ran where (full detail in docs/PERF_BASELINE.md):
  (a) Deno-level identity-proxy unit tests (packages/core/tests/gpu_instrument_test.ts, 9 tests) — RAN, all passing. Exercises the counting/bracket/corroboration logic against a fake GPUDevice (no real WebGPU in deno).
  (b) Real in-browser run (apps/site/scripts/gpu_instrument_check.ts driving apps/site/src/InstrumentProbe.tsx at /?instrument, via headless Chromium + --enable-unsafe-webgpu, the SAME environment apps/site's existing test:visual already proves has working headless WebGPU) — RAN, both acceptance scenarios PASS: (i) 5 re-renders of an unchanged spec -> {markBufferCreations:0, markBufferWrites:0, totalBufferCreations:5, totalBufferWrites:85}; (ii) one linear x-domain change (tzc.7) -> {markBufferCreations:0, markBufferWrites:0, totalBufferCreations:2, totalBufferWrites:18} — nonzero totals confirm the frame genuinely redraws (uniform/view writes happen and are correctly uncounted), zero mark numbers confirm no mark-data re-upload.
  Debugging footnote: the FIRST attempt at (b) showed 5 spurious mark writes on scenario (ii); root-caused to the PROBE (not the compiler) re-ingesting its raw data object on every spec rebuild, defeating PackCache's column-identity-rooted cache — fixed by pre-ingesting once, matching every other PackCache test's existing discipline. Documented as a residency-matrix gotcha for gggplot-1a6 in docs/RESIDENCY_MATRIX.md.
close_reason: Perf/conformance gate complete. Staged bench (packing/polar-transform/rendertree/emission × point/grouped-line/stacked-bar × 10k/100k/1M, 1M bounded, all 12 stages within budget). Source-boundary GPU instrumentation (gpu_instrument.ts): raw-source entry points useRawSource/useRawTensorSource→makeDataBuffer/uploadBuffer→createBuffer/writeBuffer; verified at deno level (fake device) AND real headless-Chromium WebGPU — {markBufferCreations:0, markBufferWrites:0} on both re-render and linear-domain change vs nonzero totals. 38 new conformance tests (node-budget, nested-array/owners tripwire, instrument) in default run. PERF_BASELINE.md + RESIDENCY_MATRIX.md written. Point uses write-only corroboration (delegates to plot Point — documented). Full check clean, 304 core + 5 site, fixtures --check clean, test:visual green. Honest epic verdict: 5/6 bullets pass, bullet 1 fails narrowly (boxplot whisker + label box nested → gggplot-cct). Verified by orchestrator.

title: Phase-3 starter: raw data-space positions for continuous linear scales
description:
STAGE 5b of epic gggplot-tzc. Blocked by tzc.5. This description is complete and final: THE PROOF STANDARD IS REFERENCE IDENTITY — numeric equality is NOT acceptable evidence anywhere in this bead.

GOAL: for continuous LINEAR untransformed scales, domain/limits changes become view-only — zero re-pack, zero re-upload — because packed positions are raw data values and the Cartesian view node's range does the mapping on-GPU.

WHAT:
1. AUDIT FIRST: read scale/mapping.ts scalePosition for kind='continuous' with no transform; confirm what it does (identity in data units vs expansion/clamping) and account for any non-identity in the DOMAIN passed to the view node, never in per-row packing.
2. Eligibility per axis: trained scale kind === 'continuous' && no transform (log/sqrt excluded). Eligible axes pack RAW column values; their Stage A pack keys (tzc.5) EXCLUDE the domain. Log/sqrt keep CPU pre-transform, keys INCLUDE the transform; discrete keeps CPU index mapping (strings never enter shaders). Mixed axes fine — eligibility is per-axis.
3. Verify trained domains flowing to the Cartesian range are data-unit domains (compile/mod.ts numericRange usage) so raw positions project correctly.
4. Document the CPU-residency rows (log/sqrt/discrete + reasons) in docs/RESIDENCY_MATRIX.md (create the scales section if gggplot-1a6 hasn't yet; note that).

TEST (the gate): build spec; compile with a persistent PackCache; rebuild the same logical spec via the DSL with scaleXContinuous({domain: B}); compile with the SAME cache -> every mark position tensor is === across the two compiles; only the view node's range prop differs. Also: log-scale and discrete routes visually unchanged; fixture regen reviewed (positions now raw data units for eligible axes).

tzc.8's browser instrumentation independently confirms zero mark-data writes on a linear-domain change; this bead's deno-level identity test is the fast gate.
acceptance_criteria: deno task check; suites + fixtures green after reviewed regen; the ===-across-domain-change test passes (reference identity, not numeric); log/sqrt/discrete visually unchanged; RESIDENCY_MATRIX scale rows written.
notes:
AMENDMENTS (2026-07-18 design review on epic gggplot-tzc):
1. THE PROOF STANDARD IS REFERENCE IDENTITY, not numeric equality. With tzc.5's PackCache, an eligible (continuous-linear) axis's pack key must EXCLUDE the domain, so: build spec, compile with cache; rebuild spec with scaleXContinuous({domain: B}); compile with SAME cache -> mark position tensors === across the two compiles, only the view node's range differs. This replaces the earlier 'numeric equality is acceptable' language — it is not.
2. Concretely this bead (a) removes domain-dependent terms from the pack key for eligible axes (coordinate with tzc.5's per-family key builders), (b) packs raw values for eligible axes, (c) keeps CPU pre-transform for log/sqrt/discrete with pack keys that DO include the transform, and documents those rows in RESIDENCY_MATRIX.md.
3. tzc.8's browser instrumentation then independently confirms zero writeBuffer calls on a linear-domain change; this bead's deno-level identity test is the fast gate, tzc.8's is the end-to-end gate.
close_reason: Phase-3 raw data-space positions verified. Audit: scalePosition continuous=identity Number(raw), log/sqrt domain-independent per-row transforms, only discrete reads domain; scale.expand applied once in training to trained domain which flows to view-node range (numericRange). tzc.5's scaleKeyFor already excludes domain for continuous/log/sqrt, includes for discrete — so mechanism pre-existed; this bead proves it. Gate test (assertStrictEquals, reference identity not numeric): continuous-linear domain change → mark position tensors ===, only Cartesian.range differs; negative controls (discrete level-order NOT ===, log packs log10). Full check clean, 266 core + 5 new gate tests, test:visual 15/15 green (scales/positions/coords opaque, 0 console errors), 0 fixture drift. RESIDENCY_MATRIX.md scales section created (pending gggplot-1a6). Verified by orchestrator.

title: Emit backend: FlatTensor literals and chunked Face in generated source
description:

title: Add GPU-native stat_count resident bars (categorical geom_bar)
description:
## Context

The only end-to-end GPU-resident product today is the unweighted 1D histogram (stat_bin → bar topology). The cheapest next product is **stat_count → resident bars** (ggplot's `geom_bar()` default on a discrete x): structurally identical to the histogram — a grouped integer reduction feeding the same bar topology — and the pieces mostly exist:

- CPU reference: `groupedCount1d` in `packages/reductions/src/cpu.ts` (valueIds × groupIds → counts matrix). Result type currently says `backend: "cpu"` only.
- WGSL patterns: `packages/reductions/src/wgsl.ts` + `gpu.ts` already implement atomic-add histogram kernels (1D and 2D) with clear/dispatch/readback plumbing and timing; a count kernel is the same shape minus the binning math (bin index = valueId directly).
- Resident runtime scaffolding: `packages/reductions/src/gpu/resident_histogram.ts`, `resident_domain.ts`; core runtime components `runtime/resident_bar.tsx` (bar topology from a count grid), `resident_live.tsx`, `resident_view.tsx`.
- Bar topology plan: `createHistogramBarTopologyPlan` in `packages/core/src/geom/bar_grid.ts` (post-refactor: in `geom/bar.ts`) already declares the grid→bars adapter with position identity/stack/dodge/fill.
- Factor columns carry levels structurally (`TypedDataFrame`), so valueIds for a discrete x are the factor codes — no CPU string hashing pass needed at render time.

Depends on the resident-capability generalization bead (per-geom `residentPlan` hooks + generic ResidentProduct node); building this on the old hardcoded path would double the special-casing.

## Scope

Eligibility gates for v1 (mirror histogram conservatism):
- `layer.geom === "bar"`, `layer.stat === "count"`, position ∈ identity/stack/dodge/fill
- cartesian, unfaceted, unweighted (`weight` param absent — weighted counts stay CPU per the floating-count policy in `stat/shared.ts`)
- x mapped to a **factor** column; no y/color/fill mapping; optional factor `group` mapping
- explicit or bounded y domain OR standalone autoYDomain via the bounded-summary path, same as histogram

Everything outside the gates falls back to the CPU `statCount` path silently.

## Steps

1. **reductions**: add a WGSL grouped-count kernel (or parameterize the existing histogram kernel: counts[groupId * valuesCount + valueId] atomic add). Extend `GroupedCount1DResult.backend` to `"cpu" | "webgpu"`. Add a GPU executor mirroring `groupedHistogram1d`'s structure in `gpu.ts`, and a resident variant in `src/gpu/` (follow `resident_histogram.ts`: keep counts in a storage buffer, expose bounded summaries — max stacked total — for y-domain metadata instead of full readback).
2. **conformance**: extend `packages/reductions/tests/gpu_test.ts` and `reductions_test.ts`: GPU results must exactly equal `groupedCount1d` CPU reference for: single group, multi-group, empty groups, 1 category, many categories (>256 to cross workgroup boundaries), and adversarial valueIds ordering. Add a benchmark entry in `bench/`.
3. **plan**: add `createStatCountProductPlan` (mirror `createStatBinProductPlan` in `stat/bin_plan.ts`) with declared inputs/outputs/dtype/dimensions; register id `@gggplot/core:stat_count@1`. Bar topology reuses the existing bar-grid plan with a `stat_count` dependency.
4. **core runtime**: a `ResidentCountProvider` (mirror `resident_live.tsx`) feeding `ResidentHistogramBars`/`resident_bar.tsx` — bar centers come from factor level index (band positions: level i at i, width 0.9) rather than bin centers. Categorical axis ticks come from the factor levels already on the CPU (levels are metadata, not data — no readback needed).
5. **eligibility**: implement `residentPlan` on the bar geom for the stat_count case alongside the existing stat_bin case, returning a `ResidentProductProps` with `product: "@gggplot/core:stat_count@1"`.
6. **docs/example**: add or extend a docs example demonstrating a large-N categorical bar chart with `resident: true`, and note count-bar residency in the Internals page's resident section.

## Constraints

- Deterministic: counts are u32 atomic adds — bit-exact vs CPU; assert exact equality, not tolerance.
- No CPU materialization of per-row stat output on the resident path; only bounded metadata (per-category stacked max, category count) crosses back for scales/guides.
- Keep the weighted path CPU-only; do not widen `statWeights` semantics.

## Verification

- All reductions tests incl. new GPU conformance cases; `resident_conformance_test.ts` extended with a count case.
- Visual: side-by-side CPU vs resident rendering of the same spec is pixel-identical (or within the established visual-baseline tolerance) for identity/stack/dodge/fill.
- Fallback: a spec with mapped fill or weight renders via CPU path unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: WGSL grouped-count kernel with GPU executor and resident variant lands in packages/reductions; GroupedCount1DResult supports backend webgpu; GPU counts are bit-exact vs groupedCount1d CPU reference across single/multi/empty-group and >256-category cases; @gggplot/core:stat_count@1 ProductPlan registered and consumed by the bar-grid topology; bar geom's residentPlan gates stat_count per the v1 eligibility list with silent CPU fallback outside gates; no per-row readback on the resident path (bounded metadata only); resident vs CPU rendering matches for identity/stack/dodge/fill; docs example added; all reductions and conformance tests pass.

If a commit referencing gggplot-2xp exists on refactor/geom-registry after c2622c4, it is UNVERIFIED — run the verification checklist in gggplot-wu0 before closing. If no commit, restart from this bead's spec; no partial work should be trusted uncommitted.

Verified deno task check; 34 reductions tests with actual WebGPU 513-category conformance; 210 core tests; 5 site tests; fixture check; production build; visual route-health 14/14 (one transient 3D device-loss timeout, clean rerun).

title: Move per-geom domain widening out of compile() into geom domainContribution hooks
description:
## Context

`compile()` in `packages/core/src/compile/mod.ts` hardcodes per-geom domain-widening special cases in its orchestration loop (lines ~100–148 pre-refactor):

- `widenForStackedBars(...)` called for every layer (bar stacking widens y),
- an inline silhouette-area block (`layer.geom === "area" && position === "stack" && params.offset === "silhouette"`) that recomputes per-x totals to symmetrize the y domain,
- bar/col width widening via `resolutionOf(xScale, scaledX) * 0.9` + `widenForTileAxis`,
- tile width/height widening via `widenForTileAxis` on both axes.

The bar case is then **duplicated** inside `buildPanel` for facet free-scale mode. This is geom knowledge leaked into the orchestrator — ggplot2 keeps it in each geom (setup_data / range contribution). Every new extent-bearing geom currently means editing compile() in two places.

Depends on the per-geom registry refactor (GeomDefinition in `packages/core/src/geom/types.ts`); do not start before it lands.

## Design

Add an optional hook to `GeomDefinition`:

```ts
domainContribution?(
  layer: Layer,
  mapping: Aes,
  data: DataFrame,
  ctx: {
    xScale?: TrainedScale; yScale?: TrainedScale;
    xDomain: [number, number]; yDomain: [number, number];
  },
): { x?: [number, number]; y?: [number, number] } | undefined;
```

Contract: the hook returns *replacement* domains (already merged with the incoming ctx domains, i.e. monotonically widening — a returned domain must contain the input domain). compile() loops layers generically:

```ts
for (const { layer, data, mapping } of perLayer) {
  const contrib = GEOM_REGISTRY[layer.geom].domainContribution?.(layer, mapping, data, ctx);
  if (contrib?.x) xDomain = contrib.x;
  if (contrib?.y) yDomain = contrib.y;
}
```

## Steps

1. Move the four widening behaviors into `domainContribution` on their owning geoms:
   - `bar`/`col` (bar.ts): stacked-bar y widening (`widenForStackedBars` covers geom bar/col with stack/fill positions — read its current implementation in `compile/coordinates.ts`) + x band widening (`resolutionOf * 0.9` + `widenForTileAxis`).
   - `area` (area.ts): stacked-area y widening (widenForStackedBars also handles area? verify) + the silhouette symmetric-y block moved verbatim.
   - `tile` (tile.ts): x and y widening honoring `params.width`/`params.height` overrides.
2. Keep `widenForStackedBars`/`widenForTileAxis` as helpers — either exported from `compile/coordinates.ts` as today or moved to `geom/shared.ts`; geoms import them.
3. Replace both call sites in compile(): the top-level loop over `allPerLayer` AND the per-panel loop inside `buildPanel` (free-scale mode) with the single generic loop. The per-panel loop currently only re-applies the bar cases; after this change every geom's contribution applies per panel automatically — confirm this matches current behavior for fixed scales (it should be a no-op difference) and improves free-scale correctness for tile/area (note any intentional behavior delta in the PR description).
4. Grep compile/mod.ts afterward for any remaining `layer.geom ===` comparisons; the orchestrator should have none related to domains.

## Constraints

- For `scales: "fixed"` (the default), compiled RenderTree output must be byte-identical to before for all existing fixtures/examples.
- For free scales, tile/silhouette contributions now apply per panel; if that changes any docs example rendering, document it and update visual baselines deliberately.

## Verification

- Full `deno test`; the plan/facet/pipeline tests in `packages/core/tests/` (facet_layout_test.ts, pipeline_test.ts, plan_test.ts) must pass.
- Visual smoke on apps/site, paying attention to: stacked bar chart, silhouette/streamgraph area example, tile heatmap, faceted examples with free scales if any exist.
acceptance_criteria: compile/mod.ts contains no geom-specific domain-widening branches (no layer.geom comparisons for domains, top-level or in buildPanel); bar/col, area (incl. silhouette), and tile implement domainContribution on their GeomDefinitions; contributions apply uniformly per panel including free-scale mode; fixed-scale RenderTree output is identical to before; any free-scale behavior delta is documented with updated visual baselines; full test suite and visual smoke pass.
close_reason: Verified @ 88438db: domainContribution hooks on bar/col, area (silhouette), tile; compile/mod.ts has zero geom-specific domain branches; 208 tests + 10/10 fixtures pass; no doc-example free-scale deltas

title: Generalize resident eligibility into per-geom capability declarations and a generic ResidentProduct node
description:
## Context

GPU-resident lowering is currently a single hardcoded special case:

- `packages/core/src/compile/resident.ts` → `residentHistogramProps()` is one long conjunction gating exactly one geom×stat pair (bar+bin, cartesian, unfaceted, unweighted, no y/color/fill mapping, numeric x, optional factor group, position ∈ identity/stack/dodge/fill).
- `compile()` in `compile/mod.ts` calls it by name inside the panel-layer loop, and again special-cases `standaloneResident?.autoYDomain` for the single-layer standalone view.
- The RenderTree has product-specific `ComponentName` variants: `"ResidentHistogram"` and `"ResidentHistogramView"` (`compile/rendertree.ts`), consumed by name in the live runtime.

Adding the next resident product (e.g. stat_count bars — see follow-up bead) this way means another bespoke props function, more compile() branches, and two more ComponentName variants. This issue generalizes the mechanism so new resident products are registered, not hand-wired.

Depends on the per-geom registry refactor (GeomDefinition / GEOM_REGISTRY); do not start before it lands.

## Design

1. **Per-geom capability hook.** Add to `GeomDefinition`:

```ts
residentPlan?(
  spec: GGSpec,
  layer: Layer,
  mapping: Aes,
  data: TypedDataFrame,
  opts: { standalone: boolean },   // !faceted && single layer — enables autoYDomain
): ResidentProductProps | undefined;
```

where `ResidentProductProps` is a discriminated union:

```ts
interface ResidentProductProps {
  product: string;                  // plan id, e.g. "@gggplot/core:stat_bin@1"
  props: Record<string, unknown>;   // serializable node props (today's ResidentHistogramNodeProps)
  standaloneView?: boolean;         // today's autoYDomain standalone path
}
```

2. **Generic RenderTree node.** Replace `"ResidentHistogram"` / `"ResidentHistogramView"` with a single `"ResidentProduct"` ComponentName carrying `{ product, ...props }` (and a `view: true` prop for the standalone form). The live backend resolves `product` → component through a runtime registry (a `Record<string, LiveComponent>` in `packages/core/src/runtime/`, seeded with the histogram components from `resident_view.tsx` / `resident_mark.tsx`). The existing plan/extension registry (`packages/core/src/plan/registry.ts`, live adapters) is the natural resolver if it fits without contortion — use it if the live adapter shape works, otherwise a simple runtime map is acceptable; document the choice.

3. **compile() becomes generic.** The panel-layer loop asks `GEOM_REGISTRY[layer.geom].residentPlan?.(...)` when `options.resident` is set; the standalone-view branch keys off `standaloneView` rather than histogram-specific fields.

4. Move the histogram eligibility conjunction from `compile/resident.ts` into `geom/bar.ts`'s `residentPlan` implementation (content unchanged). `compile/resident.ts` shrinks to shared types/helpers or disappears.

## Constraints

- Behavior-preserving for the existing histogram path: same eligibility decisions, same rendered output, including the autoDomain and autoYDomain flows and CPU fallback when gates fail.
- `emitSource` must keep its current behavior for resident nodes (resident is runtime-only; emission keeps portable CPU nodes — verify `emit/mod.ts` handles/never sees ResidentProduct and preserve that).
- RenderTree stays fully serializable — the `product` id is a string, never a function/component reference.

## Verification

- `packages/core/tests/resident_conformance_test.ts` and `runtime_test.ts` pass unchanged (update only component-name assertions if they reference "ResidentHistogram" literally).
- Manual/visual check in apps/site: the resident histogram example renders identically with `resident: true`, and still falls back to CPU when a gate fails (e.g. mapped fill).
- Grep: no remaining `"ResidentHistogram"` ComponentName strings outside the runtime registry seed.
acceptance_criteria: residentHistogramProps's eligibility logic lives in the bar geom's residentPlan hook; compile() requests resident lowering generically via GEOM_REGISTRY with no product-specific branches; RenderTree uses a single serializable ResidentProduct ComponentName resolved by a runtime registry (ResidentHistogram/ResidentHistogramView variants removed); histogram eligibility decisions, rendering, autoDomain/autoYDomain flows, and CPU fallback are behavior-identical; emitSource behavior for resident specs unchanged; resident conformance and runtime tests pass.
close_reason: Verified @ c2622c4: residentPlan hook on bar geom, generic ResidentProduct node + runtime/resident_registry.ts resolver; histogram behavior identical incl. autoDomain/fallback; emit/mod.ts untouched; 208 tests, 13 fixtures (3 new resident) pass; grep gate clean in source (only stale dist artifact matches)

title: Guarantee documentation examples for every public geom
description: Inventory every public geom constructor exported by packages/core/src/dsl/geoms.ts and ensure the documentation site contains a discoverable, runnable example where that geom is a primary teaching subject. Current docs directly exercise point, line, bar, histogram, col, text, smooth, tile, hline, vline, and abline; add coverage for path, area, ribbon, polygon, raster, label, boxplot, errorbar, density, violin, dotplot, bin2d, hex, qq, qqLine, contour, and contourFilled. Preserve coverage as new geom constructors land.
design: Add a data-only geom documentation coverage manifest keyed by the exact public constructor export name. Each entry names one or more DocExample ids and classifies the example as dedicated or an explicitly labeled comparison. A shared example may cover related geoms only when its title, prose, DSL source, and rendered result explicitly teach each listed geom. Every example must use the public DSL, provide dataPreview or a supported lazy dataset, include synchronized dslSource and executable spec/buildSpec, describe the intended visual result accessibly, and appear on a discoverable docs page. Prefer compact family comparisons for area/ribbon, polygon/raster/tile, interval forms, 2D binning, QQ, and contour variants, but do not count incidental background layers as coverage. Add a Deno test that enumerates geom[A-Z] exports from the data-safe DSL barrel and proves a manifest entry exists, referenced example ids exist exactly once, and no stale constructor or example ids remain. Planned geoms from gggplot-8e0.16 through .25 must add their own manifest entry and docs fixture in the same change; this bead establishes the gate and backfills currently shipped geoms.

The current uncovered constructors path, area, ribbon, polygon, raster, label, boxplot, errorbar, density, violin, dotplot, bin2d, hex, qq, qqLine, contour, and contourFilled receive examples with representative mappings and non-empty visible output. 3. Related comparison examples label every covered geom in prose and source; incidental layers do not satisfy coverage. 4. A data-safe automated test fails when a geom export lacks coverage, a manifest points to a missing/duplicate example id, or a stale entry remains. 5. Each fixture compiles through the normal DSL and passes emitted/Live route health without console warnings, empty chart surfaces, clipped labels, or invalid values. 6. Documentation navigation exposes the examples under appropriate representations or stats pages, with accessible visual summaries and mobile-safe layout. 7. deno task check, deno test -A, docs build, and the full visual smoke suite pass. 8. The contributor/docs guidance states that adding a public geom requires a coverage entry and example.

title: Unify layout and SDF font metrics
description: Replace production browser-canvas guide measurement with metrics from the same resolved UseGPU font faces used by SDF glyph rendering, and expose a readiness/glyph-completion gate consumable by plot export.
design: Provide synchronous measurement only after FontResources.ready(). Retain an explicitly approximate measurer for pure compiler tests. Export must await resources, requested glyph work, and a completed render before readback.

notes: Moved production compile/layout inside FontLoader and derive TextMeasurer from the same RustText context used by GlyphSource/SDF rendering. TextMeasurer now receives family/weight/style; guide layout forwards theme face fields. Added explicit approximateTextMeasurer for compiler-only contexts, glyph metric fixtures, and FontResources.readyForExport/glyphsReady contract. Removed browser Canvas2D production measurement. Validation: 200 tests, check/build, clean #guides browser, guides visual smoke.

title: Add deterministic host font resource registry
description: Implement ADR 001 FontResources host boundary with faces, defaultFace, and ready(); adapt the current fonts array; validate explicit family/weight/style requests after readiness; expose the same resource contract to Live and emitted components.
design: Keep resource URLs/lazy loaders outside GGSpec. Omitted family selects defaultFace; an unresolved explicit request throws with family, weight, and style. Preserve current array input via an adapter.
acceptance_criteria: GGPlot accepts FontResources and legacy arrays; readiness gates final rendering; explicit missing faces fail descriptively with no silent fallback; omitted family uses defaultFace; emitted component contract accepts host resources; tests cover success, pending, and failure.
notes: Implemented FontFaceResource/FontResources with faces, defaultFace, ready(), legacy array adapter, and exported helpers. GGPlot gates rendering on readiness and validates every explicit theme/layer/mapped family-weight-style request; missing faces throw descriptive errors while omitted family uses the host default. Emitted components accept fontResources and await readiness without embedding URLs. Site migrated to the resource object. Validation: 199 tests, check/build, clean #themes browser, visual smoke.
close_reason: Deterministic host font registry, readiness gate, validation, and emitted contract implemented.

title: Add semantic text face fields and batching
description: Implement ADR 001 semantic typography: theme fontWeight/fontStyle/lineHeight; geom_text literal family/fontface/lineheight; ggplot-style fontface normalization; mapped discrete family/fontface batching without automatic legends; consistent precedence across mapped, layer, theme, and host defaults.
design: Use one normalized TextStyle representation through compile and render. Split text batches by resolved semantic face when family or fontface is mapped. Preserve existing family/font-size behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Theme and text layer fields compile to normalized family/weight/style/lineHeight; plain/bold/italic/bold.italic normalize deterministically; mapped face values produce correctly separated Label nodes; precedence is tested; emitted source preserves semantic styles; gallery demonstrates at least two redistributable faces.
notes: Implemented Theme fontWeight/fontStyle/lineHeight; text family/fontface aesthetics; literal fontface/lineheight normalization; mapped face batching with mapped > literal > theme precedence; semantic weight/style/lineHeight propagation to guide/title/facet labels; emitted output preservation. Gallery now maps Basic/Lato families using official OFL resources. Validation: 196 tests pass, check/build pass, #themes browser has no errors, themes visual smoke passes.
close_reason: Semantic text styling and mapped face batching implemented and validated.

title: Implement pixel-sized PNG plot export MVP
description: Implement the smallest supported export API after the deterministic WebGPU export spike proves the path. Accept an explicit GGSpec, integer output width/height in pixels, and background; render on a dedicated target; return one documented browser result type; and clean up GPU/canvas resources. Do not include physical units, DPI, scale aliases, vector formats, implicit last-plot state, or download UI.
design: Use CSS layout pixels equal to output pixels for MVP, making DPR irrelevant inside export. Return Blob unless the spike demonstrates a stronger cross-runtime contract. Add byte conversion as a separately named helper only when required.
acceptance_criteria: Public async API exports PNG for an explicit GGSpec at exact requested pixel dimensions; background/alpha behavior is deterministic; live chart dimensions/state are unchanged; fonts/resources are awaited according to the chosen host contract; unsupported WebGPU, device loss, invalid/oversized dimensions, and cleanup are tested or produce actionable errors; docs show Blob/URL usage using the single chosen return contract.
notes: Implemented public ggsave(spec,{width,height,backgroundColor,fontResources,signal}): Promise<Blob>. It preflights browser/WebGPU/adapter limits, awaits readyForExport, mounts a dedicated low-level Canvas at pixelRatio=1, captures through Workbench GPU readback after a rendered frame, validates PNG type/IHDR dimensions, and always unmounts/removes the temporary host. Added actionable timeout/device-loss, abort, invalid/oversized, encoder/size errors; transparent default and explicit background. docs/EXPORTING.md covers Blob/URL use. Unit validation plus production Chromium probe confirms image/png 320x200, signature, no live-canvas mutation, and no leaked host. Full 14-route visual/export smoke, 202 tests, check/build pass.
close_reason: Exact-pixel dedicated-canvas PNG Blob export implemented and validated in production Chromium.

title: Remove proprietary and misregistered fonts from the gallery
description:
## Problem
The site registers both sans-serif and Georgia against apps/site/public/fonts/SFNS.ttf, an untracked proprietary Apple font. This is non-portable and maps Georgia to unrelated bytes.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start the gallery from a fresh checkout without the untracked apps/site/public/fonts directory.
2. Open any example with axes/text and inspect font network/loading and renderer diagnostics.
3. Compare the registrations in apps/site/src/scene.tsx: both declared families resolve to /fonts/SFNS.ttf.
4. Verify that the repository has no redistributable source/license for that file.

## Scope
Replace this with a redistributable demo-font strategy or a documented deterministic fallback, independently of the larger typography ADR.
design: Prefer a permissively licensed bundled face if UseGPU requires an explicit source; otherwise use a deterministic host-provided fallback supported by the font loader. Keep this fix independent from adding new semantic typography fields.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh checkout renders all gallery text without apps/site/public/fonts/SFNS.ttf; Georgia is not mapped to unrelated font bytes; no proprietary font is committed or required; missing demo font behavior is deterministic and visible in tests or browser smoke coverage; repository docs state any bundled font license/source.
notes: Replaced both incorrect SFNS registrations with one self-hosted Basic-Regular.ttf from google/fonts/ofl/basic and copied its SIL OFL 1.1 license. Site theme/examples now request family Basic; README records source/license. No tracked code references SFNS or fake Georgia mapping. Site tests/check/build and start-route visual smoke pass. The user's untracked SFNS.ttf scratch file was not deleted or committed.
close_reason: Gallery now uses a licensed self-hosted Basic font with provenance and no proprietary or misregistered font dependency.

title: Specify complete facet panel layout semantics
description: After the blank-facet Live regression is repaired, define and implement the broader facet layout contract independently: strip placement/sizing, fixed-scale exterior-axis policy, free/free_x/free_y per-panel axes, empty grid combinations, clipping, panel spacing, coord_flip/coord_fixed interaction, shared legends, and responsive resizing. Existing compiler tests already cover free-scale domains; this bead focuses on visible layout semantics rather than retraining logic.
design: Start from an explicit panel layout model in CSS pixels that assigns panel, strip, and axis rectangles. Preserve one top-level canvas. Allow Live and emitted backends to use different rendering mechanics while testing equivalent semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A documented matrix states axis/strip behavior for wrap/grid and fixed/free scale modes; every mode has a visible gallery or browser fixture; empty combinations, shared legends, coord_flip/fixed, and resizing are covered; panel/strip/axis rectangles do not overlap at documented minimum sizes; Live and emitted output are semantically equivalent.
close_reason: Documented the wrap/grid fixed/free axis and strip matrix; implemented responsive CSS-pixel facet cell/strip/panel rectangles with configurable spacing and strip height in Live and emitted backends; added free/free_x/free_y plus coord_flip/fixed gallery fixtures, empty-grid/shared-legend coverage, and layout tests. Full 205-test, check, build, parity, and 14-route visual gates pass.

title: Audit module boundaries and propose a staged reorganization
description: File size suggests investigation, not proof of poor organization. Produce an objective module/dependency audit for compile, stats, DSL, scales, render interpretation, emitted source, tests, and public barrels. Identify high-coupling responsibilities, duplicated semantic models, circular-import risk, and extractions that can be mechanical versus those blocked on unsettled layout behavior. Do not perform the large refactor in this bead.
design: Define allowed dependency directions and stable public barrel exports. Treat emitted-source inlining as a distinct backend constraint: require semantic equivalence or generated templates, not literal helper reuse. Recommend staged implementation beads by subsystem.
acceptance_criteria: A module map records current and proposed dependency directions; coupling evidence supports each proposed split; public API compatibility constraints and circular-import checks are explicit; independent stat/DSL/scale extractions are separated from layout-dependent work; focused implementation beads are filed with validation and migration order.
close_reason: Recorded objective module/dependency map, stable barrel and backend constraints, circular-import rule, and staged migrations. Filed gggplot-zsu/c0g/4x4 then layout-dependent gggplot-k5m.

title: Research 3D grammar and plugin extension boundaries
description: Architecture spike, not an implementation feature. Establish principles for when a z aesthetic meaningfully extends an existing 2D geom, when a distinct 3D primitive is required, and whether optional 3D support should use statically imported plugin packages. Separately analyze the serialization conflict between function-based typed registrations and string identifiers requiring registry/version contracts.
design: Produce two decisions within one bounded research deliverable: a 3D semantic compatibility matrix/principles, and an extension-interface ADR. Do not promise dynamic discovery, untrusted-code security, lighting, picking, every renderer feature, or implementation. If static packages are chosen, limit security discussion accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: A finite matrix classifies current geom families as meaningful z-extension, distinct 3D primitive, or not meaningful; ADR chooses core-vs-plugin ownership and identifier/serialization/versioning approach; one point-cloud vertical slice is specified with typed IR/RenderTree examples; separate dependency-ordered beads are filed for extension API implementation and any @gggplot/3d implementation epic.
close_reason: Accepted ADR 002: finite geom-family 3D matrix, static versioned package registry, serialization/version rules, and point-cloud IR/RenderTree slice. Filed dependency-ordered gggplot-9gj then gggplot-74p.

title: Verify closed geom/stat coverage claims against ggplot2 and Gribouille
description: Verify rather than restart the previously closed coverage program. Re-audit current public constructors, IR, compile paths, Live runtime, emitted backend, tests, and gallery against ggplot2 4.0.3 and an exact Gribouille release/commit recorded at audit time. Reconcile every gap with closed epic gggplot-aei or a focused non-duplicate bead.
design: Use status vocabulary: absent, alias, constructor-only, compile-only, runtime-only, partial-stat, full. Track implementation parity separately from documentation/gallery parity. Use official upstream sources and record a reproducible extraction/query method where practical.
acceptance_criteria: Version-stamped matrix covers every gggplot geom/stat and every upstream counterpart; uses the finite status vocabulary; separately records DSL/IR/compiler/Live/emitted/test/gallery support; stale counts in coverage docs are replaced; each gap cross-links to gggplot-aei or one new focused bead with no duplicates; the extraction method is documented.
close_reason: Replaced stale counts with a ggplot2 4.0.3 and pinned Gribouille audit; generated 129-source matrix now separates DSL/IR/compiler/Live/emitted/gallery evidence, uses the finite status vocabulary, and links gaps to the standalone gggplot-isp follow-up epic.

title: Spike deterministic WebGPU plot export
description: Time-boxed technical spike for a browser-first plot export path. Determine whether a dedicated/offscreen canvas can host the existing UseGPU scene, await GPU completion and fonts, read back/encode PNG, release resources, and run in available CI/browser infrastructure. Explicitly test unsupported WebGPU, device loss, maximum texture dimensions, cross-origin font/image constraints, and whether export can remain independent of the live canvas.
design: Use an explicit GGSpec and dedicated render target; no implicit last plot. For the spike choose CSS layout pixels and output pixels explicitly and avoid physical units, DPI, scale, vector formats, or download UI.
acceptance_criteria: A minimal proof or documented blocker produces a PNG from an explicit GGSpec at an exact requested pixel size; records the chosen browser APIs and cleanup lifecycle; documents CI/headless feasibility, WebGPU/device-loss/texture-limit behavior, and external-resource constraints; files an MVP implementation bead with one return type and a separate physical-units compatibility bead.
notes: Spike decision recorded in docs/WEBGPU_EXPORT_SPIKE.md. Chosen path: dedicated HTMLCanvasElement + React/Live root + low-level UseGPU Canvas(width,height,pixelRatio=1) + explicit GGSpec/GGPlot + Workbench Screenshot GPU readback to PNG Blob. Document covers cleanup, font/glyph readiness, unsupported WebGPU, device loss, maxTextureDimension2D, CORS/origin constraints, exact integer pixels, and Chromium CI. Existing children .10 (MVP) and .11 (physical units) match the resulting dependency split.
close_reason: Browser export path and finite API/lifecycle/failure decisions established; MVP and physical-unit children already filed.

title: Decide typography semantics and host font-resource API
description: The current API already separates semantic theme.fontFamily from the renderer host's GGPlot fonts registry, but the complete contract is undecided. Produce an ADR covering: theme and geom_text/label family, weight, style/fontface semantics; whether any typography fields are mappable per row; host font registration/loading/fallback; metric consistency between layout measurement and UseGPU SDF rendering; emitted-source responsibilities; and how export waits for resources. Do not presume font URLs belong in serializable GGSpec.
design: Prefer semantic typography in GGSpec and renderer resources in host configuration unless a resolver-based serializable reference is justified. Explicitly resolve identifier-vs-resource ownership, font readiness, multiple faces, and whether missing faces fail fast or use one deterministic fallback.
acceptance_criteria: ADR chooses the public semantic fields and host resource interface; chooses exactly one missing-font behavior; states serialization and emitted-source rules; specifies metric/readiness hooks needed by layout/export; files separate implementation beads for semantic text styling, host loading, and measurement consistency; no proprietary font is required by the proposed examples/tests.
notes: Accepted docs/ADR_001_TYPOGRAPHY_AND_FONT_RESOURCES.md. Decisions: canonical family/weight/style/size/color/angle/lineHeight semantics; mapped family/fontface are discrete batch-splitting aesthetics without default legends; host owns FontResources and URLs; explicit unresolved faces fail after readiness while omitted family uses defaultFace; production layout and SDF rendering share glyph metrics; emitted source receives resources from host. Filed implementation children gggplot-8e0.13, .14, and .15.
close_reason: ADR accepted and three dependency-ordered implementation beads filed.

title: Harden plot layout, export, coverage, and extensibility
description: Tracking container for two distinct workstreams discovered in the July 2026 audit: (1) concrete rendering/layout correctness and export work, and (2) roadmap/architecture research covering parity, extension boundaries, and module organization. This umbrella does not assert that every child shares one implementation contract; each child must establish its own evidence and boundary.
design: Preserve P1 only on independently reproducible user-facing regressions. Research children produce finite decisions or inventories; implementation children produce working code and tests. Children may be closed, superseded, or explicitly deferred with a recorded reason rather than forcing speculative work into the same release.
acceptance_criteria: Every child is closed, superseded, or deferred with a documented reason; reproducible P1 regressions are repaired; research children leave finite decisions and dependency-ordered implementation beads; implementation children pass their stated validation.
close_reason: All 15 hardening children are resolved: rendering regressions, typography/font resources, legends, PNG export, parity audit, 3D/plugin ADR, module audit, and facet semantics. Follow-up implementation work is dependency-ordered outside this epic.

title: Move statistical examples to richer real datasets
description: Several examples still use tiny synthetic arrays that hide grouping, smoothing, density, and histogram behavior. Use the included mpg/iris/mtcars assets (and add the intended newly included dataset to the typed loader if present) for higher-cardinality examples, especially smoothing and statistical transformations.
acceptance_criteria: Key smoothing, histogram, grouping, and statistical examples use documented real typed datasets with enough observations to make the behavior visually meaningful, while retaining small fixtures only where they clarify semantics.

title: Move statistical examples to richer real datasets
description: Several examples still use tiny synthetic arrays that hide grouping, smoothing, density, and histogram behavior. Use the included mpg/iris/mtcars assets (and add the intended newly included dataset to the typed loader if present) for higher-cardinality examples, especially smoothing and statistical transformations.
acceptance_criteria: Key smoothing, histogram, grouping, and statistical examples use documented real typed datasets with enough observations to make the behavior visually meaningful, while retaining small fixtures only where they clarify semantics.
close_reason: Histogram, grouped histogram, and grouped smooth examples now use 234-row mpg and 150-row iris typed datasets with dense fit/bin settings.

title: Audit palettes legends and empty layout regions
description: Gallery screenshots show low-contrast or surprising fills, white/gradient bar artifacts, legends compressed into the plot edge, overlapping legend text, and fixed empty regions. Review categorical/continuous defaults, alpha compositing, legend placement/measurement, and reclaimable layout space against Gribouille and ggplot2.
acceptance_criteria: Representative bar, point, fill, colorbar, and legend examples have coherent accessible colors, no overlap/clipping, and no reserved empty bands when components are absent.
close_reason: Measured guide margin reserves legend space; discrete and continuous swatches render as independent solid faces with accessible site colors and no plot overlap.

title: Preserve effective groups in QQ and ellipse stats
description: The initial long-tail implementation pools all rows for stat_qq/stat_qq_line/stat_ellipse. Split by the effective-group resolver, preserve grouping columns in emitted products, and add multi-group pipeline coverage.
close_reason: QQ and ellipse stats now preserve effective groups; full 190-test suite passes

title: Add continuous and binned color guides
description: Implement guide_colourbar, guide_coloursteps, and guide_bins render-tree lowering for continuous and binned color/fill scales, including labels, serializable gradients/steps, and pipeline tests.
close_reason: Implemented all scoped grammar coverage and verified 189 tests plus entrypoint type checks

title: Publish canonical visual docs and a durable parity test suite
description: After the recovery foundations are green, rewrite the feature-tour examples into a curated, executable visual gallery whose examples are clear enough to serve as parity comparisons.
design: Each capability page should state data source, DSL, semantic output, residency boundary, and intentional visual result. Promote a small canonical subset per capability; preserve source links for the rest of the matrix. Add cross-layer, facets, guides, theme, coordinate, and real-data test fixtures plus accessibility-friendly chart alt text.
acceptance_criteria: The site navigates as a coherent reference; every claimed supported capability has a runnable example and visual test; documentation makes unsupported/deferred features obvious; production build passes the visual suite.
close_reason: Published canonical reference updates and durable parity/visual coverage: all runnable docs charts expose accessible visual summaries; the 14-route smoke suite passes buffer/layout/a11y/screenshot/console checks; the pinned 129-source parity matrix is generated and current; full tests and checks pass.

title: Add GPU-native point stroke aesthetic
description: Add the stroke aesthetic (point border width) only through an outline-capable mark contract. use.gpu's current Point primitive exposes size/colors but no border-width or border-color input, so this cannot truthfully be lowered as a native Point property. Define either a compositional outer/inner point representation or a compatible upstream use.gpu mark extension; preserve CPU fallback semantics while the native path is unavailable.
design: The public IR uses stroke as a semantic continuous aesthetic. The renderer adapter selects an outline-capable GPU representation that accepts GPU-native widths (or composes resident outer and inner point sources without row-shaped readback). Do not synthesize a CPU-expanded border merely to claim GPU support. Declare stroke color precedence, clipping, size/stroke validity, and hit-testing behavior before implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Mapped and literal stroke produce visible point borders with documented color/size precedence. A GPU path consumes resident width data directly and is verified against the use.gpu mark contract; otherwise the compiler selects an explicit CPU fallback. Pipeline tests cover literal, mapped, and unsupported backend selection.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the full 185-test suite

title: Add density and violin product family
description: Implement stat_density/stat_ydensity and geom_violin from raw grouped data, with CPU-reference density semantics and mirrored violin geometry.
design: Declare a dense [group, sample] density grid and topology product before a GPU executor. A resident implementation must consume typed source handles, emit a direct mark geometry/source, and request only bounded metadata for scales; otherwise it remains a named CPU fallback with equivalent semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Grouped density and mirrored violin geometry are correct against CPU fixtures, including missing values and empty groups. The product schema, normalization, sample grid, and scale metadata are documented. Any GPU path uses resident dense products without row readback; otherwise fallback selection is tested.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the full 185-test suite

title: Add raw-y stat_boxplot product
description: Implement stat_boxplot from raw y grouped by the effective-group resolver, while retaining pre-aggregated geom_boxplot input. Define a compact per-group summary product with x/group, quartiles, whiskers, and outlier policy; establish CPU-reference semantics first.
design: The CPU product is the semantic oracle. A future GPU executor may expose a compact summary buffer only after deterministic quantile policy, product shape, bounded metadata, and a direct boxplot mark consumer are specified. Do not materialize row-shaped summaries in a live GPU mark.
acceptance_criteria: geom_boxplot(aes(x,y)) computes correct group-aware quartiles and whiskers from raw y; pre-aggregated input remains supported; missing/outlier/group policy is documented and pipeline tests cover it. GPU execution is either proven under the declared compact product contract or explicitly CPU fallback.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the full 185-test suite

title: Extend resident grid marks with tile, fill, and dodge semantics
description: Add the next consumers of resident count grids: tile/grid rendering and explicitly specified position_fill and position_dodge topology/compute paths. Do not expose a position mode until its GPU semantics, shape contract, and CPU conformance are implemented.
acceptance_criteria: Tile/grid and each enabled position mode consume GPU-native products without count-row readback; contracts declare output shape/topology and conformance fixtures cover grouping, empty cells, and normalization/placement semantics.
notes: Completed the resident grid-mark extension. The histogram executor now emits a dense GPU tile-vertex product alongside bar vertices; zero [group,bin] cells retain tile topology and counts never read back. Added ResidentHistogramTiles as the mounted Face consumer. The packed GPU layout contract now selects identity, stack, dodge, or fill in the vertex pass; dodge partitions bin width, fill performs zero-safe per-bin normalization, and position-aware summaries provide y bounds. Compiler accepts only these declared modes; plan, compiler, runtime, and hardware fixtures cover grouping, empty cells, tile topology, placement, normalization, and GPU-native products.
close_reason: Tile-grid and all declared resident position modes are implemented and verified without count-row readback.

title: Add streaming GPU SourceAdapter
description: Implement the separate streaming/subrange upload adapter with persistent buffers, range writes, logical length/content version, capacity policy, and device-loss rehydration; do not misuse useRawSource for subviews.
acceptance_criteria: Append/subrange updates write only modified ranges; capacity and logical length are explicit; static RawData/useRawSource and streaming paths share resolved field contracts; tests verify no whole-buffer upload assumption.
notes: Implemented GPUStreamingSourceAdapter as a deliberately separate mutable-storage path from RawData/useRawSource. It validates the same FieldSpec dtype contract as mounted fields; exposes logical length, capacity, version, and storage source shape; accepts explicit update ranges; writes only the changed subrange while capacity is sufficient; doubles capacity and uploads the logical snapshot on growth; and retains a CPU snapshot to rehydrate after device loss. Runtime fixture verifies offsets/byte counts for subrange, append, growth, and rehydration.
close_reason: Streaming range-write contract, capacity policy, rehydration, and coverage are complete.

title: Specify and implement weighted count/bin execution policy
description: Add correct weighted stat_count/stat_bin semantics: retain unweighted n:u32 atomic mode, define fractional count:f32 output, and use either a deterministic GPU reduction or explicit CPU fallback until portable floating accumulation is available.
acceptance_criteria: Weighted and unweighted modes have distinct schemas and documented selection; no weight is silently quantized; CPU/GPU/unsupported fallback behavior is observable and tested at bin boundaries and across groups/panels.
notes: Implemented the weighted execution policy. The weight parameter accepts a numeric column name or finite scalar in stat-bearing geom parameters; weighted stat_count and stat_bin accumulate Float64 CPU counts, retain fractional values, omit non-finite weights, and preserve group/bin boundaries and density totals. Resident eligibility rejects every weighted layer, so the RenderTree visibly uses the existing CPU stat/Polygon path instead of coercing weights into the u32 GPU kernel. Documented the selection contract and added conformance tests.
close_reason: Weighted semantics are correct and the unsupported GPU path is explicit, documented, and tested.

title: Show computed stat rows in docs examples
description: Extend the feature-tour docs examples with an optional computed-data preview for stat examples. For stat_count/stat_bin/stat_summary/stat_smooth pages, show raw input rows beside post-stat rows so readers can see how data is manipulated before geoms render.
acceptance_criteria: Stats docs show raw data and computed stat rows for count, bin, summary, and smooth examples; implementation reuses core applyStat/compile helpers rather than duplicating reducer logic; browser/build/tests pass.
close_reason: Docs stat examples now show computed stat rows from the real applyStat pipeline for count, bin, summary, and smooth; validated with core check, full tests, Vite build, and browser smoke test.

title: Add a site typecheck task for React app shell
description: The site content modules and Vite config type-check, and Vite build catches the React app shell, but direct deno check on App.tsx currently fails because React JSX runtime/types are not resolved cleanly. Add a reliable site check task or config fix so future docs changes can validate the app shell directly.
acceptance_criteria: apps/site exposes a check task that validates the docs app shell and content modules without JSX intrinsic/runtime errors; root validation can call it or document it; existing build/tests still pass.
close_reason: Added apps/site check task with React JSX runtime/types configured, wired root deno task check to include it, and validated with deno task check, deno test -A, and deno task build.

title: Add visual QA and responsive polish for feature-tour docs
description: Run browser-based visual QA across desktop and mobile widths for the new feature-tour docs shell, then fix layout issues such as nav behavior, overflowing code/data tables, canvas sizing, and long labels.
acceptance_criteria: Feature-tour docs are verified at desktop and mobile widths; navigation remains usable; tables/code/canvas panels do not overlap or overflow incoherently; screenshots or notes are attached in the bead; build/tests pass.
notes: QA notes 2026-07-16: Browser-checked feature-tour pages at 1280x900 and 390x844. Before fix, stats mobile had document-level horizontal overflow (scrollWidth 1004 vs viewport 390) because the side nav stayed beside content. After fix, all checked pages (start/stats/aesthetics/data/scales/positions/facets/coords/annotations/themes/internals) report no document-level horizontal overflow at mobile or desktop; mobile stats scrollWidth 375 vs viewport 390. Mobile nav is an intentional horizontal scroller with hidden scrollbar; tables stay contained; chart canvases stay contained (mobile about 317x240). Code blocks with long DSL lines scroll internally only. Visual screenshots inspected for mobile stats and desktop coords.

Cover stats, geoms/representations, aesthetics, scales, facets, coords, themes, annotations, data typing, and reductions internals with a practical page/example matrix for contributors.

description: Evolve apps/site from a single examples array into a multipage docs/reference site with sections for examples, reference, stats, data, internals, and FAQ. Keep the existing DSL/source/render panels but make contribution units page modules plus dataset modules.

Keep page modules declarative; GPU examples may expose bounded benchmark reports rather than materialized data.

title: Design typed DataFrame ingestion and low-level buffer lowering boundary
description: The current DataFrame is Record<string, unknown[]>; scale typing relies on first-value string sniffing and stats perform scattered Number() coercions. Design and prototype a typed column model with an ingest(raw) boundary that accepts column-store and row-store input, infers numeric vs factor columns, supports explicit asFactor()/asNumeric() overrides, and keeps ggplot({ x: [...], y: [...] }) working by inference. This should clarify where stats/scales/grouping operate over typed tabular data and where rendering lowers to UseGPU-native typed buffers/TensorArray-like props. The immediate motivation is gggplot-48e's implicit grouping bug: effective grouping should be explicit group=, else the interaction of mapped factor/discrete aesthetics; numeric-coded categories must be representable via asFactor(). UseGPU has TensorArray/storage/compute primitives and contour/grid helpers, but no built-in group-by/count/bin/summary stat primitive, so this issue should preserve a CPU-side stat pipeline while documenting a future path for optional GPU kernels when row counts justify it.
acceptance_criteria: A short design note or architecture-doc update defines Column/DataFrame/InputData types, ingest() behavior for row-store and column-store data, asFactor()/asNumeric() override API, factor level ordering, NA/null handling, and the lowering boundary to RenderTree/UseGPU props. Prototype or follow-up beads identify the minimal mechanical code changes required in ir/types.ts, dsl/mod.ts, stat/mod.ts, scale/mod.ts, compile/mod.ts, and tests.
close_reason: Added typed ingestion prototype with row/column-store support, asFactor/asNumeric overrides, factor levels, missing-value handling, legacy materialization, buffer lowering helpers, tests, and docs/TYPED_DATAFRAME_INGESTION.md. Filed gggplot-e76 for full mechanical pipeline migration.

title: Expand color/fill scale palette families (gradient2, gradientn, viridis, brewer, binned steps)

This is purely a palette/parameter-surface expansion on top of the existing scale/mod.ts continuous-color-training machinery (scaleColorValue already interpolates a domain into a ramp) -- doesn't need new architecture, just more configurable range functions plus a couple of built-in palette tables.
design: Palette selection must compose as lazy semantic scale data: constants/uniforms for small ramps and typed GPU LUT sources for larger or stepped palettes. A palette change should invalidate only scale/mark bindings, not stat products or source uploads. CPU output remains the reference fallback and palette tables must stay serializable.

At least viridis and a diverging gradient2 are implemented with tests; brewer/gradientn can follow if time allows.

Each child begins with CPU-reference semantics and may add a resident GPU executor only after its typed product, lazy source handles, bounded summaries, and direct mark consumer are declared.
design: Define versioned product schemas before implementation: boxplot summaries are compact per-group products; density/violin and dotplot outputs are dense grids/topologies that can remain GPU-resident. Begin with CPU-reference conformance, then add a GPU executor only when its source handles, shape, bounded metadata, and direct mark consumer are specified. No implicit row readback.

title: Add GPU-native linetype and linewidth aesthetics and scales
description: docs/COVERAGE_BACKLOG.md section 1/5. gggplot has no linetype (dashed/dotted) or linewidth (ggplot2's line-width aesthetic). This focused addition introduces AesName entries, a discrete linetype scale mapping levels to dash patterns, and a continuous linewidth scale reusing existing auxiliary-scale interpolation. It unlocks dashed reference lines (geom_hline/vline/abline) and multi-series line charts distinguished by dash pattern without CPU row expansion.
design: Treat line style fields as semantic visual inputs. Lower linetype as a per-effective-group dash binding and linewidth as a GPU-consumable typed width input where use.gpu Line supports it. Keep style data lazy through scale and mark bindings; do not create a row-shaped CPU result solely to draw a mark. Preserve CPU rendering as an explicit equivalent fallback. Point stroke is separately tracked by gggplot-aei.9 because use.gpu Point has no outline primitive.
acceptance_criteria: linetype: solid/dashed/dotted/dotdash (at minimum) render distinct dash patterns on Line nodes; a discrete linetype scale trains and legends like the existing shape scale. linewidth is mappable (continuous) in addition to the existing literal params.width. Tests in pipeline_test.ts cover literal and mapped styles, grouping, and renderer-node lowering.
notes: Pre-implementation backend review (2026-07-16): use.gpu Line exposes dash and widths, so linetype lowers as a per-effective-group dash binding and linewidth as a typed per-vertex width input. use.gpu Point has no stroke-width/outline prop; point-border work is intentionally split into gggplot-aei.9 so this bead never claims an unavailable native primitive.
close_reason: Implemented typed linetype and linewidth scales, effective-group dash lowering, GPU Line widths, legends, literal reference-line styles, real mtcars coverage, and pipeline/site validation.

title: Fix stat_summary to aggregate per effective group

A grouped stat_summary (e.g. aes(x=day, y=value, color=series)) should compute one aggregated point per (x, effective group) and preserve the group column so a mapped color/fill legend still works and downstream geoms (point/line) can still split by group for rendering.
