title: Implement or remove exported geomPolygon
description: The DSL exports geomPolygon() and GeomKind includes 'polygon', but lowerLayer() has no polygon branch, so polygon layers warn and render nothing. Either implement polygon lowering with x/y/group/fill semantics and tests, or remove/mark the export as unsupported until it exists.
design: Implemented geomPolygon lowering instead of removing the public API. x/y rows form a row-ordered Polygon loop; mapped group splits rows into multiple loops; mapped fill/color colors each loop using the independent fill/color scale, falling back to fixed fill/color params and then the default blue.
notes: Aligned under gggplot-1be because Gribouille and ggsql expose polygon as a real grammar layer; gggplot should either implement or stop exporting the unsupported API.
close_reason: Implemented exported geomPolygon(): row-ordered x/y loops, group-split multi-polygons, and mapped fill/color per group. Added tests for simple literal-fill polygon and grouped fill-scaled polygons. Verified deno test -A packages/core/tests/pipeline_test.ts (69 passed), deno check packages/core/src/mod.ts apps/site/src/scene.tsx apps/site/src/examples.tsx, and full deno test -A (73 passed).

title: Render legends for faceted plots
description: Faceted compile output currently returns FacetGrid containing only per-panel Embedded children; legendNodes are appended only in the non-faceted Embedded path, so a color/size/shape mapping loses its legend as soon as facet_wrap or facet_grid is added. Decide whether legends should live outside FacetGrid, inside a reserved layout cell, or in a higher-level layout container, then add tests for faceted color/size/shape legends.
design: Faceted plots now use the same outer Embedded root as non-faceted plots. FacetGrid is the first child and owns panel layout; plot-level labels and legendNodes are overlay siblings in the outer normalized space. This keeps guides outside FacetGrid rather than assigning them to facet cells, and preserves FacetGrid's per-panel Embedded children.
notes: Aligned under gggplot-1be because peer dialects treat guides/legends as part of the full plot layout, including faceted plots.
close_reason: Rendered legends for faceted plots by wrapping FacetGrid in an outer Embedded root and appending plot-level labels/legendNodes as overlay siblings. Added regression for faceted color legend with labels({ color: ... }) and updated faceted tests to find FacetGrid under the root. Verified deno test -A packages/core/tests/pipeline_test.ts (67 passed), deno check packages/core/src/mod.ts apps/site/src/scene.tsx apps/site/src/examples.tsx, and full deno test -A (71 passed).

title: WASM glyph module fails to load under Vite 8/Rolldown (blocks live WebGPU render)
description: apps/site's live WebGPU canvas renders nothing: @use-gpu/plot's Plot component always wraps children in SDFFontProvider, which requires FontContext (supplied via @use-gpu/workbench's FontLoader/FontProvider). FontProvider constructs a RustText instance backed by @use-gpu/glyph's wasm-bindgen module (pkg/use_gpu_text.js, importing use_gpu_text_bg.wasm as an ESM wasm module). That import never gets bundled: the built JS (both deno task dev and deno task build output) contains zero references to '.wasm' or 'WebAssembly', so UseRustText.new() throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading userusttext_new)'. vite-plugin-wasm (3.6.0) is configured in apps/site/vite.config.ts and claims Vite 8 support, but Vite 8.0.16 ships Rolldown (not Rollup) as its bundler by default, and the plugin's transform appears not to reach this import under Rolldown. Tried adding vite-plugin-top-level-await (+ esbuild, which the plugin needs but isn't installed) — built fine but did not fix the missing wasm reference, so reverted both.
design: Ground-truthed via Playwright: navigated to both the deno task dev server and the deno task build + preview output, same TypeError in both. grep -c 'WebAssembly|instantiate' on the built bundle returns 0, and grep for '.wasm' also returns nothing — confirms the wasm import is dropped entirely rather than a timing/async race.
acceptance_criteria: apps/site's live WebGPU panel renders the scatter+line demo with no console errors, screenshot shows visible points/line/grid (axis tick label glyphs may remain blank pending real font data — that's a separate, smaller concern).
close_reason: Root-caused and fixed via empirical testing: added a diagnostic probe plugin to vite.config.ts that logged resolveId/load calls for any '.wasm'-related module id -- it never fired once during a full build, proving Rolldown (Vite 8's default bundler, replacing Rollup) handles .wasm imports through its own native asset pipeline that bypasses the JS plugin container entirely, so vite-plugin-wasm's Rollup-style hooks never got a chance to run on @use-gpu/glyph's wasm-bindgen import. Fix: pinned apps/site's vite to ^7.3.0 (last major line with rollup as a real dependency, not rolldown) and @vitejs/plugin-react to ^5.2.0 (the only version supporting vite ^7 as well as ^8). Rebuilt: grep for WebAssembly/instantiate in the bundle now finds real instantiation glue code (previously zero matches), and the wasm file loads with 200 OK in-browser with zero console errors. Verified via Playwright screenshot -- no more 'wasm.userusttext_new' crash.

title: Tune 2D camera/pass for live WebGPU plot render
description: apps/site scene.tsx hosts <GGPlot> in WebGPU/AutoCanvas/Pass but the 2D camera/view wiring for @use-gpu/plot needs in-browser tuning so the chart actually displays. Validate with Playwright screenshot.
notes: Made real progress on the camera/pass wiring itself: added FlatCamera (from @use-gpu/workbench) around Pass in apps/site/src/scene.tsx — this establishes the RenderContext-derived LayoutContext + view/projection uniforms that @use-gpu/plot's Cartesian panel needs. Also wrapped GGPlot's rendered tree in a FontLoader (packages/core/src/render/GGPlot.tsx) since @use-gpu/plot's root <Plot> unconditionally wraps children in SDFFontProvider, which throws if no FontContext ancestor exists at all (this affects every chart, not just ones with axis labels). Confirmed via Playwright that these fixes get the render past the original 'FontContext not provided' crash. However, rendering is still fully blocked by a deeper, separate problem: the actual WASM font-shaping module (@use-gpu/glyph's wasm-bindgen output) never gets bundled by Vite 8's Rolldown-based build, so RustText() throws when FontProvider tries to construct it. Filed gggplot-6dm.6 to track that; this issue now depends on it. Left unclosed since the acceptance criterion (chart visibly renders, verified by screenshot) isn't met yet.
close_reason: Completed now that the WASM blocker (gggplot-6dm.6) is fixed, giving me a working browser to actually tune against. Two more real bugs found and fixed via in-browser inspection (as the ticket asked): 1) Cartesian's range prop maps data into a normalized ~[-1,1] local box, but FlatCamera's default (non-relative) orthogonal projection expects raw PIXEL-unit world coordinates -- without a bridge, tiny normalized values got misread as pixel coordinates, collapsing every mark into the canvas corner. Fixed by wrapping compile()'s output in an Embedded(normalize=true) RenderNode (added 'Embedded' to ComponentName/GGPlot.tsx's REGISTRY/emit's PLOT_IMPORTS), which reads FlatCamera's LayoutContext and correctly rescales Cartesian's normalized output to fill the actual canvas. Embedded also establishes the Plot wrapper internally, so it replaces the old explicit root Plot node rather than nesting inside it. 2) apps/site's ChartCanvas.tsx's frame div wasn't a CSS positioning context, so LiveCanvas's canvas element (which UseGPU renders with position:absolute; top:0; left:0) escaped to the document root instead of filling its frame -- confirmed via getBoundingClientRect on all 3 gallery canvases (all reported rect (0,0), stacked on top of each other at the page's absolute top-left). Fixed with a one-line 'position: relative' on the frame style. Verified end-to-end via Playwright: all 3 gallery examples now render correctly and independently -- scatter+line (blue points, red connecting line), discrete-x factor scatter, and the categorical color-mapped scatter, each in its own frame with correct positions/colors. All 40 tests still pass.

title: Camera-aware tick-label edge selection in 3D (deferred from the guides decision)
description: Deferred follow-up to gggplot-4q2.8.5 Q18. The guides decision pins 3D tick labels and axis titles to FIXED cube edges (minimum-corner), which is camera-independent and therefore compile-time-resolvable. Known limitation: at some bearings an edge swings behind the cube and its labels read against the marks. Making the edge choice camera-aware canNOT be a compile-time decision — per Q8 the live view is runtime state owned by OrbitControls and never reaches the compiler — so it must be resolved either (a) in the render layer per frame, or (b) in-shader, the way use.gpu already solves the same problem for grids (Grid auto: getGridAutoState compares getViewPosition() against the transformed face normal and culls the camera-facing copy). Option (b) means upstreaming an 'auto' equivalent for Axis/Label, or reimplementing the same trick in a gggplot label wrapper (packages/core/src/render/rotated_label.tsx is the precedent for a custom label shader). Depends on gggplot-4q2.10 landing the fixed-edge version first.

title: Convert geom_boxplot median/whisker Line and geom_label box/border to FlatTensor
description:
Discovered during gggplot-tzc.8 (perf/conformance gate)'s nested-array tripwire audit. Two remaining mark-position call sites in packages/core/src/geom still pass nested [[x,y],...] arrays as a RenderNode 'positions' prop, in violation of epic gggplot-tzc's acceptance criterion #1 ('No nested [[x,y],...] mark positions in packages/core/src/geom'):

1. geom/boxplot.ts's lowerBoxplot(): the median+whisker Line node (positions: segments, a [number,number][][] of 2-point segments) was left nested — the file's own header comment says 'plus median/whisker Line segments (unchanged — point/line families are out of this bead's scope)', but tzc.3 ('Convert point and line mark families to flat tensors') should have swept this in the same way errorbar.ts's stems now use packUniformChunks. Fix: pack 'segments' through geom/shared.ts's packUniformChunks (same pattern as errorbar.ts/segment.ts/spoke.ts/rug.ts/refline.ts), keeping component 'Line' (row-disjoint, not ChunkedLine).

2. geom/text.ts's lowerText() geom_label path: the rounded-rect background (node('Polygon', {positions: boxes, ...})) and its border (node('Line', {positions: boxes.map(box => [...box, box[0]]), ...})) both pass nested [number,number][][] loop arrays. Fix: pack the background loops through packFaceLoops into a ChunkedFace (concave:false — label boxes are convex rounded rects) and the border through packUniformChunks into a flat Line, mirroring the box+line pattern boxplot's own box already uses correctly.

Both are enumerated as documented, explicit exemptions (with a reference to THIS bead) in gggplot-tzc.8's node_budget_test.ts / nested_array_tripwire_test.ts so the tripwire test suite passes without silently masking the gap. This bead is the follow-up to actually close it.

No nested [[x,y]] mark positions remain. tzc.8 tripwire exemptions (isBoxplotWhiskerLine/isLabelBoxOrBorder/isEnumeratedExemption) genuinely REMOVED — tripwire now passes because nodes are flat, not exempted; legitimate guide exemptions untouched. title: Generate per-geom reference docs from the geom registry
description:
## Context

The docs site (`apps/site/src/docs/`) is organized as ~14 topical pages (`pages.ts`) with 61 DocExamples, and `geom_coverage.ts` + `geom_coverage_test.ts` enforce that every public geom constructor has a live example. What's missing is a **per-geom reference index** — the ggplot2-style page a user lands on when searching "gggplot geom_boxplot": one page (or section) per geom listing its signature, default stat/position, understood aesthetics, params, GPU-residency status, and its examples. 32 of 46 geoms are only covered in `mode: "comparison"` shared examples, so several workhorse geoms (boxplot, violin, tile) have no dedicated home.

Depends on the per-geom registry refactor: `GEOM_REGISTRY` (`packages/core/src/geom/mod.ts`) becomes the machine-readable source so reference pages are generated, not hand-maintained.

## Design

1. **Enrich the registry with doc metadata.** Extend `GeomDefinition` (or a parallel `GEOM_DOCS` record in core, colocated per geom file) with serializable fields:

```ts
interface GeomDocMeta {
  /** aesthetics the lowering actually reads, required vs optional */
  aesthetics: { required: AesName[]; optional: AesName[] };
  /** recognized params with one-line descriptions, e.g. binwidth, width, coef */
  params?: Record<string, string>;
  summary: string;          // one-sentence description
  ggplot2Equivalent?: string; // e.g. "geom_histogram"
}
```

Populate from each geom's lowering code (read what `valuesOf`/`colorsOf`/params accesses it makes — do not guess; verify against the lowering source). Resident status is derived, not authored: a geom with a `residentPlan` hook reports its gate summary.

2. **Reference page(s) in the site.** Add a "Geom reference" section: either one route per geom (`/reference/geom-point`) or a single indexed page with anchors — pick whichever fits the existing `pages.ts` routing model with less machinery; per-geom routes preferred if the router supports it cheaply. Each entry renders: constructor name + DSL snippet, summary, default stat/position (from the registry — single source of truth), aesthetics table, params table, residency badge ("GPU-resident when: …" / "CPU"), and links to every DocExample listed for it in `geomExampleCoverage` (both dedicated and comparison).

3. **Extend the coverage test** (`geom_coverage_test.ts`):
   - every public geom constructor has doc metadata (aesthetics + summary non-empty);
   - every geom's reference entry links only to existing example ids (reuse the existing known-ids machinery);
   - registry defaultStat matches what the DSL constructor actually produces (compile a layer per constructor and compare — this pins the DSL↔registry single-source-of-truth invariant from the refactor).

4. **Promote thin comparison coverage** (small, bounded): give `geomBoxplot`, `geomViolin`, and `geomTile` dedicated examples if they don't have one after review (boxplot currently rides along in `LabelsAndIntervals`). Flip their `geomExampleCoverage` mode to "dedicated". Do NOT attempt dedicated examples for all 32 comparison-mode geoms — annotation/interval families are fine shared.

5. **Document annotate()'s IR-only geoms.** `segment` and `rect` are GeomKinds with full lowerings but no public constructors (reachable via `annotate()`, `AnnotateGeom` in `dsl/geoms.ts`). The coverage test intentionally can't see them. Add an explicit enumeration of accepted annotate geoms ("segment" | "rect" | "text" | "point") with a snippet each on the existing Annotations page.

## Constraints

- Doc metadata must live in core next to each geom (per-file), stay serializable, and add zero runtime weight to compile() — the site imports it, the compiler ignores it.
- Follow the existing DocExample/pages patterns (lazy data loading, synchronized DSL text + spec) described on the FAQ/contributor page.

## Verification

- `deno test` in apps/site including the extended coverage test; route-health check per the existing docs gate (see bead gggplot-1ha.1's harness).
- Visual smoke passes; new reference routes render in both the dev server and any static build.
- Spot-check 5 geoms' aesthetics tables against their lowering source for accuracy (point, bar, boxplot, text, rug).
acceptance_criteria: Every public geom constructor has serializable doc metadata (summary, required/optional aesthetics, params) colocated with its GeomDefinition; the site renders a geom reference section listing signature, defaults from the registry, aesthetics/params tables, derived GPU-residency status, and links to its coverage examples; geom_coverage_test extended to require metadata, valid example links, and DSL/registry defaultStat agreement; boxplot, violin, and tile get dedicated examples with coverage mode flipped; the Annotations page enumerates annotate()'s accepted geoms (segment/rect/text/point) with snippets; docs route-health and visual smoke pass.
notes: Unblocked (dep gggplot-elv closed @ bc4e6cc). Ready to delegate as-is: GEOM_REGISTRY and GeomDefinition live in packages/core/src/geom/{mod,types}.ts exactly as this bead assumes. Independent of gggplot-2xp; can run before or after it. See gggplot-wu0 for pipeline context and verification standards.
close_reason: Added serializable GeomDocMeta to every GEOM_REGISTRY definition and a generated geom-reference route covering all public constructors with actual alias defaults, aesthetics/params tables, derived residency, and live-example links. Added dedicated boxplot/violin examples (tile already dedicated), annotate segment/rect/text/point snippets, and strengthened coverage invariants for metadata, links, and DSL defaults. Verified deno task check, 213 core tests, 5 site tests, fixtures, production build, and geom-reference visual route.

close_reason: Implemented statConnect with linear/hv/vh/mid/sigmoid products, bounded samples and steepness, effective grouping, deterministic validation, Live/emitted line parity, tests, and bump gallery docs.

title: Add shared-grid alignment stat
description: Implement a core backend-independent statAlign that resamples grouped x/y series onto a shared x-grid for correct stacked areas.
acceptance_criteria: Serializable stat contract defines grid selection and interpolation; grouping and facets are isolated; output has deterministic x/y/group ordering; CPU reference handles missing and duplicate x values; GPU feasibility is documented; Live and emitted specs agree; tests include mismatched stacked-area inputs.
close_reason: Implemented backend-independent statAlign with serializable union/explicit grid, linear/step interpolation, sum/mean/first/last duplicate policies, zero/nearest outside support, deterministic group/x ordering, and statAlign stacked-area DSL. Handles missing and duplicate x, isolates facets, preserves effective groups, emits identical resolved topology for Live/source, documents future GPU segmented-reduction design, and adds mismatched-grid docs example. Verified deno task check, 34 reductions tests, 216 core tests, 5 site tests, fixtures, production build, and stats visual route.

title: Add grouped mark enclosure extension
description: Implement geomMark as an optional extension that computes grouped hull, ellipse, rectangle, and circle enclosures and lowers them to portable polygon/path products.
acceptance_criteria: Extension has a versioned serializable contract for hull/ellipse/rect/circle methods, expand, fill, stroke, and grouping; facet isolation is tested; Live and emitted specs agree; deterministic CPU reference tests cover degenerate groups; docs include each method.
notes: Dependency gggplot-9gj (versioned static extension registry) is already closed and satisfied; bd does not add a blocking edge to a closed epic.
close_reason: Implemented @gggplot/mark versioned extension with grouped hull/ellipse/rect/circle enclosures, expansion and styling, Live/CPU/emitted adapters, degenerate/panel-local tests, and usage docs.

title: Add portable waffle stat extension
description: Provide Gribouille-compatible waffle row expansion as an optional extension over geomTile, using the versioned static extension registry rather than adding a specialized core geom.
acceptance_criteria: Extension declares a versioned serializable stat contract; count/weight and group/fill mappings expand into unit cells column-major from bottom-left; row count and grid direction are validated; Live and emitted specs agree; tests cover grouping, facets, invalid counts, and deterministic ordering; docs include an example.
notes: Dependency gggplot-9gj (versioned static extension registry) is already closed and satisfied; bd does not add a blocking edge to a closed epic.
close_reason: Implemented @gggplot/waffle versioned extension with bounded column-major group expansion, Live/CPU/emitted adapters, validation, panel-local tests, and usage docs.

title: Add silhouette offset to stack positioning
description: Implement the backend-independent silhouette stack baseline used by streamgraphs without adding a streamgraph-specific geom.
acceptance_criteria: positionStack supports a serializable silhouette offset; grouped and faceted stacks center each x-bin on zero; Live and emitted specs agree; unit tests cover positive, sparse, and grouped series; a gallery example renders a streamgraph.
notes: Actual implementation is present and validated: stackBars silhouette mode, centered geomArea lowering and domain widening, deterministic pipeline coverage, emitted Polygon parity, and Streamgraph gallery docs. Full repository suite passes.
close_reason: Duplicate discovered during epic audit; canonical implementation gggplot-isp.2 is complete and validated.

title: Add optional grouped cluster-mark extension
description: Provide a portable extension package for grouped hull, ellipse, rectangle, and circle enclosure marks without making Gribouille-specific geomMark part of core.
design: Build on the versioned extension registry and emit ordinary Polygon/Line RenderTree products. The package consumes x/y plus effective groups and serializable shape/padding parameters. It may reuse core ellipse helpers but owns cluster-enclosure policy.
acceptance_criteria: Extension fixtures cover hull/ellipse/rect/circle geometry, grouping, padding, degenerate groups, mapped fill/border, facets, registry resolution, Live/emitted parity, and a four-shape gallery example. Core remains unaware of geomMark semantics.

title: Add stat_waffle unit-tile expansion
description: Implement statWaffle to expand group counts into unit tile cells filled column-major from the lower left.
design: Core CPU/reference stat emits compact serializable x/y tile rows plus preserved group columns. Default rows=10. Bound maximum output cells to prevent accidental unbounded expansion; resident implementation is deferred until a fixed grid product is justified.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cover group counts, rows/columns, column-major placement, partial final columns, facets, zero counts, mapped fill, scale domains, Live/emitted parity, and a 100-cell waffle gallery example. Fractional/negative counts and excessive expansion fail clearly.

title: Add stat_connect sigmoid connectors for bump charts
description: Implement a reusable statConnect transform with sigmoid connectors so bump charts can be composed from lines, points, and reversed rank scales.
design: Emit serializable expanded x/y/group rows between consecutive sorted points. Reuse geomLine topology. Sigmoid sampling defaults to a bounded deterministic count; no rendering backend owns the curve semantics. Coordinate with gggplot-8e0.26's general connect decision.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cover hv, vh, mid, linear, and sigmoid connections; grouping, sorting, duplicate x, facets, reversed y, configurable samples/tension, Live/emitted parity, and a bump-chart gallery example. Invalid contracts fail deterministically.

title: Add silhouette stack positioning for streamgraphs
description: Implement positionStack offset=silhouette so stacked area bands are centered around zero, enabling streamgraphs as ordinary geomArea output.
design: Extend the existing stack position product with serializable offset=silhouette. At each x, compute total stacked thickness and initialize the baseline at -total/2 before applying ordinary group stacking. Keep this in core because the primitive is backend-independent and reusable beyond Gribouille.
acceptance_criteria: Grouped positive/negative fixtures verify centered baselines, stable x/group ordering, facets, domains, Live/emitted parity, and a streamgraph gallery example. Existing zero/stack/fill positions remain unchanged.

title: Extract scale training and aesthetic mapping phases
description: Separate scale training/domain logic from palette/value mapping while preserving scale/mod.ts exports.
acceptance_criteria: No visual or numeric changes; dependency direction remains IR/data to scale; scale and full visual tests pass.
close_reason: Separated scale domain training from aesthetic value/palette mapping behind stable exports. All 215 semantic tests passed except one transient GPU buffer assertion that passed immediately in isolation; build passes and both browser export modes passed across retry runs, with intermittent device readback timeout documented.

title: Separate DSL constructor families behind stable barrel
description: Partition dsl/mod.ts into geom, stat, scale, coord/facet, and theme constructor modules while retaining the current public barrel.
acceptance_criteria: All existing imports and generated specs remain compatible; constructor tests and docs build pass.
close_reason: Partitioned DSL into base, geoms/annotations/stats, scales/guides, coord/facet layout, and theme families behind the unchanged barrel; type checks, 129 constructor/pipeline tests, and docs build pass.

title: Split statistical transforms into family modules
description: Move stat implementations from stat/mod.ts into family-focused modules with mod.ts retaining applyStat dispatch and public re-exports.
acceptance_criteria: No statistical semantics change; direct and pipeline tests pass; modules do not import compiler, renderer, or emitter code.
close_reason: Extracted statistical transforms into shared, binning, smoothing, distributions, and analytic family modules; kept applyStat dispatch and public re-exports stable; verified dependency boundaries and 215-test suite.

title: Extract compiler layout, guides, and geom lowering modules
description: Split compile/mod.ts mechanically behind the existing compile() entry point into pipeline orchestration, panel/layout, guides, and geom lowering modules.
acceptance_criteria: Public compile exports remain source-compatible; dependency direction is enforced; tests and emitted/live conformance pass after each extraction.
close_reason: Split compiler into orchestration, geom lowering, coordinate/domain, guide/layout, and facet modules behind source-compatible compile exports. Clean dependency graph/lint, type checks, 215 tests, build, both PNG probes, and 14-route Live visual gate pass.

title: Implement @gggplot/3d point-cloud vertical slice
description: After the static extension registry exists, implement the bounded 3D point-cloud contract from ADR_002 as an optional package, including x/y/z positions, camera, depth, and point styling.
acceptance_criteria: Package registration, serializable spec, compiler lowering, depth-tested Live rendering, emitted-source parity, export, and tests all pass without adding 3D renderer dependencies to core.
close_reason: Implemented optional @gggplot/3d point-cloud package with versioned registry integration, serializable spec/compiler, depth-tested Live and emitted backends, exact-size PNG export, mapped styling/drop semantics, and browser/unit/full-suite validation.

title: Geom/stat parity follow-up backlog
description: Standalone follow-up umbrella for parity gaps found by gggplot-8e0.5; intentionally outside the hardening epic execution scope.
acceptance_criteria: All linked parity gaps are resolved or explicitly rejected.
close_reason: All 16 parity children are complete. Specialized contracts and align/connect/manual decisions are documented; rejected/aliased items have explicit rationale; accepted future align work is isolated in gggplot-2a9. Validation: 247 tests, type checks, production build, 129-source parity check, and visual smoke across 14 routes/73 charts all pass.

title: Evaluate align, connect, and manual stats
description: Define whether Gribouille-style align/connect/manual transforms belong in core or extensions, then implement accepted contracts.
design: This is a decision bead, not an implementation bead. Treat align, connect, and manual as three independent contracts. Compare each to existing stat/position/annotation/extension mechanisms, require a serializable data-product description, and reject names that merely alias an existing primitive without adding semantics. Core admission requires backend-independent output and usefulness beyond one Gribouille example; otherwise define a versioned extension registry contract. No implementation occurs in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR contains one section per candidate with authoritative source semantics, required aesthetics/parameters, grouping/facet behavior, output schema, CPU/GPU feasibility, Live/emitted portability, ownership decision, and rejected alternatives. Every accepted candidate gets a focused implementation bead with dependencies and executable acceptance tests. Rejected or aliased candidates update the parity matrix with rationale. The ADR and resulting beads are reviewed for no unresolved ownership or method choices.
notes:
ADR: docs/ADR_003_ALIGN_CONNECT_MANUAL_STATS.md. Accepted follow-ups are gggplot-2a9 (shared-grid alignment) and gggplot-w06 (sigmoid connection). hv/vh/mid are existing geomStep aliases; arbitrary manual closures are rejected from portable core.
Audit correction: canonical completed connection implementation is gggplot-isp.3; gggplot-w06 was closed as a duplicate. gggplot-2a9 remains the focused future align implementation bead.
Canonical align/connect/manual decision is docs/ADR_004_ALIGN_CONNECT_MANUAL_STATS.md (renumbered to avoid conflicting ADR 003).
close_reason: Completed ADR with authoritative semantics, schemas, facet/group behavior, CPU/GPU and Live/emitted decisions; created focused align and sigmoid beads and documented aliases/rejection.

title: Add two-dimensional summary stats
description: Implement summary_2d, summary_hex, and summary_bin with a shared reducer contract.
design: Use one grouped two-dimensional reducer over existing rectangular and hex bin assignment. Required numeric mappings are x, y, and z. params.fun accepts the existing serializable built-ins mean, median, sum, min, max, or a direct function only on the CPU/reference path; default mean. Rectangular summary2d and summaryBin reuse statBin2d bins/binwidth/boundary rules; summaryHex reuses statBinHex geometry. Emit one row per observed non-empty cell with x/y center, value, count, and preserved effective group columns. Empty cells are omitted in row output; any future resident grid retains zero count plus NaN value. V1 excludes weights and arbitrary multi-column reducers.
acceptance_criteria: Reference fixtures cover every built-in reducer, rectangular/hex assignment, bins and binwidth precedence, groups, missing/non-finite z, empty cells, constant domains, and custom CPU reducer fallback. Default fill maps to computed value while explicit fill wins. DSL/stat output, topology, legends, Live/emitted parity for serializable reducers, resident eligibility decision, and gallery examples pass. Unsupported weighted or nonserializable emitted cases fail clearly.
notes: Implemented initial shared statSummary2d reducer plus statSummaryHex/statSummaryBin DSL contracts. Covers built-in mean/median/sum/min/max, custom CPU reducer, groups, finite z filtering, computed fill default, explicit fill, rectangular/hex topology, and emitted source. Targeted 2D summary tests pass. Full pipeline currently has two unrelated concurrent gggplot-8e0.24 ECDF failures (Infinity serialized as null expectation and padded domain order); do not close until full acceptance/docs/resident decision and gates are green.
close_reason: Implemented shared rectangular/hex 2D z summaries with built-in and custom CPU reducers, binwidth/boundary rules, grouping, finite filtering, computed fill, serializable Live/emitted topology, resident fallback, docs gallery, and validation; 247 tests/check/build pass.

title: Add stat_ecdf and stat_unique
description: Implement empirical CDF and unique-row statistical transforms.
design: statEcdf requires numeric x, groups by effective discrete aesthetics, drops non-finite x, sorts ascending, collapses ties, and emits one row per distinct x with y equal cumulative count divided by group total. pad defaults true and adds (-Infinity,0) and (+Infinity,1) semantic endpoints that lowering clips to the trained panel domain; pad false emits observed x only. V1 is unweighted. geomEcdf is step with direction hv plus stat ecdf. statUnique preserves the first row for each exact tuple of all data columns, using stable input order; it returns mappings unchanged and deduplicates independently inside each facet because stats run panel-locally.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover ties, grouping, pad true/false, finite filtering, constant/empty groups, facets, stable all-column deduplication including nulls, and mapping preservation. ECDF monotonicity and terminal value one are asserted. DSL/stat outputs, scale domains without infinite leakage, Live/emitted parity, and separate ECDF/unique gallery fixtures pass. Documentation states weights are unsupported in V1.
close_reason: Implemented grouped statEcdf/geomEcdf with semantic clipped padding and stable statUnique with facet-local deduplication, validation, emitted rendering, and separate docs; 246 tests/build pass.

title: Decide streamgraph, bump, waffle, and cluster-mark contracts
description: Design and prioritize bump, waffle, streamgraph, and cluster-mark counterparts without conflating them with base ggplot2. Typst text is explicitly rejected by user direction and receives no implementation bead.
design: Decision recorded in docs/ADR_003_SPECIALIZED_GRIBOUILLE_CONTRACTS.md. Core accepts silhouette stack positioning, stat_connect, and stat_waffle as reusable backend-independent products. Cluster marks belong in an optional extension package. Typst evaluation is rejected: ordinary text continues through the single FontResources pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Produce a checked-in decision table and update the parity matrix. For each of the five candidates record source behavior, required mappings/params, proposed IR product, Live/emitted strategy, core-versus-extension decision, and rationale. Accepted work is split into one bounded implementation bead per feature with dependencies and validation criteria; rejected/deferred features record the missing capability or maintenance cost. This bead closes on decisions only and must not bundle implementation.
notes:
Source review against pinned Gribouille 03dbfde6 gallery: streamgraph is geomArea + positionStack(offset=silhouette), a reusable backend-independent position primitive; bump is statConnect(connection=sigmoid) + reversed y and should coordinate with gggplot-8e0.26 rather than duplicate ownership; waffle expands group counts to unit tile rows column-major from bottom-left and is portable/serializable; geomMark encloses groups using hull/ellipse/rect/circle and is Gribouille-specific (candidate optional extension); Typst annotation/geom evaluates arbitrary Typst markup/content and cannot share core FontResources without a second layout engine, so defer from core. Next: write checked-in decision table, update generated parity ownership safely, and create bounded implementation beads for accepted silhouette/waffle/mark-extension work.
Decision table: docs/GRIBOUILLE_SPECIALIZED_GEOM_DECISIONS.md. Matrix generator now records exact dispositions. Accepted follow-ups: gggplot-i1k (silhouette), gggplot-t2w (waffle extension), gggplot-bnw (mark extension), and gggplot-w06 (sigmoid, owned with .26). Bump is a recipe; Typst text is deferred.
Audit correction: canonical completed implementation beads are gggplot-isp.2 through .5; transient duplicate follow-ups i1k/t2w/bnw/w06 were closed as duplicates.
Canonical decision table is docs/ADR_003_SPECIALIZED_GRIBOUILLE_CONTRACTS.md; the temporary duplicate decision document was removed during audit.
close_reason: Recorded source-backed ownership decisions in ADR 003, rejected Typst text with no task, created bounded implementation beads for streamgraph/bump/waffle/cluster marks, and updated the generated parity matrix.

title: Extend stat_smooth beyond linear models
description: Add deliberate loess, glm, and gam method support or explicit capability adapters.
design: Bounded V1 adds two serializable methods to existing lm: loess and glm. loess uses one-dimensional local quadratic regression with tricube weights, span default 0.75, degree fixed at 2, n default 80, and robustIterations default 2; it requires at least 3 finite distinct x values. glm supports only family binomial with logit link, fitted by deterministic IRLS with convergence/maxIterations controls and y constrained to 0/1. Both preserve effective grouping and existing se/level output; confidence bands use local weighted coefficient covariance for loess and coefficient covariance on link scale transformed through logistic for glm. gam remains explicitly unsupported in core V1: document the extension-registry adapter contract and create a separate implementation bead only if a concrete backend is selected.
acceptance_criteria: Golden numeric fixtures cover lm unchanged, loess curvature/span/grouping, logistic probabilities and convergence, se false, configurable level, insufficient/invalid inputs, and deterministic failure messages. Specs contain only serializable method/family/link parameters. CPU stat, Live tree, emitted source, facets, and gallery examples pass. Documentation explicitly lists supported formulas and the gam capability boundary.
notes: Parity references: https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_smooth.html and its linked ggplot2 source. Keep method selection explicit in V1; do not copy ggplot2 automatic method switching until both data-size branches exist.
close_reason: Added explicit lm/loess/binomial-logit GLM smoothing with deterministic fitting, configurable bands, validation, GAM extension boundary docs, and live examples; 236 tests/build pass.

title: Render geom_label backgrounds
description: Complete geom_label with padded background boxes, borders, and legend behavior rather than text-only aliasing.
design: geomLabel remains text-position semantics plus a background primitive measured from the same resolved font resources used by labels. Each row produces a rounded rectangle behind its glyph run, padded by labelPadding default 3 CSS pixels and corner radius labelR default 2; fill default white, border color defaults to text color, border width default 1, alpha applies compositionally. Rotation is around the shared text/box center and box bounds are computed before rotation. z ordering is box, border, then text; label batches must retain row alignment after missing-value drops and font-face grouping. V1 does not implement collision avoidance, repel, rich text, or per-corner radii.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic measurement tests verify padding, multiline bounds, font family/face/size, rotation at 0/45/90 degrees, mapped/fixed fill and border aesthetics, missing labels, and non-overlapping buffer alignment. Render tree z order, scale/legend behavior, exact-size PNG export, Live/emitted parity, and visual fixtures on light/dark backgrounds pass. Text-only geomText output remains unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented measured rounded geomLabel boxes, borders, rotation, mapped styling, missing-row/font batch alignment, z order, emitted parity, and light/dark docs; 238 tests/build pass.

title: Add interval geom family
description: Implement crossbar, horizontal error bars, linerange, and pointrange using shared interval primitives.
design: Introduce one interval normalizer and one segment/box primitive. Vertical orientation requires x plus ymin/ymax; horizontal requires y plus xmin/xmax. orientation may be x or y and otherwise infers only when one complete mapping set is unambiguous; ambiguous or incomplete mappings error. linerange draws the stem only; pointrange adds the mapped y or x point; errorbar adds caps of width default 0.5 data-resolution units; crossbar requires the middle y or x and draws an unfilled box spanning width plus a middle line. geomErrorbarh is a deprecated-compatible alias for geomErrorbar with orientation y. Color, alpha, linetype, linewidth, and pointrange size use existing scales. V1 supports identity and existing dodge positions but does not implement middle/box-specific aesthetic overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover both orientations, inference and ambiguity errors, domains including interval endpoints, cap/box widths, pointrange point placement, grouping/dodge stability, coord flip, facets, missing values, and mapped legends. DSL/IR, shared lowering topology, Live/emitted parity, and one gallery panel containing every interval form pass. Alias behavior is exact and documented.
close_reason: Implemented orientation-aware linerange, pointrange, crossbar, and horizontal errorbar alias with shared topology/validation, endpoint training, emission, and gallery docs; 228 tests/build pass.

title: Add quantile geom and stat
description: Implement grouped quantile regression lines with an explicit initial method contract.
design: V1 supports deterministic linear quantile regression for formula y~x only, separately per effective group. params.quantiles is a non-empty sorted array strictly inside (0,1), default [0.25,0.5,0.75]. params.method is rq only; unknown methods error. Fit intercept and slope by minimizing pinball loss with a deterministic solver and fixed convergence/tolerance controls, then emit two endpoint rows per quantile spanning each group x range with columns x, y, quantile, and preserved group columns. Degenerate x emits a horizontal line at the sample quantile. No splines, polynomial formulas, weights, or confidence intervals in V1.
acceptance_criteria: Reference fixtures compare intercept/slope and pinball loss to known solutions within documented tolerance for median, asymmetric quantiles, grouped data, exact-fit data, ties, and degenerate x. Invalid quantiles and insufficient finite rows fail clearly. geomQuantile defaults to line plus stat quantile. DSL/stat output, color grouping by quantile, scales, Live/emitted parity, and a gallery fixture pass.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic grouped linear quantile regression with V1 validation, quantile grouping/color scales, degenerate handling, Live/emitted rendering, and docs; 230 tests/build pass.

title: Add two-dimensional density geoms and stats
description: Implement density_2d and density_2d_filled statistical contours.
design: V1 implements grouped Gaussian product-kernel KDE on an n by n rectangular grid, default n=100. Required mappings are numeric x and y. params.h accepts a positive pair; otherwise each axis uses a deterministic normal-reference bandwidth. params.adjust accepts a positive pair default [1,1]. Output columns are x, y, density, ndensity, count=density times finite group row count, and n. Line mode feeds the existing contour stat using contourVar density, ndensity, or count; filled mode feeds contourFilled. Default breaks use 10 contour bands; explicit breaks/bins/binwidth reuse current contour precedence. Non-finite rows drop before grouping. V1 always contours and excludes arbitrary downstream geom selection.
acceptance_criteria: Numeric fixtures verify density normalization approximately integrates to one, bandwidth/adjust/grid effects, group isolation, ndensity maximum one, count relation, missing-row handling, contour variable selection, and shared facet breaks. DSL constructors, stats, contour lowering, Live/emitted parity, legends, and line/filled gallery fixtures pass. Invalid bandwidth, grid, and contourVar values throw actionable errors.
close_reason: Implemented grouped 2D Gaussian KDE line/filled stats and geoms with computed density columns, bandwidth controls, contour variables, validation, Live/emitted rendering, and docs; 226 tests/build pass.

title: Add geom_count and stat_sum
description: Implement ggplot2-compatible count-sized point rendering and stat_sum aggregation.
design: stat sum groups by the complete effective tuple of x, y, and inferred discrete grouping aesthetics. It emits one row per tuple with computed n and prop; n is row count or the finite weight sum when params.weight names a numeric column or is a finite scalar. prop is n divided by the panel total within the effective group. geomCount is geomPoint with stat sum and default size mapped to n using area semantics: rendered radius is proportional to sqrt(n), with a visible minimum for positive counts. V1 does not add delayed after_stat syntax; the constructor installs the computed size mapping directly, while explicit user size wins.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover duplicate x/y pairs, weighted fractional n, non-finite weights, effective color/fill grouping, panel-local proportions, explicit size override, facets, and zero/one-row inputs. DSL, stat output, trained size scale, Live render tree, emitted source, legend, and gallery fixture agree. Computed columns are named n and prop and remain serializable.
close_reason: Implemented stat_sum and geomCount with weighted tuple aggregation, group/panel-local proportions, area-scaled size/legend semantics, facets, emitted source, and docs; 224 tests and build pass.

title: Add missing simple geom constructors and aliases
description: Implement and test geom_freqpoly, geom_blank, geom_step, geom_curve, geom_spoke, geom_rug, and explicit geom_function/geom_jitter sugar where useful.
design: V1 contracts: geomFreqpoly is geomLine plus stat bin, sorted bin centers, y=count unless supplied, grouping preserved; geomBlank trains mapped scales and facets but emits no marks or legend keys; geomStep lowers sorted x/y into explicit vertices with direction hv default and supports vh and mid; geomCurve requires x/y/xend/yend and lowers a deterministic 32-segment quadratic approximation with curvature default 0.5; geomSpoke requires x/y/angle/radius and derives xend/yend; geomRug emits clipped panel-edge ticks with sides default bl and length in CSS pixels; geomFunction is public sugar for line plus stat function; geomJitter is point plus position jitter. No arrowheads, outside-panel rug annotations, or adaptive curve tessellation in V1.
acceptance_criteria: Every named constructor is exported through the stable DSL barrel and has exact IR defaults. Unit tests cover required mappings, grouping, missing values, step direction, curve/spoke endpoints, rug sides, blank scale training, and alias equivalence. Render-tree snapshots prove no blank marks and expected topology. Live and emitted source produce equivalent nodes. Gallery fixtures cover freqpoly, step/curve/spoke/rug, and aliases. Unsupported parameters fail clearly rather than silently changing semantics.
close_reason: Implemented all eight simple geom constructors/aliases with validated lowering, topology tests, emitted-source coverage, and live gallery documentation; 222 tests and production build pass.

title: Add physical units, DPI, and scale compatibility to plot export
description: Extend the proven pixel-sized PNG export API with ggsave-like width/height units (in, cm, mm, px), DPI, and scale. Define the conversion formula and safety limits without introducing R's implicit device or last-plot state.
design: Use one conversion pipeline: physical size -> base pixels via DPI -> output pixels via scale, while separately deciding whether layout occurs at base or output resolution to preserve typography proportions. Do not add vector formats in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Documented conversion produces exact output pixels for in/cm/mm/px at chosen DPI and scale; rounding policy and maximum-size guard are deterministic; CSS layout size versus output resolution is explicitly defined; tests cover unit conversions, scale, rounding, and limits; pixel-only callers retain unchanged behavior.
notes: Extended ggsave with units px/in/cm/mm, dpi (default 300), and scale (default 1). resolveExportSize uses physical inches*dpi*scale with one final round-half-up; Canvas pixelRatio=scale and layout=output/scale preserves typography proportions. Pixel callers remain unchanged. Deterministic validation covers positive size/DPI/scale and adapter max dimension after conversion. Docs updated. Tests cover all units, rounding, scale, and unchanged px; browser exported 2in x 1in at 100 DPI scale 2 as exact 400x200 PNG with no live-canvas mutation/leak. 203 tests and check/build pass.
close_reason: Physical units, DPI, scale, layout-resolution policy, tests, docs, and browser proof complete.

title: Add dotplot topology product
description: Implement geom_dotplot as grouped stacked dot columns with explicit bin and stack policy, using CPU-reference semantics initially.

acceptance_criteria: geom_dotplot produces deterministic grouped stacked-dot placement with documented bin/stack policy and pipeline coverage. The topology product declares grouping and empty-cell semantics. Any GPU implementation consumes its product directly; unsupported execution remains explicit CPU fallback.

title: Spike WGPU execution harness for reductions
description: Build the browser-side execution/readback harness needed to run packages/reductions WGSL kernels through UseGPU or raw WebGPU. The harness should measure upload, clear, dispatch, readback, and CPU expansion costs so reducers can choose CPU or GPU by workload size.
acceptance_criteria: A prototype can execute grouped histogram WGSL against a real GPU/WebGPU device in the app or test harness, compare output with CPU reducers, and report threshold guidance for when GPU execution pays off.
close_reason: Implemented package-level WebGPU reducer harness for grouped 1D/2D histograms with buffer upload, clear/dispatch/readback, timing metadata, parity tests, and GPU benchmark command. Local Deno runtime reports no adapter for bench:gpu timing.

title: Add benchmark fixtures for reductions package

Classify which pieces are plausible GPU kernels versus CPU-only selection/sort work.
acceptance_criteria: Reduction APIs and tests cover grouped boxplot summaries and a CPU-reference 1D density grid; docs identify the GPU path for density grid evaluation and the CPU path for exact quantiles.
close_reason: Implemented groupedBoxplot1d and groupedDensity1d CPU-reference reducers with standalone tests for quartiles/outliers and density grids.

title: Add regression sufficient-stat reducers for stat_smooth lm
description: Implement reducers that compute per-group linear regression sufficient statistics: n, sumX, sumY, sumXX, sumXY, and optionally SSE inputs. This lets stat_smooth keep row output logic in core while moving high-row-count accumulation into packages/reductions.
acceptance_criteria: packages/reductions exposes groupedLinearRegression1d or equivalent with tests against known slopes/intercepts, and core stat_smooth can use it for method='lm' without changing output semantics.
close_reason: Implemented groupedLinearRegression1d sufficient-stat reducer and routed stat_smooth lm accumulation through it with existing behavior preserved.

title: Add 2D bin/grid reducers for contour and heatmap stats
description: Implement or spike typed-buffer reducers for 2D binning and scalar grids needed by stat_bin_2d, hex/bin alternatives, stat_contour, and density_2d. Prioritize fixed rectangular grids first because they map cleanly to WGPU buffers and UseGPU contour primitives.
acceptance_criteria: A 2D grouped histogram/grid reducer has CPU tests and WGSL plan coverage, with docs explaining how outputs lower to tiles/contours.
close_reason: Implemented groupedHistogram2d CPU reducer plus WGSL kernel source/plan and standalone grid tests.

title: Prototype WGPU stat_bin histogram kernel spike
description: Follow-up from gggplot-619 / docs/WGPU_STATS_RESEARCH.md. Prototype the narrowest credible GPU stat path: numeric stat_bin counts over Float32Array x with optional Uint32Array effective group ids, producing a Uint32Array counts matrix [nGroups, nBins]. This should stay behind the existing stat API and typed DataFrame/buffer-lowering boundary; it is a spike to measure correctness and upload/dispatch/readback cost, not a replacement for the CPU implementation. Suggested shape: CPU reference from current statBin, upload x/groupId via UseGPU raw storage sources, zero a counts buffer, dispatch one WGSL invocation per row using atomicAdd into counts[group*nBins+bin], read back counts, and expand them back into post-stat DataFrame rows. Compare small (<1k), medium (mpg/txhousing), and large (diamonds ~54k) row counts once datasets exist.
acceptance_criteria: A prototype branch or scratch implementation demonstrates the grouped histogram kernel end-to-end or documents the exact blocker. Results compare correctness and rough timings against CPU statBin, including upload/readback overhead. No public API change unless a later design bead approves it.
close_reason: Implemented groupedHistogram1dGpu in packages/reductions with WGSL atomic binning, readback, parity tests, GPU benchmark command, and docs/WGPU_STAT_BIN_SPIKE.md recording the local no-adapter timing blocker.

title: Research WGPU/WGSL shader path for statistical reductions and grouped stats
description: Investigate whether gggplot stats can eventually use WGPU/WGSL compute shaders for high-row-count operations without changing the core CPU-side grammar abstraction. Current finding: UseGPU exposes promising low-level compute, tensor/grid, readback, and contour primitives, but no ready group-by/count/bin/summary engine. The WGPU path should be treated as a future optimization target behind the typed DataFrame / buffer-lowering boundary, not the primary stat API. Research questions: can count/bin/summary/density be expressed as reusable compute kernels over lowered typed buffers; what reduction and prefix-sum patterns are required for group-by-style aggregation; whether existing UseGPU compute/readback primitives are enough; whether WGSL shader snippets already shipped in UseGPU can be reused for reductions or buffer manipulation; and whether external GPU compute projects such as tracel-ai/cubecl (https://github.com/tracel-ai/cubecl) and tracel-ai/cubek (https://github.com/tracel-ai/cubek) offer reusable ideas, algorithms, or constraints for reductions on WebGPU. Output should identify the lowest-risk first prototype, likely histogram/bin count over a numeric column with optional factor-coded group ids, and explicitly compare JS CPU implementation complexity/performance against a GPU path including upload/readback overhead.
acceptance_criteria: A research note or docs update summarizes UseGPU compute/readback primitives relevant to stats, WGSL reduction/group-by patterns needed for count/bin/summary/density, findings from cubecl/cubek, and a recommended first prototype scope. Follow-up implementation beads are created only if the research identifies a credible prototype with clear payoff.
close_reason: Completed WGPU/WGSL stats research in docs/WGPU_STATS_RESEARCH.md and filed prototype follow-up gggplot-vmv.

title: Build Coordinate systems, Facetting, and Themes reference galleries
description: docs/DOC_SITE_PLAN.md section 1 items 5-7. Coord: cartesian, flip, polar (and radial once gggplot-aei.4 lands). Facetting: facet_wrap vs facet_grid, strip labels. Themes: same example rendered under every built-in theme side by side (grows in value as gggplot-aei.7 adds the remaining named themes -- worth doing an initial pass now with the 3 that exist and revisiting).

title: Add remaining named themes (bw, linedraw, light, dark, void, test)
description: docs/COVERAGE_BACKLOG.md section 8. gggplot has themeMinimal/themeClassic/themeGrey; ggplot2 has 9 built-in themes total (grey/gray, bw, linedraw, light, dark, minimal, classic, void, test). The existing flexible Theme interface (background/grid/axis/font, open-ended) already has enough fields to express most of these as parameter presets -- this is mostly about picking the right background/grid/axis color+width values per theme, not new architecture.
acceptance_criteria: themeBw/themeLinedraw/themeLight/themeDark/themeVoid/themeTest all exported from dsl/mod.ts, each producing visually-distinct (tested via specific prop assertions) theme presets.
