title: Add facet free scales (scales="free"/"free_x"/"free_y")
description: docs/COVERAGE_BACKLOG.md section 7. facet_wrap/facet_grid currently always share one fixed x/y domain across every panel (compile()'s scale training runs once over all panels combined). ggplot2's default is shared/fixed scales too, but scales='free'/'free_x'/'free_y' let each panel train its own domain independently -- useful when panels cover very different y ranges. Needs per-panel scale training instead of the current single global trainScales() call, threaded through to each panel's Cartesian/Polar range.
design: Model free scales as per-panel declarative view/scale products. A GPU-native panel may obtain only bounded domains/summaries from resident data; it must not materialize stat rows. Keep current facet paths as CPU fallback until per-panel source handles, caching keys, and invalidation policy are specified and tested.
acceptance_criteria: facetWrap()/facetGrid() accept a scales option; 'free'/'free_x'/'free_y' produce independently-domained panels while the current shared-scale behavior remains the default. Test with panels of deliberately different y ranges confirming independent domains.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the full 185-test suite

title: Add position_dodge2, position_jitterdodge, position_nudge
description: docs/COVERAGE_BACKLOG.md section 4. gggplot has identity/stack/dodge/jitter/fill (5 of 8 ggplot2 positions). position_dodge2 dodges non-uniform-width bars/boxplots without needing a shared width param (unlike the current dodge, which assumes uniform width). position_jitterdodge combines dodge+jitter (e.g. jittered points over a dodged boxplot). position_nudge applies a fixed x/y offset (commonly used to offset geom_text labels from their points).
design: Specify each position as a composable topology/offset product. For resident grids, dodge2/jitterdodge/nudge must be a GPU compute or uniform transform with declared shape and direct mark consumption; do not expose a GPU mode until CPU conformance, zero-cell behavior, and no-readback execution are proven. CPU positions remain explicit fallback.
acceptance_criteria: All three positions implemented in position/mod.ts and wired into the PositionKind union + compiler lowering, each with a pipeline_test.ts case.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the full 185-test suite

title: Add coord_radial and coord_fixed
description: docs/COVERAGE_BACKLOG.md section 6. coord_radial is ggplot2 4.0's successor to coord_polar (end/donut/rotate_angle params, pairs with guide_axis_theta()) -- Gribouille has ALREADY moved to radial-only and dropped a distinct polar, signaling this is where both peers are heading, so it's worth prioritizing over further polar-specific refinement. coord_fixed (locked aspect ratio between x/y units) is a small, separate, self-contained addition. Both should compose with the Coord.project field added in gggplot-1be.3 rather than reintroducing a special case.
design: Coordinate work is a uniform-only view transform when possible: radial/fixed parameters must not force reducer reruns, source uploads, or stat readback. Extend the declarative Coord contract and preserve GPU product handles across view changes; retain CPU fallback only for marks/projections not yet represented by a GPU consumer.
acceptance_criteria: coordRadial({ end, donut, rotateAngle }) renders a donut/sector chart (partial-circle polar). coordFixed(ratio) locks the x:y unit ratio in the Cartesian view. Tests for both in pipeline_test.ts.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by the full 185-test suite

title: Document gggplot's RenderTree-first architecture relative to peer dialects
description: Update design docs to explicitly position gggplot as a render-backend-native grammar dialect: TypeScript DSL -> serializable GGSpec -> RenderTree -> UseGPU live/codegen. Contrast with Gribouille's Typst-native document graphics and ggsql's SQL/query-native visualization language so future design choices are judged against the right architectural center.
design: Documented gggplot's architectural center relative to peers: Gribouille is Typst/document-native, ggsql is SQL/query-native, and gggplot should remain RenderTree/UseGPU-backend-native. Added a Peer Dialect Alignment section to docs/ARCHITECTURE.md that links to docs/GRAMMAR_ALIGNMENT.md.
close_reason: Documented gggplot as a RenderTree/UseGPU-backend-native grammar dialect relative to Gribouille's Typst/document-native approach and ggsql's SQL/query-native approach. Added Peer Dialect Alignment section to docs/ARCHITECTURE.md linking to docs/GRAMMAR_ALIGNMENT.md.

title: Audit grammar coverage against Gribouille and ggsql
description: Create a small coverage matrix comparing gggplot geoms/stats/positions/scales/facets/coords/themes against Gribouille and ggsql. Use it to identify intentional omissions versus accidental API gaps. Seed it with known gaps: linetype/linewidth scales, stroke aesthetics, free facet scales, density/violin/spatial/range/segment/rule layers, labels, and annotations.
design: Added docs/GRAMMAR_ALIGNMENT.md with a coverage matrix comparing gggplot against Gribouille and ggsql. The matrix records implemented, partial, tracked, and missing grammar areas, and explicitly ties known gaps to existing beads: gggplot-1be.1, gggplot-1be.2, gggplot-1be.3, gggplot-1be.4, gggplot-ob3, gggplot-165, and gggplot-gic.
close_reason: Completed grammar coverage audit in docs/GRAMMAR_ALIGNMENT.md, comparing gggplot with Gribouille and ggsql across architecture, geoms, stats, positions, scales, facets, coords, themes, labels, annotations, and backend invariants. Linked gaps to existing alignment beads and documented recommended implementation order.

title: Add annotation/literal layer API
description: ggsql separates data-bound DRAW layers from literal PLACE annotation layers. Design a gggplot annotation API for reference lines, segments, labels, points, and rectangles that do not inherit data mappings and whose aesthetics are literal settings. This should reduce awkward inheritAes:false use for annotations and provide a clear home for non-data guide-like marks.
close_reason: Added annotate(geom, opts) for literal segment/rect/text/point layers plus dedicated geom_hline/geom_vline/geom_abline reference-line builders; all reuse existing geom lowering via synthetic single-row data, inheritAes:false, and render across every facet panel. Tests: 7 new cases in pipeline_test.ts, full suite 80/80 passing.

title: Generalize coordinate projection beyond coordFlip
description: ggsql's PROJECT clause treats coordinate projection as a mapping from position aesthetics to a coordinate system, e.g. PROJECT y, x TO cartesian. Evaluate replacing coordFlip's special-case axes swizzle with a more general projection model in IR/compile that can support cartesian swaps, polar angle/radius naming, and future coordinate systems while preserving current coordFlip ergonomics.
close_reason: Replaced the cartesian-only 'flip' CoordKind with a shared Coord.project: [PositionAxis, PositionAxis] field consumed identically by Cartesian and Polar's axes swizzle trait. coordFlip() and coordPolar({theta:'y'}) both reduce to project:['y','x']. Removed the dead unreachable 'fixed' CoordKind. Tests: 1 new case (coord_polar theta:'y'), full suite 81/81 passing. This closes epic gggplot-1be (9/9 children complete).

title: Separate simultaneous color and fill scales in compiler
description: compile() collapses color/fill to a single colorScale via scales.get('color') ?? scales.get('fill'). That works when only one aesthetic is mapped, but plots with both color and fill mappings can apply the color scale to fill-based geoms/legends. Keep separate colorScale and fillScale paths through lowerLayer/lowerBarLayer/lowerTileLayer/legends, with tests covering a point color layer plus a filled bar/tile layer.
design: Kept color and fill as independent trained scales in compile(): colorScale=scales.get('color'), fillScale=scales.get('fill'). Added a color preference helper so point/text/line use color-or-fill while filled polygon geoms use fill-or-color. Legend generation now emits separate discrete color and fill guide sections when both scales exist.
notes: Aligned under gggplot-1be because peer dialects keep colour/fill/stroke aesthetics independently scaled rather than collapsing them into one colorScale.
close_reason: Separated simultaneous color/fill scale plumbing in the compiler and legend generation. Added regression test covering point color plus tile fill with independent manual domains/ranges. Verified deno test -A packages/core/tests/pipeline_test.ts (64 passed), deno check packages/core/src/mod.ts apps/site/src/scene.tsx apps/site/src/examples.tsx, and full deno test -A (68 passed).

title: Wire real font source for live Label text
description: GGPlot wraps renders in a fontless FontLoader, so Label-based text (geom_text, facet strips, legend labels/titles, axis tick text) compiles into the RenderTree but is invisible in the live WebGPU site. Wire a real font source in the app/render host so Label text is visually rendered, then verify with Playwright screenshots.
close_reason: Wired a real font source into the live site: GGPlot now accepts host-provided FontLoader sources, apps/site serves SFNS.ttf from public/fonts, and Scene passes sans-serif/Georgia font entries. Verified deno test -A (65 passed), deno check packages/core/src/mod.ts apps/site/src/scene.tsx apps/site/src/examples.tsx, and live screenshot /private/tmp/gggplot-color-legend-text-visible.png showing rendered legend text.

title: theme.background Polygon makes subsequent Grid/Axis invisible in live WebGPU render
description: compile.ts draws theme.background (when set) as an opaque full-panel Polygon, first in the guides array so Grid/Axis/marks layer on top of it in RenderTree/emitted-source order. The compiled RenderTree/emitSource output is correct (verified: dumped RenderTree JSON shows Polygon->Grid->Axis->Axis->Point in the right order with the right props, and 5 headless pipeline tests assert this with exact values). But in the live WebGPU backend (GGPlot.tsx's FlatCamera/Pass host), adding the background Polygon causes the Grid and Axis Line draws that follow it to render completely invisible -- confirmed via pixel-level histogram sampling of Playwright screenshots (not just eyeballing), reproduced after a cold dev-server restart (ruled out HMR staleness).
design: Resolved: the live backend guide occlusion was handled by keeping the full-panel background Polygon below guide lines in depth/layer terms: background emits depth=1 and depthWrite=false, while Grid/Axis emit zBias=1. Earlier attempts on the background alone were insufficient; the working design relies on both background depth behavior and guide zBias. Keep live Playwright verification for this class of issue because RenderTree/source order alone does not prove WebGPU visibility.
acceptance_criteria: A themed chart with theme.background set renders the panel fill AND visible grid/axis lines together in the live WebGPU demo, verified via Playwright screenshot (not just headless RenderTree assertions).
close_reason: Fixed live WebGPU guide occlusion for theme.background by emitting background Polygon with depth=1/depthWrite=false and Grid/Axis with zBias=1; restored ThemedChart background demo copy. Verified deno test -A, deno check packages/core/src/mod.ts, and browser screenshot at localhost:8082 showing panel fill plus visible lavender grid/axis lines.

title: Subdivide (munch) Polygon/Grid edges for clean coord_polar wedges
description: coord_polar's infrastructure is wired up and works for point geoms (verified visually), but bar/polygon-based geoms (geom_bar/col/area/ribbon/tile/boxplot) render as distorted fans instead of clean pie/rose wedges, because Polygon's straight 2-point edges don't curve under Polar's nonlinear vertex shader transform (getPolarPosition) -- only the endpoints bend, leaving long straight chords. Real ggplot2 solves this with coord_munch(), which subdivides straight path segments into many small steps before a non-linear coordinate transform, so each tiny segment approximates a smooth curve. The Grid guide has the same issue (fans out instead of showing concentric rings + radial spokes) -- worth checking whether @use-gpu/plot's Grid component has its own polar-aware config, or whether it needs a different guide entirely under Polar.
design: Verified via Playwright screenshots against a live dev build: a 3-bar geom_col under coord_polar rendered as a triangular fan of straight lines (not a rose chart); the same data with geomPoint instead rendered the points at roughly correct positions but the surrounding Grid still fanned out rather than showing circular rings.
acceptance_criteria: A geom_col/geom_bar chart under coord_polar renders as clean pie/rose wedges with curved outer edges, and the Grid guide shows concentric circles + radial spokes, verified via Playwright screenshot.
close_reason: Implemented coord_polar munching for Polygon nodes, explicit polar Line guide rings/spokes, and full-width x-domain training for bar/col geoms. Verified with deno test -A (62 passed), deno check packages/core/src/mod.ts, and browser screenshot /private/tmp/gggplot-polar-bars-widened.png showing curved rose wedges plus polar grid guides.

title: geom_line doesn't sort by x before connecting (geom_path should stay unsorted)
description: Noticed while visually verifying the WASM/camera fixes: the scatter+line gallery example's connecting line criss-crosses instead of forming a clean left-to-right line, because compile.ts's lowerLayer() treats 'line' and 'path' identically (both just connect positionsOf()'s rows in raw data order). Real ggplot2 semantics: geom_line always sorts by x before connecting (so an unsorted dataset still draws a proper line), while geom_path preserves the data's row order (for trajectories/spirals where visit order matters, not x order). Fix: sort rows by x specifically for the 'line' case (and each of its split-by-group subsets) before building positions; leave 'path' as-is.
close_reason: Fixed: added sortByX() in compile.ts, which reorders every column by ascending x. Applied only to the 'line' case (per group, since sorting happens after splitByGroup) -- geom_path continues to preserve raw row order for trajectory-style plots where visit order matters. 1 new test with unsorted input data confirms geom_line reorders to [[0,10],[1,20],[2,30]] while geom_path keeps the original [[2,30],[0,10],[1,20]] order. All 41 tests pass.

title: Deployable build & hosting
description: Ensure deno task build output is deployable (static host); document deploy.
close_reason: Verified deployable static Vite build with deno task build; apps/site/dist contains index.html, JS bundle, glyph WASM, and the public font asset. Documented static deployment and secure-context/WebGPU requirements in README.md. Build passes with only Vite's existing large chunk warning.

title: Theme -> UseGPU props (background/grid/fonts)
description: theme_minimal/theme_bw etc mapped to Grid/Axis/background props.
close_reason: Implemented theme -> UseGPU props mapping. Theme gained background/grid/gridColor/gridWidth/axisColor/axisWidth/fontFamily/fontSize/textColor fields (ir/types.ts); compile.ts maps these onto Grid/Axis width+color traits and geom_text's Label size/color/family (falling back to theme values only when the layer doesn't set its own param). theme_*() calls now merge additively (dsl/mod.ts's GG.add: {...this.spec.theme, ...part.value}) matching ggplot2's theme_minimal() + theme(...) composition instead of the previous full-replace behavior. Added themeClassic() (grid:false), themeGrey() (grey background + white grid), and a general theme(overrides) builder mirroring ggplot2's theme(...). 5 new headless tests with exact-value assertions (default/themeGrey/themeClassic/merge-behavior/font-fallback), all passing, plus live-in-browser Playwright verification that grid/axis color+width overrides and geom_text font theming render correctly. Known limitation, tracked separately as gggplot-b15.4: theme.background draws an opaque full-panel Polygon first in the guides array (correct in the RenderTree/emitSource output, verified structurally), but in this project's live WebGPU backend it causes the following Grid/Axis draws to render invisibly -- zBias/depthWrite/depthTest toggles on the Polygon didn't fix it, root mechanism still unknown. Scoped out of the live gallery demo (ThemedChart example uses grid/axis/font theming only, with a note pointing to b15.4) rather than shipping a visually broken background.

title: Position adjustments (stack/dodge/fill/jitter)
description: Transform mark positions post-scale; needed by bars and overlapping points.
close_reason: Implemented position adjustments in a new packages/core/src/position/mod.ts: stackBars (stack rows sharing an x on top of each other in group-key order, or 'identity' for an unstacked shared baseline), the 'fill' mode within stackBars (normalizes each x's stack to [0,1]), dodgeBars (side-by-side placement with a stable per-group slot across all x values, sorted group-key order so a group's slot doesn't shift between x's), and jitter (uniform random nudge within +/-amount). Exported from mod.ts for direct testing. 3 new unit tests plus integration coverage via the geom_bar/col tests in the paired v04.1 close.

title: facet_wrap/facet_grid panel layout
description: Partition data into panels; lay out multiple Cartesian views (grid) with shared or free scales.
close_reason: Implemented facet_wrap/facet_grid: partitions data by facet vars before stat transform (so stat_count/bin aggregate per-panel), trains shared/fixed scales across all panels (ggplot2 default), and lays out panels via a new custom FacetGrid Live component that subdivides the ambient LayoutContext pixel rect at render time (not a real @use-gpu/plot export -- documented in rendertree.ts/GGPlot.tsx; emitSource inlines its definition for standalone output). 5 new exact-value pipeline tests + verified live in-browser via Playwright screenshot: a facet_wrap(cyl) scatter renders 3 correctly-positioned, correctly-scaled panels in a 2x2 grid. Strip labels (facet value as text) compile correctly but don't visually render yet -- confirmed via Playwright this is the same pre-existing FontLoader 'fontless-by-default' gap that already affects geom_text (not a new regression, not in scope here).

title: coord_polar & coord_flip
description: Real polar view (pie/rose) and axis flip; map to @use-gpu/plot Polar / swapped axes.
close_reason: Implemented and visually verified both. Researched @use-gpu/plot's compiled Cartesian/Polar source before implementing (not guessed): both share the same range/axes trait shape, and 'axes' is a swizzle string applied AFTER the range-to-clip-space matrix is built -- so coord_flip is just axes:'yx' on the panel + Grid (verified: range/positions stay untouched, only the rendered orientation swaps; confirmed visually as clean horizontal bars). coord_polar selects the Polar view component and passes through spec.coord.params (bend/on/helix) -- confirmed via Playwright that point geoms bend correctly into a circular layout. However, visual verification also surfaced a real, deeper limitation: Polygon's straight 2-point edges don't curve under Polar's nonlinear per-vertex shader transform (only endpoints bend, leaving straight chords), so geom_bar/col renders as a distorted fan instead of clean pie wedges, and Grid has the same issue. This mirrors ggplot2's coord_munch() problem exactly (subdividing straight paths before a non-linear coordinate transform) -- filed as gggplot-97e.4 rather than silently shipping broken-looking bar/polygon polar charts. Added FlippedBars and PolarPoints to the doc site gallery, both DSL builders (coordFlip/coordPolar) already existed. 2 new tests covering axes swizzle + params passthrough; all 43 tests pass.

title: geom_boxplot/geom_errorbar
description: Statistical geoms composed of lines + rects.
close_reason: Implemented geom_boxplot/geom_errorbar as pre-summarized statistical geoms composed of lines + rects (scope note: this covers the geometry/rendering the ticket describes, not a stat_boxplot quantile-computing stat -- StatKind has no 'boxplot' entry yet, so both geoms currently expect pre-computed columns via aes(), same pattern as geom_ribbon's ymin/ymax; computing quantiles from raw y would be a separate stat ticket). Added 'lower'/'middle'/'upper' aesthetics and 'boxplot'/'errorbar' GeomKinds (ir/types.ts), geomBoxplot/geomErrorbar DSL builders. compile.ts: lowerErrorbarLayer emits one Line of disjoint segments (top cap, vertical stem, bottom cap) per row, width defaulting to 0.9x resolution (ggplot2's bar-style default); lowerBoxplotLayer emits a box Polygon (lower..upper) plus a Line of median + both whisker stems + half-width caps, box width defaulting to 0.75x resolution (ggplot2's default). Both reuse the resolutionOf/colorsOf helpers already established for bars/tiles. y-domain training already covered via the existing ymin/ymax handling in scale/mod.ts (lower/middle/upper fall within that range so need no separate widening). 2 new tests with exact hand-verified segment/box geometry; all 35 tests pass.

title: geom_tile/geom_raster (heatmap)
description: Grid of colored cells; pairs with Surface/tensor source.
close_reason: Implemented geom_tile/geom_raster via the same Polygon-loop pattern as bars (a scoped deviation from the ticket's 'pairs with Surface/tensor source' hint -- @use-gpu/plot's Surface/tensor-source layers are a specialized GPU scalar-field pipeline I haven't verified against a working render given the still-open WASM blocker, whereas N-rectangle Polygon loops are consistent with the already-established, tested Point/Line/Polygon architecture and fully correct for tile-grid rendering). lowerTileLayer() in compile.ts: one rectangle per row, centered on (x,y), sized to each axis's resolution (smallest gap between distinct values, or 1 level-index unit for discrete) by default so adjacent cells tile edge-to-edge with no gaps -- params.width/height override it. Added widenForTileAxis() to extend both x and y domains by half a cell so edge tiles aren't clipped (tiles extend past their center point, unlike point-based marks). geomTile and geomRaster DSL builders (both map to the same 'tile' GeomKind; geom_raster's real distinction -- always full resolution, no custom width/height -- isn't hard-enforced, a minor simplification). 2 new tests: exact grid positions + widened domain, and a no-gap edge-to-edge sanity check; all 33 tests pass.

title: geom_text/geom_label
description: Text marks via @use-gpu/plot Label.
close_reason: Implemented geom_text/geom_label via @use-gpu/plot's Label component. Added Label to GGPlot.tsx's render REGISTRY (it was already in ComponentName/rendertree.ts and emit/mod.ts's PLOT_IMPORTS but never wired to the actual component, so it was previously unusable). lowerTextLayer() in compile.ts builds one Label node per layer: per-point positions (reusing positionsOf) + a 'labels' array from the mapped label column (stringified), plus per-point colors when color/fill is mapped. geomLabel added as a DSL alias for geomText -- both currently render identically, since geom_label's background box needs real text-metrics-aware sizing that requires the font pipeline (same blocker as gggplot-6dm.6), documented as a scoped simplification. 1 new test covering exact Label positions/labels plus emitSource output. All 36 tests pass. This closes out the Geoms library epic (gggplot-v04) at 5/5.

title: Legends as guides
description: Render legends for color/size/shape into the RenderTree.
notes: Update: the WASM/camera blockers (gggplot-6dm.6, gggplot-6dm.4) are now both resolved -- text/font rendering and the Embedded pixel-space bridge both work in-browser. This issue is unblocked; a legend can now be built as a real, visually-verifiable RenderNode (Label + swatch) rather than guessed-at structure.
close_reason: Implemented legend guides in the compiler RenderTree for discrete color/fill, continuous size, and discrete shape: overlay Label titles/labels plus Point swatches; shape-mapped points now split by shape. Verified deno test -A (65 passed), deno check packages/core/src/mod.ts, and live browser screenshot /private/tmp/gggplot-color-legend.png showing legend swatches rendered. Legend text is still invisible in the live site due to the host font-source gap, filed separately as gggplot-2wy.

title: Log/sqrt transforms & scale limits/expansion
description: Transformed scales; user domain limits; axis expansion.
close_reason: Implemented log10/sqrt transforms, confirmed+tested user domain limits, and opt-in axis expansion. scale/mod.ts: added transformFor() (log10/sqrt/identity) applied both to scalePosition's per-value mapping and to the trained continuous domain (so declared limits are transformed consistently with plotted points), and expandRange() ([mult,add] padding, ggplot2's expansion()) applied only when a scale explicitly sets 'expand' -- kept off by default to avoid silently changing every existing chart's trained range. Wired expand support into compile.ts's discrete numericRange() too. Added scaleXLog10/scaleYLog10/scaleXSqrt/scaleYSqrt DSL builders (ir/types.ts Scale gained an 'expand' field). Scope note: real ggplot2 enables ~5% continuous / 0.6-unit discrete expansion by default; I deliberately kept it off-by-default here since flipping every chart's default range would require rewriting the numeric expectations of most existing exact-match tests without a chance for review -- left as a clearly-documented, fully working opt-in mechanism instead. 4 new tests covering log/sqrt transform+domain, explicit domain limits, and expand padding; all 18 tests pass.

title: Size/alpha/shape scales
description: Map aesthetics to point size, opacity, glyph.
close_reason: Implemented size/alpha/shape scale training and wired size into rendering. scale/mod.ts: trainContinuousAuxScale (shared by size/alpha, default ranges [1,6] and [0.1,1]) and trainShapeScale (discrete factor levels -> a fixed 6-glyph palette, same fixed-order pattern as the categorical color palette), plus scaleSizeValue/scaleAlphaValue (linear interpolation into range) and scaleShapeValue (level lookup) value functions. Wired size into compile.ts: a mapped size column now produces a per-point 'sizes' array on the Point node (UseGPU's Point supports per-vertex sizes). Also added a flat layer.params.alpha -> 'opacity' passthrough for point/line, since UseGPU's Point/Line only expose a single scalar opacity (no per-vertex opacities array) -- so aesthetic-mapped alpha and shape are trained/testable at the scale layer (scaleAlphaValue/scaleShapeValue) but not wired into per-point rendering, since the underlying renderer has no per-vertex prop for either; documented this as a real, current renderer constraint rather than a gap in this ticket's implementation. Added scaleSize/scaleAlpha/scaleShape DSL builders. 4 new tests covering mapped size on Point, the two interpolation value functions, shape level lookup, and the flat alpha->opacity passthrough; all 22 tests pass.

title: stat_summary
description: Aggregate y per x group (mean/median/etc).
close_reason: Implemented stat_summary in packages/core/src/stat/mod.ts: aggregates y per distinct x value (first-seen order) via params.fun, default 'mean', also 'median'/'sum'/'min'/'max' by name, or a custom (values: number[]) => number function. Only x/y are re-emitted (one row per x group) -- like the existing stat_count/stat_bin, other per-row columns (e.g. a fill/group column) don't have a well-defined per-group value and are dropped; this is a pre-existing pattern/limitation in this codebase, not new. No new geom was added: ggplot2 defaults stat_summary to geom_pointrange, which this codebase doesn't implement, so stat_summary is used by overriding an existing geom's stat, e.g. geomPoint({ stat: 'summary', fun: 'median' }) -- consistent with how GeomOpts.stat already lets any geom override its default stat. Tested with exact-value assertions: default mean aggregation, fun:'median', and a custom aggregator function, all via applyStat directly (matching the stat_count/stat_bin test style). 3 new tests, all passing. deno task check and deno task --cwd packages/core test both pass (50 tests total, up from 43).

title: stat_smooth (lm/loess)
description: Fit trend + optional CI ribbon. Backs geom_smooth.
close_reason: Implemented stat_smooth with method='lm' (ordinary least-squares linear regression) in packages/core/src/stat/mod.ts. Re-emits x as params.n (default 80) evenly spaced points across the data's x range (bin-center style, like stat_bin), with fitted y, and unless params.se===false, ymin/ymax for a CI ribbon -- mapping.y/ymin/ymax always overridden to the new column names since the fitted point count differs from the input row count. CI band uses the standard OLS prediction formula se(y_hat) = s*sqrt(1/n + (x-xbar)^2/Sxx) but a fixed z=1.96 multiplier rather than the exact Student's-t critical value (large-sample approximation, documented in a code comment as a known simplification -- not a full stats package). loess (ggplot2's default method) is NOT implemented -- it's a substantially bigger lift (weighted local regression with a bandwidth/span parameter); an unrecognized method value warns and falls back to lm. Added geomSmooth() to the DSL (packages/core/src/dsl/mod.ts) and a 'smooth' GeomKind (ir/types.ts). Wired rendering in compile/mod.ts: geom_smooth lowers to an optional Ribbon Polygon (drawn first, light-indigo #c7d2fe fill, only when ymin/ymax are mapped) plus a Line for the fit -- reuses the existing bandPositions/positionsOf helpers. y-domain widening for the ribbon comes for free since trainScales already unions mapping.y/ymin/ymax for the y aesthetic. Tested with exact-value assertions: stat_smooth against noise-free linear data (y=2x+1, zero residual -> deterministic fitted values and a zero-width CI band, verifying the regression math exactly), se:false omitting ymin/ymax, and full compile() tests checking the Line+Polygon RenderNode shapes and that se:false skips the Polygon entirely. 4 new tests, all passing.

title: gggplot compile CLI on top of emitSource
description: Deno CLI: gggplot compile spec.ts -> chart.tsx. Reads a spec module, runs compile+emitSource, writes .tsx.
close_reason: Implemented the gggplot compile CLI: packages/core/src/cli.ts exports runCli(args) (dynamic-imports a spec module via node:url pathToFileURL, looks for a 'spec' named export or default export, runs compile()+emitSource(), writes the .tsx) plus an import.meta.main entry point for direct execution. Output path defaults to the spec's basename with a .tsx extension; component name defaults to a PascalCase-ified output filename, overridable via --name=. Wired up as 'deno task gggplot' (deno run -A packages/core/src/cli.ts) at the repo root -- usage: deno task gggplot compile spec.ts chart.tsx. Added a demo-spec.ts test fixture (mirrors examples/emit-demo.ts) and 4 new tests in cli_test.ts covering successful compilation, default/explicit component naming, and the missing-argument error path (packages/core's test task gained --allow-write for the temp-file writes). Verified end-to-end with a real 'deno task gggplot compile ...' invocation producing correct emitted source. All 40 tests pass.

title: Aesthetic inheritance & layer overrides semantics
description: Match ggplot: layer mapping/data override plot defaults; fixed aes vs mapped aes; group aesthetic; inherit.aes=FALSE equivalent.
close_reason: Implemented the two missing pieces of aesthetic inheritance/override semantics (layer mapping/data overriding plot defaults, and fixed vs mapped aes were already correctly handled by the existing Aes vs Layer.params split). 1) inherit.aes=FALSE equivalent: Layer gained an inheritAes?: boolean field (ir/types.ts) and geom() DSL builders accept an inheritAes option; compile.ts's stage-1 mapping resolution now uses only the layer's own mapping (ignoring spec.mapping entirely) when inheritAes===false, instead of always merging plot+layer mapping. 2) group aesthetic: added splitByGroup() in compile.ts, which partitions a layer's rows by its mapped group column (first-seen order) before lowering; geom_line/path/area/ribbon now render one connected Line/Polygon per group instead of zigzagging across all groups' points in raw data order. lowerLayer() was changed to return RenderNode[] (flatMapped in compile()) to support the one-node-per-group case; geom_point is unaffected since group has no connectivity meaning for independent points. 2 new tests covering group-split lines and inheritAes:false; all 24 tests pass.

title: Long tail: 2D binning (bin_2d/hex/contour), stat_qq/ellipse/function, colorbar/binned guides
description:
docs/COVERAGE_BACKLOG.md sections 2/3/9, grouped as one lower-priority catch-all since each item is small in isolation but the group as a whole is long: geom_bin2d/geom_hex + stat_bin_2d/stat_bin_hex (2D binned density), geom_contour/geom_contour_filled + stat_contour, geom_qq/geom_qq_line + stat_qq/stat_qq_line, stat_ellipse, stat_function (evaluate a function over a range with no input data), guide_colourbar (continuous color/fill gradient legend -- notably, gggplot currently has NO legend at all for continuous color/fill, only discrete/size/shape are legended, so this specific piece may be worth splitting out and prioritizing higher later), guide_coloursteps/guide_bins (binned/stepped legends, depends on gggplot-aei.3's binned scales existing first). Split into its own issues once work actually starts here rather than speculatively now.

UPDATE (docs/COVERAGE_BACKLOG.md section 10, native @use-gpu primitive research): contour is no longer the highest-effort item here. @use-gpu/plot's ImplicitSurface component is a thin wrapper around @use-gpu/workbench's DualContourLayer -- a real dual-contouring GPU implementation. We still have to build the underlying 2D density/count grid ourselves in JS (stat_contour's actual 'stat' half has no shortcut), but the isoline/isosurface EXTRACTION step (marching-squares-equivalent) can be handed to ImplicitSurface/DualContourLayer directly instead of hand-implementing it. This meaningfully lowers the effort for geom_contour/geom_contour_filled/geom_density_2d's contour lines relative to the other items in this catch-all -- worth reconsidering priority once picked up. No equivalent native shortcut exists for stat_bin_2d/stat_bin_hex/stat_qq/stat_ellipse/stat_function/the guide items -- those still need to be fully hand-implemented (stat_function is the closest to a native fit, since @use-gpu/plot's Sampler/Tensor already evaluate an expr over a range, but that's a data-generation primitive we'd wire up ourselves, not a ready-made stat_function).
